17.1.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi kṣetragarbhaṃ mahodayam ..
tadvastrāpathamāhātmyaṃ yatra raivatako giriḥ .. 1 ..
17.1.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
अथ ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि क्षेत्रगर्भं महोदयम् ..
तद्वस्त्रापथमाहात्म्यं यत्र रैवतको गिरिः .. 1 ..
17.1.m: Īśvara said: / Now I shall tell you of the most prosperous interior of the sacred field, / that māhātmya of Vastrāpatha where Mount Raivataka is situated. // 1

17.1.s:
dāmodaraṃ raivatake bhavaṃ vastrāpathe tathā ..
etadraivatakaṃ kṣetraṃ vastrāpathamiti smṛtam .. 2 ..
17.1.d:
दामोदरं रैवतके भवं वस्त्रापथे तथा ..
एतद्रैवतकं क्षेत्रं वस्त्रापथमिति स्मृतम् .. 2 ..
17.1.m: Dāmodara is at Raivataka, and Bhava likewise at Vastrāpatha; / this Raivataka sacred field is known as Vastrāpatha. // 2

17.1.s:
suvarṇarevā yatrasthā nadī pātakanāśanī ..
yatra sākṣātsthitaḥ kṛṣṇo dāmodara iti smṛtaḥ .. 3 ..
17.1.d:
सुवर्णरेवा यत्रस्था नदी पातकनाशनी ..
यत्र साक्षात्स्थितः कृष्णो दामोदर इति स्मृतः .. 3 ..
17.1.m: Where the river Suvarṇarevā flows, destroying sins, / where Kṛṣṇa resides in visible form, remembered as Dāmodara; // 3

17.1.s:
yatra sthitaṃ mṛgīkuṇḍaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam ..
sakṛcchrāddhe kṛte yatra kalpakoṭisahasrakam ..
pitṝṇāṃ jāyate tṛptirapunarbhavakāṃkṣiṇī .. 4 ..
17.1.d:
यत्र स्थितं मृगीकुण्डं महापातकनाशनम् ..
सकृच्छ्राद्धे कृते यत्र कल्पकोटिसहस्रकम् ..
पितॄणां जायते तृप्तिरपुनर्भवकांक्षिणी .. 4 ..
17.1.m: where Mṛgīkuṇḍa is situated, which destroys great sins, / where, if a śrāddha is performed even once, for a thousand crores of kalpas / the ancestors attain satisfaction that yearns for freedom from rebirth. // 4

17.1.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
bhagavanvistarādbrūhi dāmodaramahodayam ..
kṣetragarbhasya māhātmyaṃ karṇikārūpasaṃsthitam .. 5 ..
17.1.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
भगवन्विस्तराद्ब्रूहि दामोदरमहोदयम् ..
क्षेत्रगर्भस्य माहात्म्यं कर्णिकारूपसंस्थितम् .. 5 ..
17.1.m: The Goddess said: / Lord, relate in full the great fortune of Dāmodara, / the māhātmya of the interior of the sacred field which is positioned in the form of a pericarp. // 5

17.1.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi dāmodarahariṃ prati ..
itihāsaṃ purākhyātamṛṣibhiḥ kalpavāsibhiḥ .. 6 ..
17.1.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
शृणु देवि प्रवक्ष्यामि दामोदरहरिं प्रति ..
इतिहासं पुराख्यातमृषिभिः कल्पवासिभिः .. 6 ..
17.1.m: Īśvara said: / Listen, O Goddess, I shall recount concerning Dāmodara-Hari / the ancient historical account told by seers dwelling for a kalpa. // 6

17.1.s:
gaṃgātīre śubhe ramye puṇye janapadākule ..
ṛṣibhiḥ sevite nityaṃ svargamārgaprade dhruvam .. 7 ..
17.1.d:
गंगातीरे शुभे रम्ये पुण्ये जनपदाकुले ..
ऋषिभिः सेविते नित्यं स्वर्गमार्गप्रदे ध्रुवम् .. 7 ..
17.1.m: On the auspicious, delightful, and holy bank of the Gaṅgā, crowded with inhabitants, / constantly attended by seers, which certainly grants the path to heaven, // 7

17.1.s:
tatra jñānavido viprā yajaṃti vividhairmakhaiḥ ..
ṛṣayaḥ sāṃkhyayogena dānenaivetare janāḥ .. 8 ..
17.1.d:
तत्र ज्ञानविदो विप्रा यजंति विविधैर्मखैः ..
ऋषयः सांख्ययोगेन दानेनैवेतरे जनाः .. 8 ..
17.1.m: there brahmins knowledgeable in spiritual wisdom sacrifice with diverse rituals, / seers [worship] through Sāṃkhya and Yoga, and other people purely through giving. // 8

17.1.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā svargamabhīpsavaḥ ..
sevaṃte tajjalaṃ divyaṃ devānāmapi durlabham .. 9 ..
17.1.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा स्वर्गमभीप्सवः ..
सेवंते तज्जलं दिव्यं देवानामपि दुर्लभम् .. 9 ..
17.1.m: Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, all desiring heaven, / resort to that divine water which is difficult to attain even for the gods. // 9

17.1.s:
tatra rājā gajonāma balī sarvajanādhipaḥ ..
gaṃgājalābhiṣekārthaṃ tyakvā rājyaṃ jagāma ha .. 7.2.1.10 ..
17.1.d:
तत्र राजा गजोनाम बली सर्वजनाधिपः ..
गंगाजलाभिषेकार्थं त्यक्वा राज्यं जगाम ह .. 7.2.1.10 ..
17.1.m: There a mighty king named Gaja, ruler of all people, / abandoned his kingdom and went to bathe in the waters of the Gaṅgā. // 7.2.1.10

17.1.s:
bhāryā tasya satī sādhvī putriṇī rūpasaṃyutā ..
sā'pyayātsaha tenaiva bhartrā vai bhartṛvatsalā .. 11 ..
17.1.d:
भार्या तस्य सती साध्वी पुत्रिणी रूपसंयुता ..
साऽप्ययात्सह तेनैव भर्त्रा वै भर्तृवत्सला .. 11 ..
17.1.m: His wife, chaste, virtuous, endowed with children and with beauty, / she too, devoted to her husband, went along with that very husband. // 11

17.1.s:
saṃgatā nāma nāmnā ca dakṣā dākṣāyaṇī yathā ..
evaṃ nivasatostatra varṣāṇāmayutaṃ gatam .. 12 ..
17.1.d:
संगता नाम नाम्ना च दक्षा दाक्षायणी यथा ..
एवं निवसतोस्तत्र वर्षाणामयुतं गतम् .. 12 ..
17.1.m: Saṃgatā by name, she was capable like Dākṣāyaṇī. / As they were living there thus, ten thousand years passed away. // 12

17.1.s:
ājagāma ṛṣistatra bhadronāma mahāyaśāḥ ..
sahito bahubhirviprairjapahomaparāyaṇaiḥ .. 13 ..
17.1.d:
आजगाम ऋषिस्तत्र भद्रोनाम महायशाः ..
सहितो बहुभिर्विप्रैर्जपहोमपरायणैः .. 13 ..
17.1.m: There arrived a seer named Bhadra, of great renown, / accompanied by many brahmins devoted to silent recitation and fire-offerings. // 13

17.1.s:
tyaktvā saṃsāramārgaṃ tu svargamārgajigīṣavaḥ ..
gaṃgāniṣevaṇaṃ kṛtvā sphoṭayitvā''tmajaṃ malam .. 14 ..
17.1.d:
त्यक्त्वा संसारमार्गं तु स्वर्गमार्गजिगीषवः ..
गंगानिषेवणं कृत्वा स्फोटयित्वा'ऽत्मजं मलम् .. 14 ..
17.1.m: Having forsaken the path of worldly existence, striving to conquer the path to heaven, / having attended upon the Gaṅgā and dispelled their innate impurities, // 14

17.1.s:
jalaṃ dattvā tu bhūtebhyaḥ pūjayitvā janārddanam..
yāvadyāṃti nadītīra ṛṣayo bhadrakādayaḥ ..
tāvatpaśyaṃti rājānaṃ gajaṃ varagajopamam ..15..
17.1.d:
जलं दत्त्वा तु भूतेभ्यः पूजयित्वा जनार्द्दनम्..
यावद्यांति नदीतीर ऋषयो भद्रकादयः ..
तावत्पश्यंति राजानं गजं वरगजोपमम् ..15..
17.1.m: having offered water to the living beings and worshipped Janārdana, / as the seers, Bhadra and the rest, were going toward the riverbank, / they saw King Gaja, resembling an excellent elephant. // 15

17.1.s:
tenaiva dṛṣṭā munayo rājñā nihatakalmaṣāḥ ..
saptarṣayo yathā svarge surarājena dhīmatā ..16..
17.1.d:
तेनैव दृष्टा मुनयो राज्ञा निहतकल्मषाः ..
सप्तर्षयो यथा स्वर्गे सुरराजेन धीमता ..16..
17.1.m: By that king, the sages whose sins were destroyed were seen, / just as the seven seers [are seen] in heaven by the wise king of the gods. // 16

17.1.s:
tamṛṣiṃ sa ca saṃprekṣya padāni daśa paṃca ca ..
āgacchantvatra pūjārhā bhavato mama mandiram.. 17 ..
17.1.d:
तमृषिं स च संप्रेक्ष्य पदानि दश पंच च ..
आगच्छन्त्वत्र पूजार्हा भवतो मम मन्दिरम्.. 17 ..
17.1.m: Looking upon that seer, taking fifteen steps, [he said:] / "May you, worthy of worship, come here to my residence. // 17

17.1.s:
paśyaṃtu saṃgatāṃ sarve mama bhāryāṃ yaśasvinīm ..
tasyāḥ pūjāṃ samādāya yo mārgo manasi sthitaḥ .. 18 ..
17.1.d:
पश्यंतु संगतां सर्वे मम भार्यां यशस्विनीम् ..
तस्याः पूजां समादाय यो मार्गो मनसि स्थितः .. 18 ..
17.1.m: May all of you behold Saṃgatā, my illustrious wife; / having received homage from her, whatever path is set in your mind, // 18

17.1.s:
taṃ gacchadhvaṃ mahābhāgāḥ puṇyāḥ puṇyamabhīpsavaḥ ..
evamuktāstu te rājñā ṛṣayaḥ kautukānvitāḥ ..
ājagmurmaṃdiraṃ śubhraṃ puraṃdarapuropamam .. 19 ..
17.1.d:
तं गच्छध्वं महाभागाः पुण्याः पुण्यमभीप्सवः ..
एवमुक्तास्तु ते राज्ञा ऋषयः कौतुकान्विताः ..
आजग्मुर्मंदिरं शुभ्रं पुरंदरपुरोपमम् .. 19 ..
17.1.m: upon that proceed, O highly fortunate, holy ones who desire the holy." / Thus spoken to by the king, the seers, filled with curiosity, / went to his bright dwelling, resembling the city of Purandara. // 19

17.1.s:
āsanāni vicitrāṇi dattvā teṣāṃ manasvinī ..
saṃgatā rājarājena sārddhamagre vyavasthitā ..7.2.1.20..
17.1.d:
आसनानि विचित्राणि दत्त्वा तेषां मनस्विनी ..
संगता राजराजेन सार्द्धमग्रे व्यवस्थिता ..7.2.1.20..
17.1.m: Having offered them variegated seats, the high-minded / Saṃgatā stood in front [of them] along with the king of kings. // 7.2.1.20

17.1.s:
kṛtvā karapuṭaṃ rājā ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām ..
babhāṣe vacanaṃ rājā bhadro bhadraṃ susaṃgatam..21..
17.1.d:
कृत्वा करपुटं राजा ऋषीणां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ..
बभाषे वचनं राजा भद्रो भद्रं सुसंगतम्..21..
17.1.m: Having folded his hands in reverence to the seers of holy deeds, / the king spoke words to Bhadra that were auspicious and well-composed: // 21

17.1.s:
vasudhā vasusaṃpūrṇā maṃḍitā nagarī purī ..
parvataiśca samudraiśca saridbhiśca sarovaraiḥ ..22..
17.1.d:
वसुधा वसुसंपूर्णा मंडिता नगरी पुरी ..
पर्वतैश्च समुद्रैश्च सरिद्भिश्च सरोवरैः ..22..
17.1.m: "The earth is filled with wealth, adorned with town and city, / with mountains and oceans, and with rivers and lakes; // 22

17.1.s:
grāmaiścatuṣpathairghorairgokulairākulīkṛtā ..
nararatnairaśvaratnairgajaratnaistu saṃkulā .. 23 ..
17.1.d:
ग्रामैश्चतुष्पथैर्घोरैर्गोकुलैराकुलीकृता ..
नररत्नैरश्वरत्नैर्गजरत्नैस्तु संकुला .. 23 ..
17.1.m: it is teeming with villages, terrible crossroads, and herds of cattle, / and crowded with jewels among men, jewels among horses, and jewels among elephants. // 23

17.1.s:
dustyajā bhogabhoktṛṇāṃ paraṃ jñānamajānatām ..
saṃsāre'tra mahāghore punarāvṛttikāriṇi .. 24 ..
17.1.d:
दुस्त्यजा भोगभोक्तृणां परं ज्ञानमजानताम् ..
संसारेऽत्र महाघोरे पुनरावृत्तिकारिणि .. 24 ..
17.1.m: It is hard to abandon for those enjoying pleasures who do not know supreme knowledge. / In this terrible saṃsāra, which brings about repetition [of births], // 24

17.1.s:
pataṃti puruṣā bhadra patrāṇīva punaḥpunaḥ ..
kṛtena yena vipreṃdra svargaṃ prāpnoti nirmalam ..
dānena tapasā caiva tattvamā cakṣva suvrata .. 25 ..
17.1.d:
पतंति पुरुषा भद्र पत्राणीव पुनःपुनः ..
कृतेन येन विप्रेंद्र स्वर्गं प्राप्नोति निर्मलम् ..
दानेन तपसा चैव तत्त्वमा चक्ष्व सुव्रत .. 25 ..
17.1.m: men fall again and again, O Bhadra, like leaves. / By what performed [deed] does one attain spotless heaven, O leader of brahmins, / through giving or austerity? Explain that reality, O one of noble vows." // 25

17.1.s:
.. bhadra uvāca .. ..
tīrthāni toyapūrṇāni devāḥ pāṣāṇamṛnmayāḥ ..
ātmasthaṃ ye na paśyaṃti te na paśyaṃti tatparam .. 26 ..
17.1.d:
.. भद्र उवाच .. ..
तीर्थानि तोयपूर्णानि देवाः पाषाणमृन्मयाः ..
आत्मस्थं ये न पश्यंति ते न पश्यंति तत्परम् .. 26 ..
17.1.m: Bhadra said: / "Sacred fords are full of water, and deities are made of stone and clay; / those who do not behold the One dwelling in the Self do not behold that supreme [reality]. // 26

17.1.s:
saṃti tīrthānyanekāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca ..
puṇyatoyā pavitraśca saritaḥ sāgarāstathā ..
bahupuṇyapradā pṛthvī sthānesthāne padepade .. 27 ..
17.1.d:
संति तीर्थान्यनेकानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च ..
पुण्यतोया पवित्रश्च सरितः सागरास्तथा ..
बहुपुण्यप्रदा पृथ्वी स्थानेस्थाने पदेपदे .. 27 ..
17.1.m: There are numerous sacred fords and holy sanctuaries, / rivers with holy waters, purifiers, and likewise oceans; / at every place and every step, the earth bestows abundant merit. // 27

17.1.s:
yadyasti tava rājeṃdra jñānaṃ jñānavatāṃ vara ..
viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ śaṃkhinaṃ gadinaṃ tathā .. 28 ..
17.1.d:
यद्यस्ति तव राजेंद्र ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतां वर ..
विष्णुं जिष्णुं हृषीकेशं शंखिनं गदिनं तथा .. 28 ..
17.1.m: If you have spiritual knowledge, O lord of kings, best among the wise, / [behold] Viṣṇu, victorious, Hṛṣīkeśa, holding the conch and mace, // 28

17.1.s:
caturbhujaṃ mahābāhuṃ prabhāse daityasūdanam ..
vārāhaṃ vāmanaṃ caiva nārasiṃhaṃ balārjunam .. 29 ..
17.1.d:
चतुर्भुजं महाबाहुं प्रभासे दैत्यसूदनम् ..
वाराहं वामनं चैव नारसिंहं बलार्जुनम् .. 29 ..
17.1.m: the four-armed, mighty-armed slayer of Daityas at Prabhāsa, / the Boar, the Dwarf, the Man-Lion, Bala, and Arjuna,

17.1.s:
rāmaṃ rāmaṃ ca rāmaṃ ca puruṣottamameva ca ..
puṃḍarīkekṣaṇaṃ caiva gadāpāṇiṃ tathaiva ca .. 7.2.1.30 ..
17.1.d:
रामं रामं च रामं च पुरुषोत्तममेव च ..
पुंडरीकेक्षणं चैव गदापाणिं तथैव च .. 7.2.1.30 ..
17.1.m: Rāma, Rāma, and Rāma, and Puruṣottama, / the lotus-eyed, and likewise mace-in-hand,

17.1.s:
rāghavaṃ śakradamanaṃ goviṃdaṃ bahupuṇyadam ..
jayaṃ ca bhūdharaṃ caiva devadevaṃ janārddanam .. 31 ..
17.1.d:
राघवं शक्रदमनं गोविंदं बहुपुण्यदम् ..
जयं च भूधरं चैव देवदेवं जनार्द्दनम् .. 31 ..
17.1.m: the descendant of Raghu, the subduer of Indra, Govinda who bestows great merit, / Jaya, the earth-supporter, Janārdana the god of gods,

17.1.s:
surottamaṃ śrīdharaṃ ca hariṃ yogīśvaraṃ tathā ..
kapileśaṃ bhūtanāthaṃ śvetadvīpapatiṃ harim .. 32 ..
17.1.d:
सुरोत्तमं श्रीधरं च हरिं योगीश्वरं तथा ..
कपिलेशं भूतनाथं श्वेतद्वीपपतिं हरिम् .. 32 ..
17.1.m: the best of gods, the bearer of Śrī, Hari the lord of yogins, / Kapileśa, the lord of beings, Hari the lord of Śvetadvīpa,

17.1.s:
badaryāśramavāsau ca naranārāyaṇau tathā ..
padmanābhaṃ sunābhaṃ ca hayagrīvaṃ viśāṃ pate .. 33 ..
17.1.d:
बदर्याश्रमवासौ च नरनारायणौ तथा ..
पद्मनाभं सुनाभं च हयग्रीवं विशां पते .. 33 ..
17.1.m: the two dwellers in the hermitage of Badarī, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, / Padmanābha, Sunābha, and Hayagrīva, O lord of the people,

17.1.s:
dvijanāthaṃ dharānāthaṃ khaḍgapāṇiṃ tathaiva ca ..
dāmodaraṃ jalāvāsaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ harim ..34..
17.1.d:
द्विजनाथं धरानाथं खड्गपाणिं तथैव च ..
दामोदरं जलावासं सर्वपापहरं हरिम् ..34..
17.1.m: the lord of the twice-born, the lord of the earth, and likewise sword-in-hand, / Dāmodara, whose abode is in the waters, Hari who removes all sin:

17.1.s:
etānyeva hi sthānāni devadevasya cakriṇaḥ ..
gacchate yatra tatraiva mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ .. 35 ..
17.1.d:
एतान्येव हि स्थानानि देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ..
गच्छते यत्र तत्रैव मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः .. 35 ..
17.1.m: these indeed are the places of the god of gods who bears the discus; / wherever one goes to them, there one is freed from all sins.

17.1.s:
gaṃgā ca yamunā caiva tathā devī sarasvatī ..
dṛṣadvatī gomatī ca tāpī kāveriṇī tathā .. 36 .. . .
17.1.d:
गंगा च यमुना चैव तथा देवी सरस्वती ..
दृषद्वती गोमती च तापी कावेरिणी तथा .. 36 .. . .
17.1.m: The Gaṅgā, the Yamunā, and likewise the goddess Sarasvatī, / the Dṛṣadvatī, the Gomatī, the Tāpī, and the Kāverī,

17.1.s:
narmadā śarmadā caiva nadī godāvarī tathā ..
śatadruśca tathā viṃdhyā payoṣṇī varadā tathā .. 37 ..
17.1.d:
नर्मदा शर्मदा चैव नदी गोदावरी तथा ..
शतद्रुश्च तथा विंध्या पयोष्णी वरदा तथा .. 37 ..
17.1.m: the Narmadā that bestows happiness, and likewise the river Godāvarī, / the Śatadru, and likewise the Vindhyā, the Payoṣṇī, and the Varadā,

17.1.s:
carmaṇvatī ca sarayūrgaṃḍakī caṃḍapāpahā ..
caṃdrabhāgā vipāśā ca śoṇaścaiva punaḥpunaḥ .. 38 ..
17.1.d:
चर्मण्वती च सरयूर्गंडकी चंडपापहा ..
चंद्रभागा विपाशा च शोणश्चैव पुनःपुनः .. 38 ..
17.1.m: the Carmaṇvatī, the Sarayū, the Gaṇḍakī that removes terrible sins, / the Candrabhāgā, the Vipāśā, and repeatedly the Śoṇa:

17.1.s:
etāścānyāśca bahavo himavatprabhavāḥ śubhāḥ ..
tāsu snāto naraḥ svargaṃ yāti pātakavarjitaḥ .. 39 ..
17.1.d:
एताश्चान्याश्च बहवो हिमवत्प्रभवाः शुभाः ..
तासु स्नातो नरः स्वर्गं याति पातकवर्जितः .. 39 ..
17.1.m: these and many other auspicious rivers arising from the Himavat, / a man who has bathed in them, freed from sins, goes to heaven.

17.1.s:
vanāni naṃdanādīni parvatā maṃdarādayaḥ ..
nāmoccāreṇa yeṣāṃ hi pāpaṃ yāti rasātale ..7.2.1.40 ..
17.1.d:
वनानि नंदनादीनि पर्वता मंदरादयः ..
नामोच्चारेण येषां हि पापं याति रसातले ..7.2.1.40 ..
17.1.m: Forests beginning with Nandana, mountains beginning with Mandara, / at the mere utterance of whose names sin sinks to the netherworld.

17.1.s:
.. gaja uvāca .. ..
bhadraṃ hi bhāṣitaṃ bhadra ākhyānamamṛtopamam ..
pṛcchāmi sarvadharmajña tvāmahaṃ kiṃcideva hi .. 41 ..
17.1.d:
.. गज उवाच .. ..
भद्रं हि भाषितं भद्र आख्यानममृतोपमम् ..
पृच्छामि सर्वधर्मज्ञ त्वामहं किंचिदेव हि .. 41 ..
17.1.m: Gaja said: / Auspicious indeed was that spoken, O noble one, an account resembling nectar. / I ask you indeed something, O knower of all righteousness:

17.1.s:
yasminmāse dine yasmiṃstīrthe yasminkramānnaraiḥ ..
akṣayaṃ sevyate svargastanmamācakṣva suvrata .. 42 ..
17.1.d:
यस्मिन्मासे दिने यस्मिंस्तीर्थे यस्मिन्क्रमान्नरैः ..
अक्षयं सेव्यते स्वर्गस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुव्रत .. 42 ..
17.1.m: in which month, on which day, at which sacred ford in due order / eternal heaven is attained by men—tell me that, O you of noble vows.

17.1.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devatārcanam ..
akṣayo yena vai svargastanme gaditumarhasi .. 43 ..
17.1.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायो देवतार्चनम् ..
अक्षयो येन वै स्वर्गस्तन्मे गदितुमर्हसि .. 43 ..
17.1.m: Bathing, giving, recitation of mantras, oblation, study of the Veda, worship of deities— / that by which heaven becomes truly imperishable, you ought to tell me that.

17.1.s:
.. bhadra uvāca .. ..
śrūyatāṃ rājaśārdūla kathāṃ kathayato mama ..
yāṃ śrutvā mucyate pāpānnaro naravarottama .. 44 ..
17.1.d:
.. भद्र उवाच .. ..
श्रूयतां राजशार्दूल कथां कथयतो मम ..
यां श्रुत्वा मुच्यते पापान्नरो नरवरोत्तम .. 44 ..
17.1.m: Bhadra said: / Let it be heard, O tiger among kings, as I tell the story, / hearing which a man is freed from sin, O best of excellent men.

17.1.s: ṛṣīṇāṃ kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ nāradena mahātmanā .. 45 ..
17.1.d: ऋषीणां कथितं पूर्वं नारदेन महात्मना .. 45 ..
17.1.m: It was told formerly to the seers by the great-souled Nārada. / [45]

17.1.s:
evaṃ pṛṣṭaśca taiḥ sarvairnārado munisattamaḥ ..
kathayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭo meghadudubhinisvanaiḥ .. 46 ..
17.1.d:
एवं पृष्टश्च तैः सर्वैर्नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ..
कथयामास संहृष्टो मेघदुदुभिनिस्वनैः .. 46 ..
17.1.m: And thus questioned by all of them, Nārada, the best of sages, / greatly delighted, spoke in a voice like the rumbling of thunder-clouds: / [46]

17.1.s:
ramye himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe samavāye mayā śrutam..
tadahaṃ tava vakṣyāmi śrotukāmaṃ nararṣabha .. 47 ..
17.1.d:
रम्ये हिमवतः पृष्ठे समवाये मया श्रुतम्..
तदहं तव वक्ष्यामि श्रोतुकामं नरर्षभ .. 47 ..
17.1.m: “On the lovely ridge of the Himavat, in an assembly, it was heard by me; / that I will tell you who desire to hear, O bull among men.

17.1.s:
tīrthānyeva hi sarvāṇi punarāvarttakāni tu ..
akṣayām̐llabhate lokāṃstattīrthaṃ kathayāmi te .. 48 ..
17.1.d:
तीर्थान्येव हि सर्वाणि पुनरावर्त्तकानि तु ..
अक्षयाम्̐ल्लभते लोकांस्तत्तीर्थं कथयामि ते .. 48 ..
17.1.m: All other sacred fords indeed cause one to return [to rebirth], / but that sacred ford through which one attains imperishable worlds, I shall tell to you.

17.1.s:
mārgaśīrṣe kānyakubja uṣitvā rājasattama ..
na śocati naro nārī svargaṃ yāti parāvaram ..49..
17.1.d:
मार्गशीर्षे कान्यकुब्ज उषित्वा राजसत्तम ..
न शोचति नरो नारी स्वर्गं याति परावरम् ..49..
17.1.m: Having dwelt at Kānyakubja in Mārgaśīrṣa, O best of kings, / a man or woman does not grieve and goes to the highest heaven.

17.1.s:
pauṣasya paurṇamāsī yā yadi sā kriyate'rbude ..
varṣāṇāmarbudaṃ svarge modate pitṛbhiḥ saha ..7.2.1.50..
17.1.d:
पौषस्य पौर्णमासी या यदि सा क्रियतेऽर्बुदे ..
वर्षाणामर्बुदं स्वर्गे मोदते पितृभिः सह ..7.2.1.50..
17.1.m: If the full-moon day of Pauṣa is observed on Arbuda, / one rejoices together with the ancestors in heaven for an arbuda of years.

17.1.s:
māghyāṃ yadi gayāśrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ yacchate naraḥ ..
trayāṇāmapi devānāṃ caturthaḥ sa prajāyate ..51..
17.1.d:
माघ्यां यदि गयाश्राद्धं पितॄणां यच्छते नरः ..
त्रयाणामपि देवानां चतुर्थः स प्रजायते ..51..
17.1.m: If on the full-moon day of Māgha a man offers a śrāddha at Gayā to the ancestors, / he becomes a fourth alongside the three gods.

17.1.s:
phālgunyāṃ himavatpṛṣṭhe vasannekāṃ niśāṃ naraḥ ..
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo janārddanaḥ .. 52 ..
17.1.d:
फाल्गुन्यां हिमवत्पृष्ठे वसन्नेकां निशां नरः ..
स याति परमं स्थानं यत्र देवो जनार्द्दनः .. 52 ..
17.1.m: Dwelling for a single night on the ridge of the Himavat on the full-moon day of Phālguna, / a man goes to that supreme abode where God Janārdana resides.

17.1.s:
caitryāṃ śrāddhaṃ prabhāse tu ye kurvaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ ..
na te marttyā bhavantīha kulajaiḥ saha sattamāḥ .. 53 ..
17.1.d:
चैत्र्यां श्राद्धं प्रभासे तु ये कुर्वंति मनीषिणः ..
न ते मर्त्त्या भवन्तीह कुलजैः सह सत्तमाः .. 53 ..
17.1.m: Those wise people who perform a śrāddha at Prabhāsa on the full-moon day of Caitra, / those best of men do not become mortals here again, along with their kinsmen.

17.1.s:
caturbhuje tu vaiśākhyāṃ ye kurvaṃti jalapriye ..
tathāvaṃtyāṃ naraḥ kaścitsa yāti paramāṃ gatim .. 54 ..
17.1.d:
चतुर्भुजे तु वैशाख्यां ये कुर्वंति जलप्रिये ..
तथावंत्यां नरः कश्चित्स याति परमां गतिम् .. 54 ..
17.1.m: Those who perform it on the full-moon day of Vaiśākha at Caturbhuja, fond of water, / or any person in Avantī, goes to the supreme goal.

17.1.s:
jyaiṣṭhyāṃ jyeṣṭharkṣayuktāyāṃ śrāddhaṃ ca tritakūpake ..
kuryuryugāni te trīṇi vasaṃti nākasadmani .. 55 ..
17.1.d:
ज्यैष्ठ्यां ज्येष्ठर्क्षयुक्तायां श्राद्धं च त्रितकूपके ..
कुर्युर्युगानि ते त्रीणि वसंति नाकसद्मनि .. 55 ..
17.1.m: Those who perform a śrāddha on the full-moon day of Jyaiṣṭha conjoined with the Jyeṣṭhā constellation at Tritakūpaka, / dwell in the heavenly abode for three yugas.

17.1.s:
yo vrajeśavane nadyāṃ dināni nava paṃca ca ..
tiṣṭhate ca naraḥ svargaṃ vaikuṇṭhamabhigacchati .. 56 ..
17.1.d:
यो व्रजेशवने नद्यां दिनानि नव पंच च ..
तिष्ठते च नरः स्वर्गं वैकुण्ठमभिगच्छति .. 56 ..
17.1.m: Whatever man stays at the river in Vrajeśavana for nine and five days, / goes to heaven, to Vaikuṇṭha.

17.1.s:
śrāvaṇasya tu māsasya pūrṇāyāṃ pūrvasāgare ..
snānaṃ dānaṃ japaṃ śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kurvanna śocati .. 57 ..
17.1.d:
श्रावणस्य तु मासस्य पूर्णायां पूर्वसागरे ..
स्नानं दानं जपं श्राद्धं नरः कुर्वन्न शोचति .. 57 ..
17.1.m: On the full moon of the month of Śrāvaṇa at the eastern ocean, / a man performing bath, gift, recitation, and śrāddha does not grieve.

17.1.s:
tathā bhādrapade kṣetre prabhāse śaśibhūṣaṇam ..
pūjayitvā naro liṃgaṃ devaliṃgī bhavettataḥ .. 58 ..
17.1.d:
तथा भाद्रपदे क्षेत्रे प्रभासे शशिभूषणम् ..
पूजयित्वा नरो लिंगं देवलिंगी भवेत्ततः .. 58 ..
17.1.m: Likewise, having worshipped the moon-adorned liṅga in the sacred field of Prabhāsa in Bhādrapada, / a man will then become endowed with a divine body.

17.1.s:
āśvine caṃdrabhāgāyāṃ śrāddhaṃ snānaṃ karoti yaḥ ..
sthānaṃ yugasahasrāṇāṃ kṛtaṃ tena triviṣṭape .. 59 ..
17.1.d:
आश्विने चंद्रभागायां श्राद्धं स्नानं करोति यः ..
स्थानं युगसहस्राणां कृतं तेन त्रिविष्टपे .. 59 ..
17.1.m: He who performs bath and śrāddha at the Candrabhāgā in Āśvina, / by him an abode in heaven is secured for thousands of yugas.

17.1.s:
aṣṭākṣaraiścaturbāhuṃ dhyāyaṃti munisattamāḥ ..
bahunā'tra kimuktena gajāhaṃ pravadāmi te .. 7.2.1.60 ..
[[File:Damodar Kund - Junagadh - Gujarat - DSC004.jpg|thumb|600px|dāmodarakuṇḍaḥ]]
17.1.d:
अष्टाक्षरैश्चतुर्बाहुं ध्यायंति मुनिसत्तमाः ..
बहुनाऽत्र किमुक्तेन गजाहं प्रवदामि ते .. 7.2.1.60 ..
[[Fइले:दमोदर् कुन्द् - जुनगध् - गुजरत् - द्स्च्004.ज्प्ग्|थुम्ब्|600प्x|दामोदरकुण्डः]]
17.1.m:
The best of sages meditate upon the four-armed one with the eight-syllable mantra; / what need of saying much here? O Gaja, I tell you:
[[File:Damodar Kund - Junagadh - Gujarat - DSC004.jpg|thumb|600px|dāmodarakuṇḍaḥ]]

17.1.s:
dāmodarasamaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati ..
māsānāṃ kārttikaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kārttike bhīṣmapaṃcakam .. 61 ..
17.1.d:
दामोदरसमं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति ..
मासानां कार्त्तिकः श्रेष्ठः कार्त्तिके भीष्मपंचकम् .. 61 ..
17.1.m: There was never, nor will there ever be, a sacred ford equal to Dāmodara. / Among the months Kārttika is the best, and in Kārttika the five days of Bhīṣma.

17.1.s:
tatrāpi dvādaśī śreṣṭhā rājandāmodare jale ..
kimanyairbahubhistīrtheḥ ki kṣetraiḥ ki mahāvanaiḥ ..
dāmodare naraḥ snātvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 62 ..
17.1.d:
तत्रापि द्वादशी श्रेष्ठा राजन्दामोदरे जले ..
किमन्यैर्बहुभिस्तीर्थेः कि क्षेत्रैः कि महावनैः ..
दामोदरे नरः स्नात्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 62 ..
17.1.m: Even there the twelfth day is best in the waters of Dāmodara, O king. / What is the use of other numerous sacred fords, what of sacred fields, what of great forests? / Having bathed at Dāmodara, a man is completely freed from all sins.

17.1.s:
.. gaja uvāca .. ..
bhadra bhadraṃ tvayā proktaṃ rasāyanamivāparam ..
bhūyo'haṃ śrotumicchāmi tīrthasyāsya mahāphalam .. 63 ..
17.1.d:
.. गज उवाच .. ..
भद्र भद्रं त्वया प्रोक्तं रसायनमिवापरम् ..
भूयोऽहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तीर्थस्यास्य महाफलम् .. 63 ..
17.1.m: Gaja said: / O Bhadra, auspicious things have been spoken by you, like another elixir of life. / Again I wish to hear the great fruit of this sacred ford.

17.1.s:
ke deśāḥ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ tu kā nadī keḥ ca parvatāḥ ..
janā vasaṃti ke tatra ṛṣayaḥ ke tapasvinaḥ .. 64 ..
17.1.d:
के देशाः किं प्रमाणं तु का नदी केः च पर्वताः ..
जना वसंति के तत्र ऋषयः के तपस्विनः .. 64 ..
17.1.m: What regions, what size, what river, and what mountains are there? / What people live there, what seers and ascetics?

17.1.s:
.. bhadra uvāca .. ..
pṛthivī vasusaṃpūrṇā sāgareṇa tu veṣṭitā ..
maṃḍitā nagarairgrāmaiḥ suraiḥ parapuraṃjaya .. 65 ..
17.1.d:
.. भद्र उवाच .. ..
पृथिवी वसुसंपूर्णा सागरेण तु वेष्टिता ..
मंडिता नगरैर्ग्रामैः सुरैः परपुरंजय .. 65 ..
17.1.m: Bhadra said: / The earth is filled with wealth and encircled by the ocean, / adorned with cities and villages, and with gods, O conqueror of enemy cities.

17.1.s:
vārāṇasī prabhāsaṃ ca saṃgamaṃ sitakṛṣṇayoḥ ..
evaṃ sārāṇi tīrthāni yasmānmṛtyuharāṇi ca .. 66 ..
17.1.d:
वाराणसी प्रभासं च संगमं सितकृष्णयोः ..
एवं साराणि तीर्थानि यस्मान्मृत्युहराणि च .. 66 ..
17.1.m: Vārāṇasī, Prabhāsa, and the confluence of the white and black [rivers]— / these are the essential sacred fords, because they take away death.

17.1.s:
dāmodareti ye nūnaṃ smaraṃto yatra tatra hi..
te vasaṃti harergehaṃ na saraṃti kadācana .. 67 ..
17.1.d:
दामोदरेति ये नूनं स्मरंतो यत्र तत्र हि..
ते वसंति हरेर्गेहं न सरंति कदाचन .. 67 ..
17.1.m: Those who remember [the name] 'Dāmodara', wherever they may be, / live in Hari's abode and never wander [in transmigration].

17.1.s:
somanāthasya sānnidhya udayanto girirmahān ..
tasya paścimabhāge tu raivataka iti smṛtaḥ .. 68 ..
17.1.d:
सोमनाथस्य सान्निध्य उदयन्तो गिरिर्महान् ..
तस्य पश्चिमभागे तु रैवतक इति स्मृतः .. 68 ..
17.1.m: In the presence of Somanātha is the great mountain Udayanta; / on its western side is known the one called Raivataka.

17.1.s:
vāhinī vahate tatra nadī kāṃcanaśekharāt ..
dhātavastatra te raktāḥ śvetā nīlāstathā'sitāḥ .. 69 ..
17.1.d:
वाहिनी वहते तत्र नदी कांचनशेखरात् ..
धातवस्तत्र ते रक्ताः श्वेता नीलास्तथाऽसिताः .. 69 ..
17.1.m: There flows a stream, a river from Kāñcanaśekhara. / The minerals there are red, white, blue, and black.

17.1.s:
pāṣāṇāḥ kuñjarākārāścānye sairibhasannibhāḥ ..
caṇakākṛtayaścānye anye gokṣurakaprabhāḥ .. 7.2.1.70 ..
17.1.d:
पाषाणाः कुञ्जराकाराश्चान्ये सैरिभसन्निभाः ..
चणकाकृतयश्चान्ये अन्ये गोक्षुरकप्रभाः .. 7.2.1.70 ..
17.1.m: The rocks have the shapes of elephants, others resemble buffaloes, / others have the form of chickpeas, and others have the appearance of gokṣuraka thorns.

17.1.s:
vṛkṣā vallyaśca gulmāśca saṃtānāḥ saṃtyanekaśaḥ ..
sarvaṃ tatkāṃcanamayaṃ mūlaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ dalam .. 71 ..
17.1.d:
वृक्षा वल्ल्यश्च गुल्माश्च संतानाः संत्यनेकशः ..
सर्वं तत्कांचनमयं मूलं पुष्पं फलं दलम् .. 71 ..
17.1.m: There are trees, creepers, shrubs, and groves in abundance; / every root, flower, fruit, and leaf there is made of gold.

17.1.s:

By the power of that sacred ford, they do not commit wicked deeds. / When beasts, birds, and reptiles meet death in due course of time,
They all mount aerial chariots and go to the abode of Hari. / Where leaves, flowers, fruits, and the like are brought down by the wind,
everything that touches the water of that river attains liberation. / That river, O king, has pierced the earth and come from Pātāla.
Formerly, the king of serpents came by that path / to bathe in the Damodara tīrtha, which destroys Death and Yama.
Even the Moon, having come from heaven to perform a most plentiful sacrifice, / was freed from consumption and went to heaven free from disease.
Gifts were given there, having arrived in Kārtika, by Bali, / and according to rule by Hariścandra, Nala, and Nahuṣa,
and by Nābhāga, Ambarīṣa, and others deeds most difficult to perform were done. / Having given many gifts—elephants, cows, horses, chariots,

bulls, gold, land, and various kinds of gems, / umbrellas, vehicles, and garments to the foremost of brahmins,
and foods mixed with savory flavors—before Dāmodara, / they went to the realm of Viṣṇu and do not return to the surface of the earth.
Whoever gives a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water at that sacred ford / to the twice-born with devotion, goes to the One who reclines upon the waters.
And whoever gives food in its natural state, or a fistful, to one afflicted by hunger, / mounts an excellent aerial chariot and goes to Soma.
Having made mountains made of food before Dāmodara, / worshiped with fruits and flowers, one should offer a lamp with a wick.
Attaining a station difficult to reach, he delivers a hundred families. / Even if a gift measuring merely four finger-breadths is given before Dāmodara,
he is exalted in heaven for a thousand yugas. / Do not go to the slope of the Himālaya, nor to Malaya, nor to Mandara;

go to Mount Raivataka, where Dāmodara resides. / A twice-born man who observes a fast for a month before Dāmodara
does not return in time, but goes to the city of Dāmodara. / And whatever man or woman undertakes a complete fast, / having transcended all worlds, reaches the home of Hari.
Five hundred obstacles stay there constantly, / working the destruction of dharma; a man does not easily go there.
By Pradyumna, Balarāma, Śaineya, Gada, Cakra, and others, / amounting to hundred-thousands, that great mountain is always served.
Indeed, their women sport constantly before Dāmodara— / moon-faced, fair, dark, of slender waists,
large-hipped, fine-haired, radiant, with wide and long eyes, / with charming cheeks and graceful, with lovely armpits and beautiful breasts,
splendid, with well-formed shanks, feet, and lovely toes— / royal daughters laugh and take delight on that mountain.

17.1.m:
Safflower dye on both feet, saffron, and a yellow bodice / they give to brahmin women here, competing one by one.
Foods to chew, to feast on, to drink, to lick, to suck, and glaucous dishes, / betel leaf together with flowers on the day of Hari in Kārtika,
and beholding the Revatīkuṇḍa, one should bestow excellent fruit. / She becomes a mother of sons, endowed with prosperity, fortunate, and chaste.
Having acted thus, that night is spent without sleep / through holy chants of the Vedas and readings of the Bhārata narrative,
with shouts of huṃ, the clapping of palms, and rhythmic beats again and again, / while women speaking regional tongues within the circle of women / join in laughter and dance, O king, before Dāmodara.
Whoever builds an abode of Śiva made of five stones / is exalted in the world of heaven for five thousand years.
Having built one made of ten stones before Dāmodara, / he sports and rejoices in heaven for ten thousand years.

17.1.m:
Whoever builds an edifice of a hundred stones, O great king, / a beautiful, shining temple, goes to the abode of Hari.
Having made a sanctuary of a thousand stones, endowed with many forms, / he transcends all worlds and attains the supreme Brahman.
One should offer a five-colored banner above the temple of Dāmodara; / for as many divine years as that measure, he goes to heaven.
The auspicious sacred field Vastrāpatha extends for one gavyūti around it; / upon seeing it, many sins are completely dissolved.
O king, he attains that state having gone to which one does not return. / Having worshiped the god Bhava, who destroys the cause of worldly existence,
a man or woman, O best of kings, is exalted in the world of Śiva. / Having heard that well-spoken word of Bhadra,
he came to celebrate the Kārtikī festival before the god Dāmodara; then, / accompanied by brahmins knowers of the Veda, versed in the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas,

क्षत्रियैः क्षत्रधर्मज्ञैर्वैश्यैर्दानपरायणैः ..
सह शूद्रैः समायातस्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे गजो नृपः .. 7.2.1.110 ..
दत्त्वा दानान्यनेकानि हुत्वा हविर्हुताशने ..
अग्निष्टोमादिकान्यज्ञान्हयमेधादिकान्बहून् ..
चकार विधिवद्राजा गजस्तत्र समाहितः .. 111 ..
ततश्च न्यवसत्तत्र तपः कर्तुं सहर्षिभिः ..
ऊर्द्ध्वपादाः स्थिता विप्राः पीत्वा धूममधोमुखाः ..
शुष्कपत्राशनाश्चान्ये अन्ये वै फलभोजनाः .. 112 ..
मूलानि चान्ये भक्षंति अन्ये वार्यंशना द्विजाः ..
आलोकंति स्वमन्ये च तथान्ये जलशायिनः .. 113 ..
पञ्चाग्निसाधकाश्चान्ये शिलाचूर्णस्य भक्षकाः ..
जपंति चान्ये संशुद्धा गायत्रीं वेदमातरम् ..
सावित्रीं मनसा चान्ये देवीमन्ये सरस्वतीम्.. 114 ..
सूक्तानि हि पवित्राणि ब्रह्मणा निर्मितानि च ..
अन्येऽवसंस्तदा तत्र द्वादशाक्षरचिन्तकाः .. 115 ..
17.1.m:
by kṣatriyas knowing the duties of the kṣatriya, by vaiśyas devoted to giving, / and together with śūdras, King Gaja arrived at that sacred ford.
Having given many gifts, having offered oblations into the sacrificial fire, / King Gaja, concentrated in mind, performed in accordance with rule / Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices, and many horse-sacrifices.
And then he dwelt there to perform austerity together with the seers. / Brahmins stood with feet raised upward, drinking smoke with their heads turned down; / others ate dried leaves, while others fed on fruits;
others ate roots, and other twice-born ate only water; / others gazed within themselves, and others reclined in the water.
And others practiced the five fires; [others] ate powdered stone; / and others, fully purified, chanted the Gāyatrī, mother of the Vedas, / while others mentally [recited] Sāvitrī, and others the goddess Sarasvatī; 114
and the purifying hymns created by Brahmā. / Others then dwelt there meditating on the twelve-syllable mantra. 115

17.1.s:
ālokya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥpunaḥ ..
idameva suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā .. 116 ..
ārādhitaḥ suduṣpāre bhave bhagavato vinā ..
tathā nānyo mahādevātpatantaṃ yo'bhirakṣati .. 117 ..
gatāgatāni vartaṃte caṃdrasūryādayo grahāḥ ..
adyāpi na nivartaṃte dvādaśākṣaraciṃtakāḥ .. 118 ...
ye'kṣarā ṛṣayaścānye devalokajigīṣavaḥ ..
prāpnuvaṃti tataḥ sthānaṃ dagdhabījaṃ ca tattathā .. 119 ..
sakṛduccaritaṃ yena harirityakṣaradvayam ..
baddhaḥ parikarastena mokṣāya gamanaṃ prati .. 7.2.1.120 ..
ekabhaktaṃ tathā naktamayācyamuṣitaṃ tathā..
evamādīni cānyāni kṛtvā dāmodarāgrataḥ ..
kṛtakṛtyā bhavaṃtīha yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam.. 121 ..
sa rājā ṛṣibhiḥ sārddhaṃ yāvattiṣṭhati tatra vai ..
vimānāni sahasrāṇi tāvattatrāgatāni ca .. 122 ..
17.1.d:
आलोक्य सर्वशास्त्राणि विचार्य च पुनःपुनः ..
इदमेव सुनिष्पन्नं ध्येयो नारायणः सदा .. 116 ..
आराधितः सुदुष्पारे भवे भगवतो विना ..
तथा नान्यो महादेवात्पतन्तं योऽभिरक्षति .. 117 ..
गतागतानि वर्तंते चंद्रसूर्यादयो ग्रहाः ..
अद्यापि न निवर्तंते द्वादशाक्षरचिंतकाः .. 118 ...
येऽक्षरा ऋषयश्चान्ये देवलोकजिगीषवः ..
प्राप्नुवंति ततः स्थानं दग्धबीजं च तत्तथा .. 119 ..
सकृदुच्चरितं येन हरिरित्यक्षरद्वयम् ..
बद्धः परिकरस्तेन मोक्षाय गमनं प्रति .. 7.2.1.120 ..
एकभक्तं तथा नक्तमयाच्यमुषितं तथा..
एवमादीनि चान्यानि कृत्वा दामोदराग्रतः ..
कृतकृत्या भवंतीह यावदाभूतसंप्लवम्.. 121 ..
स राजा ऋषिभिः सार्द्धं यावत्तिष्ठति तत्र वै ..
विमानानि सहस्राणि तावत्तत्रागतानि च .. 122 ..
17.1.m:
Having examined all the scriptures and deliberated again and again, / this alone has been firmly settled: Nārāyaṇa is always to be meditated upon. 116
In this world of transmigration so difficult to cross, except for the Lord who is worshipped, / there is likewise none other than Mahādeva who protects one who is falling. 117
The planets—the moon, sun, and others—undergo rising and setting, / [yet] even today those who meditate on the twelve-syllable mantra do not turn back [to samsāra]. 118
Those imperishable seers and others who desire to conquer the realm of the gods / attain that place from there, and thus their seeds [of karma] are burnt. 119
He by whom the two syllables "Ha-ri" are uttered even once / has girded his loins to depart toward liberation. 7.2.1.120
Observing a single meal a day, fasting at night, or eating only unasked-for food, / and performing other such [vows] before Dāmodara, / they achieve their purpose here until the dissolution of the elements. 121
As long as that king remained there together with the seers, / so long did thousands of aerial chariots arrive there. 122

17.1.s:
gaṃdharvāpsarastatra siddhacāraṇakinnarāḥ ..
sarve vimānamārūḍhāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 123..
sarvairjanapadaiḥ sārddha sa rājā bhāryayā saha ..
gato vimānamārūḍho yattatpadamanāmayam .. 124 ..
ya idaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ śṛṇuyādvā'pi mānavaḥ ..
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati .. 125 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye dāmodaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 1 ..
dāmodara upari paurāṇikasaṃdarbhāḥ
dāmodara upari ṭippaṇī
[[File:Bhavnath Mahadev.jpg|thumb|600px|bhavanāthamahādevaḥ ]]
17.1.d:
गंधर्वाप्सरस्तत्र सिद्धचारणकिन्नराः ..
सर्वे विमानमारूढाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः .. 123..
सर्वैर्जनपदैः सार्द्ध स राजा भार्यया सह ..
गतो विमानमारूढो यत्तत्पदमनामयम् .. 124 ..
य इदं पठते नित्यं शृणुयाद्वाऽपि मानवः ..
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति .. 125 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये दामोदरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः .. 1 ..
दामोदर उपरि पौराणिकसंदर्भाः
दामोदर उपरि टिप्पणी

17.1.m:
Gandharvas, apsarases there, siddhas, cāraṇas, and kinnaras— / all mounted aerial chariots by the hundreds and by the thousands. 123
Together with all the countryside people, that king, along with his wife, / mounted an aerial chariot and went to that abode free from disease. 124
The mortal who constantly recites this or listens to it / is completely freed from all sins and attains the supreme Brahman. 125
Thus ends the first chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Dāmodara', in the Vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmya, in the second [sub-section] of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the text of eighty-one thousand verses. 1

17.2.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tato gacchenmahādevi kṣetraṃ vastrāpathaṃ punaḥ ..
yatprabhāsasya sarvasvaṃ kṣetraṃ nābhiḥ priyaṃ mama .. 1 ..
17.2.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्महादेवि क्षेत्रं वस्त्रापथं पुनः ..
यत्प्रभासस्य सर्वस्वं क्षेत्रं नाभिः प्रियं मम .. 1 ..
17.2.m: Īśvara said: / Then one should go, O great goddess, once more to the sacred field Vastrāpatha, / which is the all-in-all of Prabhāsa, the navel [of the earth], and dear to me. 1

17.2.s:
yatra sākṣādbhavo devaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakaḥ ..
pṛthivyāṃ sa tvadhiṣṭhātā tattvānāmādimaḥ prabhuḥ .. 2 ..
17.2.d:
यत्र साक्षाद्भवो देवः सृष्टिसंहारकारकः ..
पृथिव्यां स त्वधिष्ठाता तत्त्वानामादिमः प्रभुः .. 2 ..
17.2.m: Where the god Bhava is present in visible form, the cause of creation and dissolution, / he is the presiding deity upon earth, the primeval lord of the principles. 2

17.2.s:
sa svayaṃbhūḥ sthitastatra prabhāse bhūtido bhavaḥ ..
bhavatīdaṃ jagadyasmāttasmādbhava iti smṛtaḥ .. 3 ..
17.2.d:
स स्वयंभूः स्थितस्तत्र प्रभासे भूतिदो भवः ..
भवतीदं जगद्यस्मात्तस्माद्भव इति स्मृतः .. 3 ..
17.2.m: He stands there in Prabhāsa as the self-manifest Bhava who grants prosperity; / since this universe comes to be (bhavati) from him, he is remembered as Bhava. 3

17.2.s:
yaḥ sakṛtkurute yātrāṃ kṣetre vastrāpathe punaḥ ..
vigāhya tatra tīrthāni kṛtakṛtyaḥ sa jāyate .. 4 ..
17.2.d:
यः सकृत्कुरुते यात्रां क्षेत्रे वस्त्रापथे पुनः ..
विगाह्य तत्र तीर्थानि कृतकृत्यः स जायते .. 4 ..
17.2.m: He who makes a pilgrimage even once to the sacred field Vastrāpatha / and bathes in the sacred fords there achieves his purpose. 4

17.2.s:
atha dṛṣṭvā bhavaṃ devaṃ sakṛtpūjyavidhānataḥ ..
kedārayātrāphalabhāksa bhavenmanujottamaḥ .. 5 ..
17.2.d:
अथ दृष्ट्वा भवं देवं सकृत्पूज्यविधानतः ..
केदारयात्राफलभाक्स भवेन्मनुजोत्तमः .. 5 ..
17.2.m: Now, having beheld the god Bhava and worshipped him once according to the rule, / that best of men shall obtain the fruit of a pilgrimage to Kedāra. 5

17.2.s:
caitre māsi bhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā na punarjāyate bhuvi ..
vaiśākhyāmathavā samyagbhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimucyate .. 6 ..
17.2.d:
चैत्रे मासि भवं दृष्ट्वा न पुनर्जायते भुवि ..
वैशाख्यामथवा सम्यग्भवं दृष्ट्वा विमुच्यते .. 6 ..
17.2.m: Beholding Bhava in the month of Caitra, one is not born again on earth; / or, beholding Bhava properly on the full moon of Vaiśākha, one is liberated. 6

17.2.s:
vārāṇasyāṃ kurukṣetre narmadāyāṃ tu yatphalam ..
tatphalaṃ nimiṣārddhena bhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā dinedine .. 7 ..
17.2.d:
वाराणस्यां कुरुक्षेत्रे नर्मदायां तु यत्फलम् ..
तत्फलं निमिषार्द्धेन भवं दृष्ट्वा दिनेदिने .. 7 ..
17.2.m: Whatever fruit is [found] in Vārāṇasī, in Kurukṣetra, and on the Narmadā, / that fruit is [gained] in half a twinkling of an eye by beholding Bhava day by day. 7

17.2.s:
durllabhastatra vāsastu durllabhaṃ bhavadarśanam ..
pretatvaṃ naiva tasyāsti na yāmyā nārakī vyathā .. 8 ..
17.2.d:
दुर्ल्लभस्तत्र वासस्तु दुर्ल्लभं भवदर्शनम् ..
प्रेतत्वं नैव तस्यास्ति न याम्या नारकी व्यथा .. 8 ..
17.2.m: Dwelling there is hard to attain, and the darśana of Bhava is hard to attain; / for him there is no state of being a ghost, nor the hellish torment of Yama. 8

17.2.s:
yeṣāṃ bhavālaye prāṇā gatā vai varavarṇini ..
dhanyānāmapi dhanyāste devānāmapi devatāḥ .. 9 ..
17.2.d:
येषां भवालये प्राणा गता वै वरवर्णिनि ..
धन्यानामपि धन्यास्ते देवानामपि देवताः .. 9 ..
17.2.m: Those whose vital breaths depart in the abode of Bhava, O fair-complexioned one, / are the most blessed among the blessed, and deities even to the gods. 9

17.2.s:
vastrāpathe matiryeṣāṃ bhave yeṣāṃ matiḥ sthirā ..
godānaṃ tatra śaṃsaṃti brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhojanam..
piṃḍadānaṃ ca tatraiva kalpāṃtaṃ tṛptimā vahet.. 7.2.2.10 ..
17.2.d:
वस्त्रापथे मतिर्येषां भवे येषां मतिः स्थिरा ..
गोदानं तत्र शंसंति ब्राह्मणानां च भोजनम्..
पिंडदानं च तत्रैव कल्पांतं तृप्तिमा वहेत्.. 7.2.2.10 ..
17.2.m: They praise the gift of a cow and the feeding of brahmins there / for those whose minds are set on Vastrāpatha and whose minds are firm in Bhava; / and the offering of rice-balls in that very place will bring satisfaction until the end of the kalpa. 7.2.2.10

17.2.s:
iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ te bhavodbhavam ..
śrutaṃ pāpopaśamanaṃ yajñāyutaphalapradam .. 11 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye vastrāpathakṣetrabhavamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ .. 2 ..
vastra/vastrāpatha upari paurāṇikasaṃdarbhāḥ
17.2.d:
इति संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तं माहात्म्यं ते भवोद्भवम् ..
श्रुतं पापोपशमनं यज्ञायुतफलप्रदम् .. 11 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रभवमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः .. 2 ..
वस्त्र/वस्त्रापथ उपरि पौराणिकसंदर्भाः
17.2.m:
Thus has the māhātmya pertaining to Bhava been declared to you in brief; / when heard, it pacifies sins and grants the fruit of ten thousand sacrifices. 11
Thus ends the second chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Bhava in the Sacred Field of Vastrāpatha', in the Vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmya, in the second [sub-section] of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the text of eighty-one thousand verses. 2

17.2.s:
kathanamasti yat vastrāpathakṣetraḥ nābhiḥ asti. ayaṃ pratīyate yat ayaṃ nābhiḥ maṇipūracakraḥ asti. maṇipūracakraḥ agneḥ sthānamasti. rajanīśamahodayānusāreṇa (kuṇḍalī aura sāta śarīra ) maṇipūracakraḥ śraddhā - aśraddhā, śraddhā - sandehasya padaḥ asti. yathā loke sārvatrikarūpeṇa pracalitaḥ asti, viṣṇoḥ nābhitaḥ padmopari brahmaṇaḥ āvirbhāvaḥ bhavati evaṃ brahmā sṛṣṭiṃ karoti. ayaṃ pratīyate yat maṇipūracakraḥ tatpadamasti yatra daivasya pradhānatā asti, puruṣārthasya prādhānyaṃ nāsti. brahmaṇaḥ āvirbhāvaḥ puruṣārthasya prathamā raśmiḥ asti. saḥ svecchayā sṛṣṭiṃ kartuṃ śaknoti. bhavasya saṃdarbhe purāṇeṣu (bhāgavatapurāṇam 5.17.15 )kathanamasti yat ilāvṛte tu bhagavānbhava eka eva pumānna hyanyaḥ.

17.2.d:
कथनमस्ति यत् वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रः नाभिः अस्ति. अयं प्रतीयते यत् अयं नाभिः मणिपूरचक्रः अस्ति. मणिपूरचक्रः अग्नेः स्थानमस्ति. रजनीशमहोदयानुसारेण (कुण्डली और सात शरीर ) मणिपूरचक्रः श्रद्धा - अश्रद्धा, श्रद्धा - सन्देहस्य पदः अस्ति. यथा लोके सार्वत्रिकरूपेण प्रचलितः अस्ति, विष्णोः नाभितः पद्मोपरि ब्रह्मणः आविर्भावः भवति एवं ब्रह्मा सृष्टिं करोति. अयं प्रतीयते यत् मणिपूरचक्रः तत्पदमस्ति यत्र दैवस्य प्रधानता अस्ति, पुरुषार्थस्य प्राधान्यं नास्ति. ब्रह्मणः आविर्भावः पुरुषार्थस्य प्रथमा रश्मिः अस्ति. सः स्वेच्छया सृष्टिं कर्तुं शक्नोति. भवस्य संदर्भे पुराणेषु (भागवतपुराणम् 5.17.15 )कथनमस्ति यत् इलावृते तु भगवान्भव एक एव पुमान्न ह्यन्यः.
भव उपरि पौराणिकसंदर्भाः
भव/यकृत उपरि टिप्पणी
नाभि उपरि टिप्पणी
17.2.m:
It is stated that the sacred field of Vastrāpatha is the navel. It appears that this navel is the maṇipūracakra. The maṇipūracakra is the place of fire. According to Rajneesh (Kuṇḍalinī and the Seven Bodies), the maṇipūracakra is the state of faith and unfaith, faith and doubt. As is universally widespread in the world, Brahmā appears upon the lotus from the navel of Viṣṇu, and thus Brahmā carries out creation. It appears that the maṇipūracakra is that state where divine destiny is predominant and human effort does not have predominance. The manifestation of Brahmā is the first ray of human effort. He can perform creation by his own will. In the context of Bhava, it is stated in the Purāṇas (Bhāgavatapurāṇa 5.17.15) that in Ilāvṛta, the blessed lord Bhava is the only male, indeed no other.

17.3.s:
.. īśvara uvāca ..
atha vastrāpathe kṣetre saṃti tīrthāni koṭiśaḥ..
tathāpi sāraṃ te vacmi sarvatīrthamahodayam .. 1 ..
17.3.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच ..
अथ वस्त्रापथे क्षेत्रे संति तीर्थानि कोटिशः..
तथापि सारं ते वच्मि सर्वतीर्थमहोदयम् .. 1 ..
17.3.m: Īśvara said: / Now, in the sacred field of Vastrāpatha there are crores of sacred fords; / nevertheless, I tell you their essence, the great elevation of all sacred fords. // 1

17.3.s:
dāmodare nadī proktā svarṇareṣeti yā smṛtā ..
brahmakuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva tathā brahmeśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 2 ..
17.3.d:
दामोदरे नदी प्रोक्ता स्वर्णरेषेति या स्मृता ..
ब्रह्मकुण्डं च तत्रैव तथा ब्रह्मेश्वरः स्मृतः .. 2 ..
17.3.m: At Dāmodara a river is proclaimed, known as Svarṇareṣā; / Brahmakuṇḍa is right there, and likewise Brahmeśvara is recorded. // 2

17.3.s:
kālameghaśca saṃprokto bhavo dāmodaraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
gavyūtidvitayenaiva kālikā tatra kīrtitā .. 3 ..
17.3.d:
कालमेघश्च संप्रोक्तो भवो दामोदरः स्मृतः ..
गव्यूतिद्वितयेनैव कालिका तत्र कीर्तिता .. 3 ..
17.3.m: And Kālamegha is proclaimed, and Bhava [along with] Dāmodara are recorded. / Just two gavyūtis away, Kālikā is celebrated there. // 3

17.3.s:
indreśvaraśca tatraiva raivataḥ parvatastathā ..
ujjayaṃtaśca tatraiva devaḥ kumbhīśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 4 ..
17.3.d:
इन्द्रेश्वरश्च तत्रैव रैवतः पर्वतस्तथा ..
उज्जयंतश्च तत्रैव देवः कुम्भीश्वरः स्मृतः .. 4 ..
17.3.m: And Indreśvara is right there, as well as Mount Raivata; / and Ujjayanta is right there, and the deity is recorded as Kumbhīśvara. // 4

17.3.s:
bhīmeśvaraśca tatraiva tataḥ kṣetraṃ mahāprabham ..
tailasāraṇikaṃnāma tretāyāṃ haimamārakam .. 5 ..
17.3.d:
भीमेश्वरश्च तत्रैव ततः क्षेत्रं महाप्रभम् ..
तैलसारणिकंनाम त्रेतायां हैममारकम् .. 5 ..
17.3.m: And Bhīmeśvara is right there; beyond it lies the splendid sacred field / named Tailasāraṇika, called Haimamāraka in the Tretā age. // 5

17.3.s:
paṃcagavyūtimātraṃ tu tatkṣetraṃ saṃprakīrtitam ..
mṛgīkuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva sarvapātakanāśanam .. 6 ..
17.3.d:
पंचगव्यूतिमात्रं तु तत्क्षेत्रं संप्रकीर्तितम् ..
मृगीकुण्डं च तत्रैव सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 6 ..
17.3.m: That sacred field is proclaimed to measure just five gavyūtis; / and Mṛgīkuṇḍa is right there, destroying all sins. // 6

17.3.s:
etadvastrāpathaṃ kṣetraṃ ratnadhātvostathā''karam ..
kathitaṃ tava deveśi punaḥ saṃkṣepato mayā .. 7 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṃḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye pravaratīrthānukīrtananāma tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ .. 3 ..
17.3.d:
एतद्वस्त्रापथं क्षेत्रं रत्नधात्वोस्तथा'ऽकरम् ..
कथितं तव देवेशि पुनः संक्षेपतो मया .. 7 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखंडे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये प्रवरतीर्थानुकीर्तननाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः .. 3 ..
17.3.m:
This sacred field of Vastrāpatha, a mine of jewels and minerals, / has thus been described to you again in brief by me, O ruler of gods! // 7
Thus ends the third chapter, named 'Enumeration of the Foremost Sacred Fords,' in the Vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmya, in the second [sub-section of] Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 3

17.4.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tato gacchenmahādevi dunnāvilleti viśrutam ..
yojanasyāṃtare devi paścime maṃgalasthiteḥ .. 1 ..
17.4.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्महादेवि दुन्नाविल्लेति विश्रुतम् ..
योजनस्यांतरे देवि पश्चिमे मंगलस्थितेः .. 1 ..
17.4.m: Īśvara said: / Then, O great goddess, one should go to the well-known Dunnāvilla, / at a distance of a yojana to the west of the station of Maṅgalā, O goddess. // 1

17.4.s:
dunnako yatra bhīmena bhuktvā tyaktaḥ purā priye ..
tatraiva vivaraṃ divyaṃ mahā pātālamārgadam .. 2 ..
17.4.d:
दुन्नको यत्र भीमेन भुक्त्वा त्यक्तः पुरा प्रिये ..
तत्रैव विवरं दिव्यं महा पातालमार्गदम् .. 2 ..
17.4.m: Where, having eaten, the dunnaka was formerly discarded by Bhīma, O beloved, / right there is a divine chasm that provides a great path to Pātāla. // 2

17.4.s:
tasya kalpaḥ purā proktaḥ pātālottarasaṃgrahe ..
tatra liṃgānyanekāni siddhasthānāni ṣoḍaśa .. 3 ..
17.4.d:
तस्य कल्पः पुरा प्रोक्तः पातालोत्तरसंग्रहे ..
तत्र लिंगान्यनेकानि सिद्धस्थानानि षोडश .. 3 ..
17.4.m: Its ritual procedure was told long ago in the Pātālottarasaṃgraha; / there are many liṅgas there, sixteen abodes of perfections. // 3

17.4.s:
suvarṇasyākaraḥ pūrvaṃ tatsthānamabhavatpriye ..
tasminsthāne narairdevi gantavyaṃ bhūtilipsayā .. 4 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye dunnāvillahṛdgiristhānamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma caturtho'dhyāyaḥ .. 4 ..
17.4.d:
सुवर्णस्याकरः पूर्वं तत्स्थानमभवत्प्रिये ..
तस्मिन्स्थाने नरैर्देवि गन्तव्यं भूतिलिप्सया .. 4 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये दुन्नाविल्लहृद्गिरिस्थानमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः .. 4 ..
17.4.m:
Formerly, that place was a mine of gold, O beloved; / men desirous of prosperity should go to that place, O goddess. // 4
Thus ends the fourth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Dunnāvillahṛda Mountain Abode,' in the Vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmya, in the second [sub-section of] Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 4

17.5.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tato gacchenmahādevi maṃgalātpaścime sthitam ..
gaṃgāsrotastathā liṃgaṃ surārkaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 1 ..
17.5.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्महादेवि मंगलात्पश्चिमे स्थितम् ..
गंगास्रोतस्तथा लिंगं सुरार्कं च विशेषतः .. 1 ..
17.5.m: Īśvara said: / Then, O great goddess, one should go to that situated to the west of Maṅgalā: / the current of Gaṅgā, as well as the liṅga, and Surārka in particular. // 1

17.5.s:
tāngacchedvidhivaddevi yadi yātrāphalepsutā ..
snātvā piṇḍapradānaṃ ca kuryāttatra yathārthataḥ ..
brāhmaṇebhyastathā deyamannaṃ bhūri sadakṣiṇam .. 2 ..
17.5.d:
तान्गच्छेद्विधिवद्देवि यदि यात्राफलेप्सुता ..
स्नात्वा पिण्डप्रदानं च कुर्यात्तत्र यथार्थतः ..
ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तथा देयमन्नं भूरि सदक्षिणम् .. 2 ..
17.5.m: One should go to them according to rule, O goddess, if one desires the fruit of pilgrimage; / having bathed, one should properly offer rice balls there, / and abundant food with fees should be given to brahmins. // 2

17.5.s:
iti te kathitaṃ mayā priye kalipāpaughavināśanaṃ śubham ..
nikhilaṃ tīrthamahodayodayaṃ paṭhitaṃ sadvinihaṃti pāpasaṃhatim .. 3 ..
17.5.d:
इति ते कथितं मया प्रिये कलिपापौघविनाशनं शुभम् ..
निखिलं तीर्थमहोदयोदयं पठितं सद्विनिहंति पापसंहतिम् .. 3 ..
17.5.m: Thus has this auspicious [teaching] been spoken by me to you, O beloved, which destroys the mass of sins of the Kali age; / reciting this, the complete rise of the glory of the sacred ford destroys the multitude of sins. // 3

17.5.s:
idaṃ na deyaṃ durbuddheḥ sutarāṃ pāpanāśanam ..
śrotavyaṃ vidhinā tadvadbhaviṣyoktavidhānataḥ .. 4 ..
17.5.d:
इदं न देयं दुर्बुद्धेः सुतरां पापनाशनम् ..
श्रोतव्यं विधिना तद्वद्भविष्योक्तविधानतः .. 4 ..
17.5.m: This, supremely destructive of sins, should not be given to one of wicked intellect; / it should be heard according to rule, in accordance with the injunction stated in the Bhaviṣya [Purāṇa]. // 4

17.5.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṃḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye gaṃgeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma paṃcamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 5 ..
17.5.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखंडे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये गंगेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम पंचमोऽध्यायः .. 5 ..
17.5.m: Thus ends the fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Gaṅgeśvara,' in the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, in the first [sub-section of] Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 5

17.6.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
adhunā saṃpravakṣyāmi maṃgalātpaścime vrajet ..
tatra siddheśvaraṃ paśyetsarvasiddhipradāyakam .. 1 ..
17.6.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
अधुना संप्रवक्ष्यामि मंगलात्पश्चिमे व्रजेत् ..
तत्र सिद्धेश्वरं पश्येत्सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम् .. 1 ..
17.6.m: Īśvara said: / Now I shall declare: one should go to the west of Maṅgalā; / there one should see Siddheśvara, who grants all perfections. // 1

17.6.s:
tatraiva cakratīrthaṃ tu tīrthakoṭiphalapradam ..
lokeśvaraṃ svayaṃbhūtaṃ pūrvamiṃdreśvareti ca .. 2 ..
17.6.d:
तत्रैव चक्रतीर्थं तु तीर्थकोटिफलप्रदम् ..
लोकेश्वरं स्वयंभूतं पूर्वमिंद्रेश्वरेति च .. 2 ..
17.6.m: Right there is Cakra-tīrtha, granting the fruit of crores of sacred fords, / and the self-manifest Lokeśvara, previously called Indreśvara. // 2

17.6.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ vidhivaddevi tato yakṣavanaṃ vrajet ..
maṃgalātpaścime bhāge yatra devī svayaṃ sthitā .. 3 ..
17.6.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं विधिवद्देवि ततो यक्षवनं व्रजेत् ..
मंगलात्पश्चिमे भागे यत्र देवी स्वयं स्थिता .. 3 ..
17.6.m: Having beheld him according to rule, O goddess, one should then go to Yakṣavana / in the region to the west of Maṅgalā, where the Goddess herself resides. // 3

17.6.s:
yakṣeśvarī mahābhāgā vāṃchitārthapradāyinī ..
tāṃ saṃpūjya vidhānena tato vastrāpathaṃ punaḥ .. 4 ..
17.6.d:
यक्षेश्वरी महाभागा वांछितार्थप्रदायिनी ..
तां संपूज्य विधानेन ततो वस्त्रापथं पुनः .. 4 ..
17.6.m: Yakṣeśvarī, highly blessed, grants desired objects; / having worshiped her according to the prescribed rules, one should then again to Vastrāpatha— // 4

17.6.s:
giriṃ raivatakaṃ gatvā kuryādyātrāvidhānataḥ ..
mṛgīkuṃḍāditīrthāni saṃti tatraiva koṭiśaḥ .. 5 ..
17.6.d:
गिरिं रैवतकं गत्वा कुर्याद्यात्राविधानतः ..
मृगीकुंडादितीर्थानि संति तत्रैव कोटिशः .. 5 ..
17.6.m: having gone to Mount Raivataka, perform the pilgrimage according to the rules; / sacred fords such as Mṛgīkuṇḍa are right there in crores. // 5

17.6.s:
yadbhuktiśikhare devi sīmāliṃgaṃ hi tatsmṛtam ..
daśakoṭistu tīrthāni tatra saṃti varāna ne .. 6 ..
17.6.d:
यद्भुक्तिशिखरे देवि सीमालिंगं हि तत्स्मृतम् ..
दशकोटिस्तु तीर्थानि तत्र संति वरान ने .. 6 ..
17.6.m: The liṅga on that peak of enjoyment, O goddess, is known as the boundary liṅga; / ten crores of sacred fords are there, O fair-faced one! // 6

17.6.s:
yatra vai yādavāḥ siddhāḥ kalau ye buddhirūpiṇaḥ ..
śatasahasrārbudaṃ ca liṃgaṃ tatraiva tiṣṭhati .. 7 ..
17.6.d:
यत्र वै यादवाः सिद्धाः कलौ ये बुद्धिरूपिणः ..
शतसहस्रार्बुदं च लिंगं तत्रैव तिष्ठति .. 7 ..
17.6.m: Where the Yādavas indeed achieved perfection, who in the Kali age have the form of intellect; / and right there stands a hundred thousand and an arbuda of liṅgas. // 7

17.6.s:
gajeṃdrasya padaṃ tatra tatraiva rasakūpikāḥ ..
sapta kuṇḍāni tatraiva raivate parvatottame .. 8 ..
17.6.d:
गजेंद्रस्य पदं तत्र तत्रैव रसकूपिकाः ..
सप्त कुण्डानि तत्रैव रैवते पर्वतोत्तमे .. 8 ..
17.6.m: The footprint of the lord of elephants is there, and right there are small wells of elixir; / right there are seven pools on Raivata, the best of mountains. // 8

17.6.s:
aṃbikā ca sthitā devī pradyumnaḥ sāṃba eva ca ..
liṃgākāre parvate tu tatra tīrthāni koṭiśaḥ .. 9 ..
17.6.d:
अंबिका च स्थिता देवी प्रद्युम्नः सांब एव च ..
लिंगाकारे पर्वते तु तत्र तीर्थानि कोटिशः .. 9 ..
17.6.m: And the goddess Ambikā resides [there], along with Pradyumna and Sāmba; / upon the mountain shaped like a liṅga, there are crores of sacred fords. // 9

17.6.s:
mṛgīkuṃḍaṃ ca tatraiva kālameghastathaiva ca ..
kṣetrapālasvarūpeṇa mahodadhi svayaṃ sthitaḥ ..
dāmodaraśca tatraiva bhavo brahmāḍanāyakaḥ .. 7.2.6.10 .. ..
17.6.d:
मृगीकुंडं च तत्रैव कालमेघस्तथैव च ..
क्षेत्रपालस्वरूपेण महोदधि स्वयं स्थितः ..
दामोदरश्च तत्रैव भवो ब्रह्माडनायकः .. 7.2.6.10 .. ..
17.6.m: Mṛgīkuṇḍa is right there, and likewise Kālamegha; / the great ocean itself stands there in the form of the guardian of the sacred field, / and Dāmodara is right there, as well as Bhava, the master of the cosmic egg. // 10

17.6.s:
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
śrutāni tava tīrthāni deveśa vadatastava ..
gaṃgā sarasvatī puṇyā yamunā ca mahānadī .. 11 ..
17.6.d:
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
श्रुतानि तव तीर्थानि देवेश वदतस्तव ..
गंगा सरस्वती पुण्या यमुना च महानदी .. 11 ..
17.6.m: Pārvatī said: / Your sacred fords have been heard, O lord of the gods, as spoken by you: / the holy Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, and the great river Yamunā; // 11

17.6.s:
godāvarī gomatī ca nadī tāpī ca narmadā ..
sarayūḥ svarṇarekhā ca tamasā pāpanāśinī .. 12 ..
17.6.d:
गोदावरी गोमती च नदी तापी च नर्मदा ..
सरयूः स्वर्णरेखा च तमसा पापनाशिनी .. 12 ..
17.6.m: the Godāvarī, the Gomatī, and the river Tāpī, and the Narmadā; / the Sarayū, the Svarṇarekhā, and the sin-destroying Tamasā. // 12

17.6.s:
nadyaḥ samudrasaṃyogāḥ sarvāḥ puṇyāḥ śrutā mayā ..
mokṣāraṇyāni divyāni. divyakṣetrāṇi yāni ca .. 13 ..
17.6.d:
नद्यः समुद्रसंयोगाः सर्वाः पुण्याः श्रुता मया ..
मोक्षारण्यानि दिव्यानि. दिव्यक्षेत्राणि यानि च .. 13 ..
17.6.m: All the holy rivers that meet the sea have been heard by me, / as well as the divine forests of liberation and the divine sacred fields; // 13

17.6.s:
nagaryo muktidāyinyastāḥ śrutāstvatprasādataḥ ..
brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ sūryeṃduvaruṇasya ca .. 14 ..
17.6.d:
नगर्यो मुक्तिदायिन्यस्ताः श्रुतास्त्वत्प्रसादतः ..
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादीनां सूर्येंदुवरुणस्य च .. 14 ..
17.6.m: those cities that grant liberation have been heard through your grace, / [sacred to] Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others, and to the Sun, Moon, and Varuṇa. // 14

17.6.s:
devatānā mṛṣīṇāṃ ca saṃti sthānānyanekaśaḥ ..
paraṃ deva tvayā puṇyaṃ prabhāsaṃ kathitaṃ mama .. 15 ..
17.6.d:
देवताना मृषीणां च संति स्थानान्यनेकशः ..
परं देव त्वया पुण्यं प्रभासं कथितं मम .. 15 ..
17.6.m: There are many places of the deities and the seers. / But, O Lord, you have described to me the holy Prabhāsa. 15

17.6.s:
tasmādyaccādhikaṃ proktaṃ kṣetraṃ vastrāpathaṃ tvayā ..
śṛṇvaṃtyā ca mayā pūrvaṃ na pṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadā .. 16 ..
17.6.d:
तस्माद्यच्चाधिकं प्रोक्तं क्षेत्रं वस्त्रापथं त्वया ..
शृण्वंत्या च मया पूर्वं न पृष्टं कारणं तदा .. 16 ..
17.6.m: And greater than that you mentioned the sacred field Vastrāpatha. / As I listened earlier, I did not ask the reason then. 16

17.6.s:
idānīṃ ca śrutaṃ sarvaṃ svasthāhaṃ kāraṇaṃ vada ..
prabhāvaṃ prathamaṃ brūhi kṣetrasya ca bhavasya ca .. 17 ..
17.6.d:
इदानीं च श्रुतं सर्वं स्वस्थाहं कारणं वद ..
प्रभावं प्रथमं ब्रूहि क्षेत्रस्य च भवस्य च .. 17 ..
17.6.m: Now that I have heard everything and am composed, tell the reason. / First speak of the power of the sacred field and of Bhava. 17

17.6.s:
kasmindeśe ca tattīrthaṃ śivaḥ kenātra saṃsthitaḥ ..
svayaṃbhūrbhagavānrudraḥ kathaṃ tatra sthitaḥ svayam ..
prabho me mahadāścaryaṃ vartate tadvadādhunā .. 18 ..
17.6.d:
कस्मिन्देशे च तत्तीर्थं शिवः केनात्र संस्थितः ..
स्वयंभूर्भगवान्रुद्रः कथं तत्र स्थितः स्वयम् ..
प्रभो मे महदाश्चर्यं वर्तते तद्वदाधुना .. 18 ..
17.6.m: In what region is that sacred ford, and by whom was Śiva established there? / How did the lord, self-manifest Rudra, stay there himself? / O Lord, it is a great wonder to me; tell it now. 18

17.6.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
vastrāpathasya kṣetrasya prabhāvaṃ prathamaṃ śṛṇu ..
paścādbhavasya māhātmyaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ ca varānane .. 19 ..
17.6.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
वस्त्रापथस्य क्षेत्रस्य प्रभावं प्रथमं शृणु ..
पश्चाद्भवस्य माहात्म्यं शृणु त्वं च वरानने .. 19 ..
17.6.m: Īśvara said: / First hear of the power of the sacred field Vastrāpatha. / Then hear the māhātmya of Bhava, O fair-faced lady. 19

17.6.s:
kānyakubje mahākṣetre rājā bhojeti viśrutaḥ ..
purā puṇyayuge dharmyaḥ prajā dharmeṇa śāsati .. 7.2.6.20 ..
17.6.d:
कान्यकुब्जे महाक्षेत्रे राजा भोजेति विश्रुतः ..
पुरा पुण्ययुगे धर्म्यः प्रजा धर्मेण शासति .. 7.2.6.20 ..
17.6.m: In the great sacred field of Kānyakubja there was a king famed as Bhoja. / Formerly, in the holy age, righteous, he ruled his subjects with righteousness. 20

17.6.s:
viśālākṣo dīrghabāhurvidvānvāggmī priyaṃvadaḥ ..
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇo bahvāścaryavilokakaḥ .. 21 ..
17.6.d:
विशालाक्षो दीर्घबाहुर्विद्वान्वाग्ग्मी प्रियंवदः ..
सर्वलक्षणसंपूर्णो बह्वाश्चर्यविलोककः .. 21 ..
17.6.m: He had large eyes and long arms; he was learned, eloquent, and pleasant-spoken, / endowed with all auspicious marks, an observer of many marvels. 21

17.6.s:
vanātkadācidabhyetya vanapālobravīdidam ..
āścaryaṃ bhramatā deva vane dṛṣṭaṃ mayādhunā .. 22 ..
17.6.d:
वनात्कदाचिदभ्येत्य वनपालोब्रवीदिदम् ..
आश्चर्यं भ्रमता देव वने दृष्टं मयाधुना .. 22 ..
17.6.m: Once, a forest keeper came from the woods and said this: / 'A wonder, O King, has now been seen by me wandering in the forest! 22

17.6.s:
girau viṣamabhūbhāge vahuvṛkṣasamākule ..
mṛgayūthagatā nārī mayā dṛṣṭā mṛgānanā .. 23 ..
17.6.d:
गिरौ विषमभूभागे वहुवृक्षसमाकुले ..
मृगयूथगता नारी मया दृष्टा मृगानना .. 23 ..
17.6.m: On a mountain, in rugged terrain dense with many trees, / I saw a woman amidst a herd of deer, with the face of a deer. 23

17.6.s:
mṛgavatplavate bālā sadā tatraiva dṛśyate ..
iti śrutvā vaco rājā tuṣṭastasmai dhanaṃ dadau .. 24 ..
17.6.d:
मृगवत्प्लवते बाला सदा तत्रैव दृश्यते ..
इति श्रुत्वा वचो राजा तुष्टस्तस्मै धनं ददौ .. 24 ..
17.6.m: The maiden leaps like a deer, and she is always seen right there.' / Hearing these words, the pleased king gave him wealth, 24

17.6.s:
caturaṃ turagaṃ divyaṃ vāsasī svarṇabhūṣaṇam..
idānīmeva yāsyāmi senādhyakṣa tvayā saha ..25..
17.6.d:
चतुरं तुरगं दिव्यं वाससी स्वर्णभूषणम्..
इदानीमेव यास्यामि सेनाध्यक्ष त्वया सह ..25..
17.6.m: a swift, splendid horse, garments, and gold ornament[s]: / 'I will go right now, commander of the army, along with you! 25

17.6.s:
aśvānāṃ daśasāhasraṃ vāgurāṇāṃ tvanekadhā ..
pattayo yāṃtu sarvatra veṣṭayaṃtu giriṃvaram ..26..
17.6.d:
अश्वानां दशसाहस्रं वागुराणां त्वनेकधा ..
पत्तयो यांतु सर्वत्र वेष्टयंतु गिरिंवरम् ..26..
17.6.m: Let ten thousand horses and snares of many kinds, / let foot-soldiers go everywhere and encircle the excellent mountain. 26

17.6.s:
na haṃtavyo mṛgaḥ kaścidrakṣaṇīyā hi sā mṛgī ..
strīveṣadhāriṇī nārī mṛgī bhavati bhūtale ..27..
17.6.d:
न हंतव्यो मृगः कश्चिद्रक्षणीया हि सा मृगी ..
स्त्रीवेषधारिणी नारी मृगी भवति भूतले ..27..
17.6.m: No deer must be killed, but that doe must indeed be protected. / A woman wearing a woman's dress is a doe upon the earth! 27

17.6.s:
kva yāsyati varākī sā madbalaiḥ paripīḍitā ..
śastrāstravarjitaṃ sainyaṃ vanapālapadānugam ..28..
17.6.d:
क्व यास्यति वराकी सा मद्बलैः परिपीडिता ..
शस्त्रास्त्रवर्जितं सैन्यं वनपालपदानुगम् ..28..
17.6.m: Where will that wretched creature go when hemmed in by my forces?' / The army, free of weapons and missiles, followed in the footsteps of the forest keeper. 28

17.6.s:
ahorātreṇa saṃprāptaṃ bahuvyādhajanāgrataḥ ..
aśvādhirūḍho balavānbhojarājo yayau svayam .. 29 ..
17.6.d:
अहोरात्रेण संप्राप्तं बहुव्याधजनाग्रतः ..
अश्वाधिरूढो बलवान्भोजराजो ययौ स्वयम् .. 29 ..
17.6.m: In a day and a night it arrived, with many hunters leading the way. / Mounted on horseback, the mighty King Bhoja went himself. 29

17.6.s:
niḥśabdapadasañcāraḥ saṃjñāsaṃketabhāṣakaḥ ..
giriṃ saṃveṣṭayāmāsa vāgurābhiḥ svayaṃ nṛpaḥ .. 7.2.6.30 ..
17.6.d:
निःशब्दपदसञ्चारः संज्ञासंकेतभाषकः ..
गिरिं संवेष्टयामास वागुराभिः स्वयं नृपः .. 7.2.6.30 ..
17.6.m: Moving with noiseless steps, communicating by signs and gestures, / the king himself encircled the mountain with snares. 30

17.6.s:
vanapālena sahito mṛgayūthaṃ dadarśa saḥ ..
sā mṛgī mṛgamadhyasthā nārīdehā mukhe mṛgī ..
mṛgavacceṣṭate bālā dhāvate ca mṛgaiḥ saha .. 31 ..
17.6.d:
वनपालेन सहितो मृगयूथं ददर्श सः ..
सा मृगी मृगमध्यस्था नारीदेहा मुखे मृगी ..
मृगवच्चेष्टते बाला धावते च मृगैः सह .. 31 ..
17.6.m: Together with the forest keeper he saw the herd of deer. / That doe stood in the midst of the deer, with a woman's body and a doe's face. / The maiden acted like a deer and ran along with the deer. 31

17.6.s:
aśvagaṃdhānsamāghrāya santrastā mṛgayūthapāḥ ..
kṣubdhā bhrāntāḥ kṣaṇe tasminsarve yāṃti diśo daśa .. 32 ..
17.6.d:
अश्वगंधान्समाघ्राय सन्त्रस्ता मृगयूथपाः ..
क्षुब्धा भ्रान्ताः क्षणे तस्मिन्सर्वे यांति दिशो दश .. 32 ..
17.6.m: Sniffing the scent of the horses, terrified, the leaders of the deer herd, / agitated and wandering in that moment, all scattered in the ten directions. 32

17.6.s:
mṛgavaktrā tu yā nārī mṛgaiḥ katipayaiḥ saha ..
plavamānā nipatitā vāgurāyāṃ vicetanā .. 33 ..
17.6.d:
मृगवक्त्रा तु या नारी मृगैः कतिपयैः सह ..
प्लवमाना निपतिता वागुरायां विचेतना .. 33 ..
17.6.m: That woman with a deer's face, however, along with a few deer, / as she leapt, fell unconscious into the snare. 33

17.6.s:
balādhyakṣeṇa vidhṛtā mṛgaiḥ saha śanairnṛpaḥ ..
dadarśa mahadāścaryaṃ bhojarājo janairvṛtaḥ .. 34 ..
17.6.d:
बलाध्यक्षेण विधृता मृगैः सह शनैर्नृपः ..
ददर्श महदाश्चर्यं भोजराजो जनैर्वृतः .. 34 ..
17.6.m: She was held by the army commander along with the deer, and gently the king, / King Bhoja, surrounded by his men, saw this great wonder. 34

17.6.s:
tataḥ kolāhalo jātaḥ paramānaṃdinisvanaḥ ..
mṛgaiḥ saha samāninye kānyakubjaṃ mṛgīṃ nṛpaḥ .. 35 ..
17.6.d:
ततः कोलाहलो जातः परमानंदिनिस्वनः ..
मृगैः सह समानिन्ये कान्यकुब्जं मृगीं नृपः .. 35 ..
17.6.m: Then an uproar arose, a sound of supreme joy. / Along with the deer, the king brought the doe to Kānyakubja. 35

17.6.s:
divyavastrasamācchannā divyābharaṇabhūṣitā ..
narayānasthitā nārī praviveśa mṛgairvṛtā .. 36 ..
17.6.d:
दिव्यवस्त्रसमाच्छन्ना दिव्याभरणभूषिता ..
नरयानस्थिता नारी प्रविवेश मृगैर्वृता .. 36 ..
17.6.m: Covered in splendid garments and adorned with celestial ornaments, / seated in a palanquin, the woman entered, surrounded by the deer. 36

17.6.s:
vāditrairbrahmaghoṣaiśca nīyate nṛpamaṃdiram ..
janairjānapadairmārge dṛśyate nṛpamandire .. 37 ..
17.6.d:
वादित्रैर्ब्रह्मघोषैश्च नीयते नृपमंदिरम् ..
जनैर्जानपदैर्मार्गे दृश्यते नृपमन्दिरे .. 37 ..
17.6.m: Accompanied by musical instruments and the chanting of the Vedas, she was brought to the king's palace. / She was watched along the road by the countrymen, and in the king's palace 37

17.6.s:
nīyamānā nāgaraiśca mahadāścaryabhāṣakaiḥ ..
puṇye muhūrtte saṃprāpte sā mṛgī nṛpamandiram .. 38 ..
17.6.d:
नीयमाना नागरैश्च महदाश्चर्यभाषकैः ..
पुण्ये मुहूर्त्ते संप्राप्ते सा मृगी नृपमन्दिरम् .. 38 ..
17.6.m: as she was being brought by the citizens who spoke of this great wonder. / When an auspicious hour arrived, that doe [entered] the king's palace. 38

17.6.s:
pratīhāreṇa rājendra vacasā vārito janaḥ ..
gataḥ senāpatiḥ sainyaṃ gṛhītvā svaniketanam .. 39 ..
17.6.d:
प्रतीहारेण राजेन्द्र वचसा वारितो जनः ..
गतः सेनापतिः सैन्यं गृहीत्वा स्वनिकेतनम् .. 39 ..
17.6.m: By the doorkeeper, O king of kings, the crowd was kept back by word. / The general, taking his army, went to his own abode. 39

17.6.s:
rājāpi svagṛhaṃ prāpya snātvā saṃpūjya devatāḥ ..
tāṃ mṛgīṃ snāpayāmāsa divyagandhānulepanām.. 7.2.6.40 ..
17.6.d:
राजापि स्वगृहं प्राप्य स्नात्वा संपूज्य देवताः ..
तां मृगीं स्नापयामास दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनाम्.. 7.2.6.40 ..
17.6.m: The king too, having reached his house, bathed, and worshipped the deities, / had that doe bathed and anointed with divine fragrances. 40

17.6.s:
kuṅkumena viliptāṃgīṃ divyavastrāvaguṃṭhitām ..
yathocitaṃ yathāsthānaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitām .. 41 ..
17.6.d:
कुङ्कुमेन विलिप्तांगीं दिव्यवस्त्रावगुंठिताम् ..
यथोचितं यथास्थानं दिव्याभरणभूषिताम् .. 41 ..
17.6.m: Her limbs were smeared with saffron, she was veiled in splendid garments, / and adorned with heavenly ornaments appropriately and in their proper places. 41

17.6.s:
ekāṃte nirjane rājā babhāṣe cārulocanām ..
kā tvaṃ kasya sutā kena kāraṇena mṛgaiḥ saha .. 42 ..
17.6.d:
एकांते निर्जने राजा बभाषे चारुलोचनाम् ..
का त्वं कस्य सुता केन कारणेन मृगैः सह .. 42 ..
17.6.m: In private, in a secluded spot, the king spoke to the fair-eyed one: / 'Who are you, whose daughter, and for what reason are you with deer? 42

17.6.s:
strīṇāṃ śarīraṃ te kasmānmṛgīṇāṃ vadanaṃ kutaḥ ..
iti sarvaṃ samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 43 ..
17.6.d:
स्त्रीणां शरीरं ते कस्मान्मृगीणां वदनं कुतः ..
इति सर्वं समाचक्ष्व परं कौतूहलं हि मे .. 43 ..
17.6.m: Why do you have the body of a woman, and whence the face of a doe? / Explain all this to me, for my curiosity is immense.' 43

17.6.s:
evaṃ sā procyamānāpi na babhāṣe kathaṃcana ..
mūkavanna vijānāti na ca bhuṃkte sulocanā .. 44 ..
17.6.d:
एवं सा प्रोच्यमानापि न बभाषे कथंचन ..
मूकवन्न विजानाति न च भुंक्ते सुलोचना .. 44 ..
17.6.m: Even though addressed in this way, she did not speak at all. / Like a mute she understood nothing, nor did the fair-eyed one eat. 44

17.6.s:
na bhuṃkte pṛthivīpālo na rājyaṃ bahu manyate ..
na dārairvidyate kāryaṃ nāśvairna ca gajai rathaiḥ .. 45 ..
17.6.d:
न भुंक्ते पृथिवीपालो न राज्यं बहु मन्यते ..
न दारैर्विद्यते कार्यं नाश्वैर्न च गजै रथैः .. 45 ..
17.6.m: The ruler of the earth did not eat, nor did he value his kingdom greatly; / he had no concern for his wives, nor for his horses, elephants, or chariots. 45

17.6.s:
tadeva rājyaṃ te dārāste gajāstaddhanaṃ bahu ..
pramadāmadasaṃraktaṃ yatra saṃkrīḍate manaḥ .. 46 ..
17.6.d:
तदेव राज्यं ते दारास्ते गजास्तद्धनं बहु ..
प्रमदामदसंरक्तं यत्र संक्रीडते मनः .. 46 ..
17.6.m: Kingdom, wives, elephants, and great wealth are truly only that / in which the mind, impassioned with passion for a woman, takes delight. 46

17.6.s:
āhūyāha pratīhāraṃ tayā saṃmohito nṛpaḥ ..
purodhasaṃ guruṃ viprānācāryāñchīghramānaya .. 47 ..
17.6.d:
आहूयाह प्रतीहारं तया संमोहितो नृपः ..
पुरोधसं गुरुं विप्रानाचार्याञ्छीघ्रमानय .. 47 ..
17.6.m: Bewitched by her, the king summoned the doorkeeper and said: / 'Quickly bring the chaplain, the preceptor, the brahmins, and the teachers, 47

17.6.s:
daivajñānatha mantrajñānbhiṣajastāṃtrikāṃstathā ..
iti sannodito rājñā pratīhāro yayau svayam .. 48 ..
17.6.d:
दैवज्ञानथ मन्त्रज्ञान्भिषजस्तांत्रिकांस्तथा ..
इति सन्नोदितो राज्ञा प्रतीहारो ययौ स्वयम् .. 48 ..
17.6.m: as well as astrologers, knowers of mantras, physicians, and tantric practitioners.' / Urged thus by the king, the doorkeeper went himself. 48

17.6.s:
ājagāma sa vegena samānīya dvijottamān..
rājñe vijñāpayāmāsa deva viprāḥ samāgatāḥ .. 49 ..
17.6.d:
आजगाम स वेगेन समानीय द्विजोत्तमान्..
राज्ञे विज्ञापयामास देव विप्राः समागताः .. 49 ..
17.6.m: He came swiftly, bringing the best of brahmins, / and announced to the king: 'O King, the brahmins have arrived.' 49

17.6.s:
praveśaya guruṃ dvāḥsthaṃ saṃprāptānmaddhite ratān ..
iti sannodito rājñā tathā cakre sa buddhimān.. 7.2.6.50 ..
17.6.d:
प्रवेशय गुरुं द्वाःस्थं संप्राप्तान्मद्धिते रतान् ..
इति सन्नोदितो राज्ञा तथा चक्रे स बुद्धिमान्.. 7.2.6.50 ..
17.6.m: 'Usher in the preceptor, the doorkeeper, and those arrived who are devoted to my welfare.' / Urged thus by the king, the intelligent man did so. 50

17.6.s:
abhyutthāya nṛpaḥ pūrvaṃ namaskṛtya prapūjya ca ..
āsaneṣūpaviṣṭāṃstānbabhāṣe kāryatatparaḥ .. 51 ..
17.6.d:
अभ्युत्थाय नृपः पूर्वं नमस्कृत्य प्रपूज्य च ..
आसनेषूपविष्टांस्तान्बभाषे कार्यतत्परः .. 51 ..
17.6.m: The king, having first risen, bowed, and worshipped them, / spoke to them as they sat upon their seats, intent on his task: 51

17.6.s:
idamāścaryamevaikaṃ kathaṃ śakyaṃ niveditum ..
jānīta hi svayaṃ sarve lokataḥ śāstrato'pi vā .. 52 ..
17.6.d:
इदमाश्चर्यमेवैकं कथं शक्यं निवेदितुम् ..
जानीत हि स्वयं सर्वे लोकतः शास्त्रतोऽपि वा .. 52 ..
17.6.m: 'How can this singular marvel be explained? / Indeed, know it yourselves, through the world or from the scriptures: 52

17.6.s:
kathameṣā samutpannā kasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam ..
asyāṃ kena prakāreṇa vacanaṃ mānuṣaṃ bhavet .. 53 ..
17.6.d:
कथमेषा समुत्पन्ना कस्येदं कर्मणः फलम् ..
अस्यां केन प्रकारेण वचनं मानुषं भवेत् .. 53 ..
17.6.m: How was she born? The fruit of what deed is this? / In what way could human speech arise in her? 53

17.6.s:
svayaṃ manuṣyavadanā kathameṣā bhaviṣyati ..
sāvadhānairdvijairbhūyaḥ sarvaṃ saṃcintya cocyatām .. 54 ..
17.6.d:
स्वयं मनुष्यवदना कथमेषा भविष्यति ..
सावधानैर्द्विजैर्भूयः सर्वं संचिन्त्य चोच्यताम् .. 54 ..
17.6.m: How will she herself come to have a human face? / Let the brahmins be attentive, reflect on everything, and tell me.' 54

17.6.s:
.. viprā ūcuḥ .. ..
deva sārasvato nāma kurukṣetre dvijottamaḥ ..
ūrddhvaretāḥ sarasvatyāṃ tapastepe jitendriyaḥ .. 55 ..
17.6.d:
.. विप्रा ऊचुः .. ..
देव सारस्वतो नाम कुरुक्षेत्रे द्विजोत्तमः ..
ऊर्द्ध्वरेताः सरस्वत्यां तपस्तेपे जितेन्द्रियः .. 55 ..
17.6.m: The brahmins said: / 'O King, an excellent brahmin named Sārasvata in Kurukṣetra, / of upward-drawn seed, practiced austerity on the Sarasvatī, his senses conquered. 55

17.6.s:
kathayiṣyati sarvaṃ te tenādiṣṭā mṛgī svayam ..
iti śrutvā vaco rājā yayau sārasvataṃ dvijam .. 56 ..
17.6.d:
कथयिष्यति सर्वं ते तेनादिष्टा मृगी स्वयम् ..
इति श्रुत्वा वचो राजा ययौ सारस्वतं द्विजम् .. 56 ..
17.6.m: Instructed by him, the doe herself will tell you everything.' / Hearing their words, the king went to the brahmin Sārasvata. 56

17.6.s:
sarasvatījale snātaṃ prabhāse dhyānatatparam ..
dṛṣṭvā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sāṣṭāṃgaṃ taṃ praṇamya ca ..
upaviṣṭo nṛpo bhūmau prāṃjaliḥ sañjitendriyaḥ .. 57 ..
17.6.d:
सरस्वतीजले स्नातं प्रभासे ध्यानतत्परम् ..
दृष्ट्वा प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य साष्टांगं तं प्रणम्य च ..
उपविष्टो नृपो भूमौ प्रांजलिः सञ्जितेन्द्रियः .. 57 ..
17.6.m: Having seen him at Prabhāsa, bathed in the waters of the Sarasvatī and absorbed in meditation, circumambulating him clockwise and bowing down to him with all eight limbs, / the king sat upon the earth with folded hands, his senses fully restrained.

17.6.s:
manuṣyapadasaṃcāraṃ śrutvā jñātvā ca kāraṇam ..
sārasvato babhāṣe'tha taṃ nṛpaṃ bhaktitatparam .. 58 ..
17.6.d:
मनुष्यपदसंचारं श्रुत्वा ज्ञात्वा च कारणम् ..
सारस्वतो बभाषेऽथ तं नृपं भक्तितत्परम् .. 58 ..
17.6.m: Hearing the sound of human footsteps and understanding the reason, / the Sarasvata then spoke to that king who was intent upon devotion.

17.6.s:
.. sārasvata uvāca .. ..
bhojarāja śubhaṃ testu jñātaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ mayā ..
mṛgānanā tvayā nārī samānītā vanātkila .. 59 ..
17.6.d:
.. सारस्वत उवाच .. ..
भोजराज शुभं तेस्तु ज्ञातं तत्कारणं मया ..
मृगानना त्वया नारी समानीता वनात्किल .. 59 ..
17.6.m: The Sarasvata said: / 'O King of Bhoja, may it be well with you! That matter is known to me: / that a deer-faced woman was brought by you from the forest indeed.

17.6.s:
mahadāścaryamevaitattava cetasi varttate ..
ādiṣṭā tu mayā bālā sarvaṃ te kathayiṣyati .. 7.2.6.60 ..
17.6.d:
महदाश्चर्यमेवैतत्तव चेतसि वर्त्तते ..
आदिष्टा तु मया बाला सर्वं ते कथयिष्यति .. 7.2.6.60 ..
17.6.m: This great wonder remains in your heart. / Instructed by me, the young woman will tell you everything.

17.6.s:
jānāmyahaṃ mahārāja caritraṃ janma yādṛśam ..
āścaryaṃ saṃbhavelloke kathyamānaṃ tayā svayam .. 61 ..
17.6.d:
जानाम्यहं महाराज चरित्रं जन्म यादृशम् ..
आश्चर्यं संभवेल्लोके कथ्यमानं तया स्वयम् .. 61 ..
17.6.m: I know, O great king, what her conduct and birth were like. / It will be a wonder in the world when told by her own mouth.'

17.6.s:
ityādiśya gato vegādrathenādityavarcasā ..
ahorātradvayenaiva saṃprāpto nṛpa mandiram .. 62 ..
17.6.d:
इत्यादिश्य गतो वेगाद्रथेनादित्यवर्चसा ..
अहोरात्रद्वयेनैव संप्राप्तो नृप मन्दिरम् .. 62 ..
17.6.m: Having thus instructed him, he went swiftly in a chariot bright as the sun; / in just two days and nights he reached the king's palace.

17.6.s:
praviśya ca mṛgīṃ dṛṣṭvā yatrāste mṛgalocanā ..
tayā sārasvato jñāto dharmajñaḥ sarvaviddvijaḥ .. 63 ..
17.6.d:
प्रविश्य च मृगीं दृष्ट्वा यत्रास्ते मृगलोचना ..
तया सारस्वतो ज्ञातो धर्मज्ञः सर्वविद्द्विजः .. 63 ..
17.6.m: Having entered and seen the doe-woman where the fawn-eyed one was staying, / she recognized the Sarasvata, the brahmin who knew dharma and was all-knowing.

17.6.s:
.. mṛgyuvāca .. ..
eṣa sarvaṃ hi jānāti kāraṇaṃ yacca yādṛśam ..
varttamānaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca bhūtaṃ yadbhuvanatraye .. 64 ..
17.6.d:
.. मृग्युवाच .. ..
एष सर्वं हि जानाति कारणं यच्च यादृशम् ..
वर्त्तमानं भविष्यं च भूतं यद्भुवनत्रये .. 64 ..
17.6.m: The doe said: / 'He indeed knows everything: the reason, of whatever kind it may be, / and whatever is present, future, and past in the three worlds.

17.6.s:
etena maraṇaṃ jñātaṃ madīyaṃ pūrvajanmani ..
vastrāpathe mahākṣetre tapastaptaṃ bhavālaye .. 65 ..
17.6.d:
एतेन मरणं ज्ञातं मदीयं पूर्वजन्मनि ..
वस्त्रापथे महाक्षेत्रे तपस्तप्तं भवालये .. 65 ..
17.6.m: By him my death in my previous birth is known. / Austerity was performed [by him] in the great sacred field of Vastrāpatha, in the abode of Bhava.

17.6.s:
vidhūya kaluṣaṃ sarvaṃ jñānamutpādya yatnataḥ ..
jarāmaraṇanirmuktaḥ pratyakṣaṃ dṛṣṭavānbhavam .. 66 ..
17.6.d:
विधूय कलुषं सर्वं ज्ञानमुत्पाद्य यत्नतः ..
जरामरणनिर्मुक्तः प्रत्यक्षं दृष्टवान्भवम् .. 66 ..
17.6.m: Having shaken off all defilement and generated knowledge with effort, / freed from old age and death, he saw Bhava face to face.

17.6.s:
asya tuṣṭo bhavo devo jñātaṃ tīrthasya kāraṇam ..
ādiṣṭayā mayā vācyaṃ bhavejjanmani kāraṇam .. 67 ..
17.6.d:
अस्य तुष्टो भवो देवो ज्ञातं तीर्थस्य कारणम् ..
आदिष्टया मया वाच्यं भवेज्जन्मनि कारणम् .. 67 ..
17.6.m: Lord Bhava was pleased with him; the cause of the sacred ford was known [by him]. / Instructed [by him], I must declare the cause that pertains to my birth.'

17.6.s:
iti cintāparā yāvattāvadvipraḥ samāgataḥ ..
tasmai praṇāmaparamā mūrcchitā nipapāta sā .. 68 ..
17.6.d:
इति चिन्तापरा यावत्तावद्विप्रः समागतः ..
तस्मै प्रणामपरमा मूर्च्छिता निपपात सा .. 68 ..
17.6.m: While she was thus absorbed in thought, the brahmin arrived. / Wholly intent upon bowing down to him, she fell into a faint.

17.6.s:
atha sārasvato jñānājjñātavānkāraṇaṃ ca tat ..
ānayantu dvijā vegātkalaśaṃ toyasaṃbhṛtam .. .. 69 ..
17.6.d:
अथ सारस्वतो ज्ञानाज्ज्ञातवान्कारणं च तत् ..
आनयन्तु द्विजा वेगात्कलशं तोयसंभृतम् .. .. 69 ..
17.6.m: Then the Sarasvata knew through his knowledge that reason: / 'Let the brahmins swiftly bring a pitcher filled with water,

17.6.s:
savauṃṣadhīḥ pallavāṃśca dūrvāḥ puṣpāṇi cākṣatān..
dhūpaṃ ca caṃdanaṃ caiva gomayaṃ madhusarpiṣī .. 7.2.6.70 ..
17.6.d:
सवौंषधीः पल्लवांश्च दूर्वाः पुष्पाणि चाक्षतान्..
धूपं च चंदनं चैव गोमयं मधुसर्पिषी .. 7.2.6.70 ..
17.6.m: all medicinal herbs, sprouts, dūrvā grass, flowers, unbroken grains, / incense, sandalwood, cow dung, honey, and clarified butter!'

17.6.s:
ityādiṣṭairdvijairvegātsamānītaṃ nṛpājñayā ..
upalipya ca bhūbhāgaṃ svastikaṃ saṃniveśya ca .. 71 ..
17.6.d:
इत्यादिष्टैर्द्विजैर्वेगात्समानीतं नृपाज्ञया ..
उपलिप्य च भूभागं स्वस्तिकं संनिवेश्य च .. 71 ..
17.6.m: Thus commanded, it was swiftly brought by the brahmins at the king's command. / And having smeared the ground with cow dung and placed a svastika design [there],

17.6.s:
tatrāgnikāryaṃ kṛtvā'tha vedānkuṃbhe nidhāya saḥ ..
indraṃ tasmiṃśca vinyasya dikpālāṃśca yathākramam ..
hutvāgniṃ sa caruṃ kṛtvā grahapūjāmakārayat .. 72 ..
17.6.d:
तत्राग्निकार्यं कृत्वाऽथ वेदान्कुंभे निधाय सः ..
इन्द्रं तस्मिंश्च विन्यस्य दिक्पालांश्च यथाक्रमम् ..
हुत्वाग्निं स चरुं कृत्वा ग्रहपूजामकारयत् .. 72 ..
17.6.m: having performed the fire-rite there, and having deposited the Vedas in the water-jar, / and having installed Indra in it and the guardians of the directions in proper order, / having made offerings into the fire and prepared the caru offering, he had worship of the planets performed.

17.6.s:
toyaṃ suvarṇapātrasthaṃ kṛtvā kuṃbhānsvayaṃ guruḥ ..
abhiṣekaṃ tataścakre muhūrte sārvakāmike .. 73 ..
17.6.d:
तोयं सुवर्णपात्रस्थं कृत्वा कुंभान्स्वयं गुरुः ..
अभिषेकं ततश्चक्रे मुहूर्ते सार्वकामिके .. 73 ..
17.6.m: Having placed water into a gold vessel and [brought] the jars himself, the guru / then performed the consecration at an astrologically auspicious hour yielding all desires.

17.6.s:
abhiṣiktā tu sā tena pūtā snānārthavāriṇā ..
