jātā sacetanā bālā sarvaṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā .. 74 ..
17.6.d:
अभिषिक्ता तु सा तेन पूता स्नानार्थवारिणा ..
जाता सचेतना बाला सर्वं पश्यति चक्षुषा .. 74 ..
17.6.m: Consecrated by him and purified with the water for ritual ablution, / the young woman regained consciousness and saw everything with her eyes.

17.6.s:
śṛṇoti sarvaṃ jānāti caritraṃ pūrvajanmanaḥ ..
badarīphalamātraṃ tu puroḍāśaṃ dadau guruḥ .. 75 ..
17.6.d:
शृणोति सर्वं जानाति चरित्रं पूर्वजन्मनः ..
बदरीफलमात्रं तु पुरोडाशं ददौ गुरुः .. 75 ..
17.6.m: She heard everything and knew the deeds of her previous birth. / Then the guru gave her a sacrificial cake merely the size of a jujube fruit.

17.6.s:
tayopabhuktaṃ yatnena tataścakre sa mārjjanam ..
mānuṣe vacane karṇe dadau jñānaṃ gurustataḥ .. 76 ..
17.6.d:
तयोपभुक्तं यत्नेन ततश्चक्रे स मार्ज्जनम् ..
मानुषे वचने कर्णे ददौ ज्ञानं गुरुस्ततः .. 76 ..
17.6.m: It was eaten by her with effort; then he performed the ritual sprinkling. / Then the guru imparted knowledge into her ear in human speech.

17.6.s:
gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā tataḥ sā ca mṛgānanā ..
bhojarājāya sarva ca caritraṃ pūrvajanmanaḥ .. .. 77 ..
17.6.d:
गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा ततः सा च मृगानना ..
भोजराजाय सर्व च चरित्रं पूर्वजन्मनः .. .. 77 ..
17.6.m: Having given the priestly fee to the guru, that deer-faced woman then / [proceeded to tell] the King of Bhoja all the deeds of her previous birth.

17.6.s:
vaktuṃ pracakrame bālyādyadvṛttaṃ pūrvajanmani ..
namaskṛtya guruṃ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇānkṣatriyāṃstathā .. 78 ..
17.6.d:
वक्तुं प्रचक्रमे बाल्याद्यद्वृत्तं पूर्वजन्मनि ..
नमस्कृत्य गुरुं पूर्वं ब्राह्मणान्क्षत्रियांस्तथा .. 78 ..
17.6.m: Having first bowed to the guru, the brahmins, and the kṣatriyas, / she began to tell what had happened from childhood in her previous birth.

17.6.s:
.. mṛgyuvāca .. ..
na viṣādastvayā kāryo rājañcchrutvā mayoditam ..
itastvaṃ saptame sthāne kaliṃgādhipateḥ sutaḥ .. 79 ..
17.6.d:
.. मृग्युवाच .. ..
न विषादस्त्वया कार्यो राजञ्च्छ्रुत्वा मयोदितम् ..
इतस्त्वं सप्तमे स्थाने कलिंगाधिपतेः सुतः .. 79 ..
17.6.m: The doe said: / 'You must not feel grief, O king, having heard what is spoken by me. / In the seventh birth from here, you were the son of the ruler of Kaliṅga.

17.6.s:
mṛte pitari bālastvaṃ svabhiṣiktaḥ svamaṃtribhiḥ ..
ahaṃ hi vaṃgarājasya saṃjātā duhitā kila .. 7.2.6.80 ..
17.6.d:
मृते पितरि बालस्त्वं स्वभिषिक्तः स्वमंत्रिभिः ..
अहं हि वंगराजस्य संजाता दुहिता किल .. 7.2.6.80 ..
17.6.m: When your father died, while still a boy you were well consecrated by your ministers. / I, indeed, was born as the daughter of the king of Vaṅga.

17.6.s:
pariṇītā tvayā deva pitrā dattā svayaṃ nṛpa ..
tvayā'haṃ paṭṭamahiṣī kṛtā yoṣidvarā yataḥ .. 81 ..
17.6.d:
परिणीता त्वया देव पित्रा दत्ता स्वयं नृप ..
त्वयाऽहं पट्टमहिषी कृता योषिद्वरा यतः .. 81 ..
17.6.m: I was wedded by you, O lord, given by my father himself, O king; / by you I was made chief queen, since I was an excellent woman.

17.6.s:
yuvā jātaḥ krameṇaiva hiṃsraḥ krūro babhūva ha ..
na vedaśāstrakuśalo dayādharmavivarjitaḥ .. 82 ..
17.6.d:
युवा जातः क्रमेणैव हिंस्रः क्रूरो बभूव ह ..
न वेदशास्त्रकुशलो दयाधर्मविवर्जितः .. 82 ..
17.6.m: Having become a youth in due course, [you] became violent and cruel indeed, / not skilled in the Vedas and Śāstras, devoid of compassion and dharma,

17.6.s:
lubdho mānī mahākrodhī satyācāra bahiṣkṛtaḥ ..
na devaṃ na guruṃ viprānno jānāti durāśayaḥ .. 83 ..
17.6.d:
लुब्धो मानी महाक्रोधी सत्याचार बहिष्कृतः ..
न देवं न गुरुं विप्रान्नो जानाति दुराशयः .. 83 ..
17.6.m: greedy, arrogant, very wrathful, expelled from truthful conduct. / Malicious, he recognized neither god nor guru nor brahmins.

17.6.s:
viraktā hi prajāstasya brāhmaṇocchedakārakaḥ ..
samāsannairnṛpaistasya deśaḥ sarvo viluṃpitaḥ ..
sainyaṃ sarvaṃ samādāya yuddhāyopajagāma saḥ .. 84 ..
17.6.d:
विरक्ता हि प्रजास्तस्य ब्राह्मणोच्छेदकारकः ..
समासन्नैर्नृपैस्तस्य देशः सर्वो विलुंपितः ..
सैन्यं सर्वं समादाय युद्धायोपजगाम सः .. 84 ..
17.6.m: His subjects were alienated, for he was a destroyer of brahmins. / All his territory was plundered by neighbouring kings; / taking all his army, he went out for battle.

17.6.s:
sahaivāhaṃ gatā deva yuddhaṃ jātaṃ nṛpaiḥ saha ..
hāritaṃ sainikaistasya gatā naṣṭā diśo daśa .. 85 ..
17.6.d:
सहैवाहं गता देव युद्धं जातं नृपैः सह ..
हारितं सैनिकैस्तस्य गता नष्टा दिशो दश .. 85 ..
17.6.m: I went along with you, O lord; a battle took place with the kings. / His soldiers were defeated; they fled and vanished into the ten directions.

17.6.s:
tyaktvā dharmaṃ nijaṃ rājā palāyanaparo'bhavat ..
gacchamānastu nṛpatiḥ śatrubhiḥ paripīḍitaḥ .. 86 ..
17.6.d:
त्यक्त्वा धर्मं निजं राजा पलायनपरोऽभवत् ..
गच्छमानस्तु नृपतिः शत्रुभिः परिपीडितः .. 86 ..
17.6.m: Abandoning his own dharma, the king became intent on flight. / But as the king was fleeing, he was hard-pressed by his enemies.

17.6.s:
tavāsmivādī duṣṭātmā hato lokavirodhakaḥ ..
dehaṃ tasya gṛhītvāgnau praviṣṭāhaṃ nṛpottama .. 87 ..
17.6.d:
तवास्मिवादी दुष्टात्मा हतो लोकविरोधकः ..
देहं तस्य गृहीत्वाग्नौ प्रविष्टाहं नृपोत्तम .. 87 ..
17.6.m: Saying "I am yours!", the wicked-souled one, enemy of the world, was killed. / Taking his body, I entered the fire, O best of kings.

17.6.s:
mṛtasyaivaṃ gatirnāsti narake sa vipacyate ..
mṛtaṃ kāṃtaṃ samādāya bhāryāgnau praviśedyadi .. 88 ..
17.6.d:
मृतस्यैवं गतिर्नास्ति नरके स विपच्यते ..
मृतं कांतं समादाय भार्याग्नौ प्रविशेद्यदि .. 88 ..
17.6.m: For a man who has died in this way there is no good state; he cooks in hell. / If a wife, taking her deceased beloved, enters the fire,

17.6.s:
sā tārayati pāpiṣṭhaṃ yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam ..
iha pāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā paścātsvarge mahīyate .. 89 ..
17.6.d:
सा तारयति पापिष्ठं यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ..
इह पापक्षयं कृत्वा पश्चात्स्वर्गे महीयते .. 89 ..
17.6.m: she delivers the most sinful man until the dissolution of the elements; / having wiped away his sin here, he is subsequently glorified in heaven.

17.6.s:
atastvaṃ brāhmaṇo jāto deśe mālavake nṛpa ..
tasyaiva tatra bhāryāhaṃ saṃbhūtā brāhmaṇī nṛpa .. 7.2.6.90 ..
17.6.d:
अतस्त्वं ब्राह्मणो जातो देशे मालवके नृप ..
तस्यैव तत्र भार्याहं संभूता ब्राह्मणी नृप .. 7.2.6.90 ..
17.6.m: Therefore you were born as a brahmin in the country of Mālava, O king; / and I was born there as that very one's brahmin wife, O king.

17.6.s:
dhanadhānyasamṛddho'bhūttathā jīvadhanādhikaḥ ..
mṛtaḥ pitā mṛtā mātā sa ca bhrātṛvivarjitaḥ .. 91 ..
17.6.d:
धनधान्यसमृद्धोऽभूत्तथा जीवधनाधिकः ..
मृतः पिता मृता माता स च भ्रातृविवर्जितः .. 91 ..
17.6.m: He was rich in wealth and grain, and had abundant cattle. / His father had died, his mother had died, and he was devoid of brothers.

17.6.s:
dhanadhānyasamṛddho'pi lubdho bhramati bhūtale ..
atīva kopano vipro vedapāṭhavivarjitaḥ .. 92 ..
17.6.d:
धनधान्यसमृद्धोऽपि लुब्धो भ्रमति भूतले ..
अतीव कोपनो विप्रो वेदपाठविवर्जितः .. 92 ..
17.6.m: Though rich in wealth and grain, greedy, he wandered upon the earth. / The brahmin was exceedingly wrathful and devoid of Vedic recitation.

17.6.s:
snānasaṃdhyādihīnaśca māyāvī yācate janam ..
bhaktiṃ karomi paramāṃ sa ca krudhyati māṃ prati .. 93 ..
17.6.d:
स्नानसंध्यादिहीनश्च मायावी याचते जनम् ..
भक्तिं करोमि परमां स च क्रुध्यति मां प्रति .. 93 ..
17.6.m: Lacking ritual ablution, the twilight prayers, and the like, deceitful, he begged from people. / I offered supreme devotion, but he was angry with me.

17.6.s:
saṃtānaṃ tasya vai nāsti dhanarakṣāparo hi saḥ ..
na dadāti na cāśnāti na juhoti sa rakṣati .. 94 ..
17.6.d:
संतानं तस्य वै नास्ति धनरक्षापरो हि सः ..
न ददाति न चाश्नाति न जुहोति स रक्षति .. 94 ..
17.6.m: Indeed he had no offspring, for he was intent only on guarding wealth; / he neither gave, nor ate, nor sacrificed into the fire; he [only] hoarded.

17.6.s:
na tarpaṇaṃ tilairvipro vidadhātyatilo bhataḥ ..
kārttike'pi ca saṃprāpte viṣṇupūjāvivarjitaḥ .. 95 ..
17.6.d:
न तर्पणं तिलैर्विप्रो विदधात्यतिलो भतः ..
कार्त्तिकेऽपि च संप्राप्ते विष्णुपूजाविवर्जितः .. 95 ..
17.6.m: Out of excessive greed, the brahmin did not even perform the water-offering with sesame seeds; / even when Kārttika arrived, he was devoid of the worship of Viṣṇu.

17.6.s:
dīpaṃ dadāti no vipro māsamekaṃ nirantaram ..
na bhuṃkte śākapatraṃ sa ekāhāro niraṃtaram .. 96 ..
17.6.d:
दीपं ददाति नो विप्रो मासमेकं निरन्तरम् ..
न भुंक्ते शाकपत्रं स एकाहारो निरंतरम् .. 96 ..
17.6.m: The brahmin did not offer a lamp continuously for one month; / he did not eat vegetable leaves, eating constantly only one meal a day [out of stinginess].

17.6.s:
māse nabhasye saṃprāpte prāpte kṛṣṇe nṛpottama ..
na karoti gṛhe śrāddhaṃ snānatarpaṇavarjitaḥ .. 97 ..
17.6.d:
मासे नभस्ये संप्राप्ते प्राप्ते कृष्णे नृपोत्तम ..
न करोति गृहे श्राद्धं स्नानतर्पणवर्जितः .. 97 ..
17.6.m: When the month of Nabhasya arrived, when its dark fortnight arrived, O best of kings, / he did not perform the ancestral offering in the house, devoid of ritual ablution and libation.

17.6.s:
na jānāti dinaṃ pitryaṃ pakṣamekaṃ nirantaram ..
anyatra bhuṃkte vipro'sau kṣayāhe'pi samāgate .. 98 ..
17.6.d:
न जानाति दिनं पित्र्यं पक्षमेकं निरन्तरम् ..
अन्यत्र भुंक्ते विप्रोऽसौ क्षयाहेऽपि समागते .. 98 ..
17.6.m: He did not observe the day of the ancestors continuously throughout the fortnight; / that brahmin ate elsewhere, even when the anniversary of death had arrived.

17.6.s:
makarasthe'pi saṃkrāṃtau kṛśarānnaṃ dadāti na ..
tilānsuvarṇaṃ tāraṃ vā vastraṃ vā phalameva ca ..
śākapatraṃ sa puṣpaṃ vā na dadāti tatheṃdhanam .. 99 ..
17.6.d:
मकरस्थेऽपि संक्रांतौ कृशरान्नं ददाति न ..
तिलान्सुवर्णं तारं वा वस्त्रं वा फलमेव च ..
शाकपत्रं स पुष्पं वा न ददाति तथेंधनम् .. 99 ..
17.6.m: Even at the solstice when [the sun] enters Capricorn, he gives no boiled rice and sesame, / nor sesame seeds, gold, silver, clothing, or even fruit, / nor leafy greens, flowers, or even firewood.

17.6.s:
gavāṃ gavāhnikaṃ naiva kathaṃ muktirbhaviṣyati ..
na yāti viṣṇuśaraṇaṃ saṃprāpte dakṣiṇāyane .. 7.2.6.100 ..
17.6.d:
गवां गवाह्निकं नैव कथं मुक्तिर्भविष्यति ..
न याति विष्णुशरणं संप्राप्ते दक्षिणायने .. 7.2.6.100 ..
17.6.m: He gives no daily grass to the cows; how could liberation come to be? / When the southern transit of the sun arrives, he does not seek refuge in Viṣṇu.

17.6.s: dhenuṃ dadāti no vipro grahaṇe caṃdrasūryayoḥ .. 101 ..
17.6.d: धेनुं ददाति नो विप्रो ग्रहणे चंद्रसूर्ययोः .. 101 ..
17.6.m: During an eclipse of the moon or the sun, the brahmin gives no milch cow.

17.6.s:
ekāpi dattā supayasvinī sā savastraghaṃṭābharaṇopapannā ..
vatsena yuktā hi dadāti dātre muktiṃ kulasyāsya karoti vṛddhim.. 102 ..
17.6.d:
एकापि दत्ता सुपयस्विनी सा सवस्त्रघंटाभरणोपपन्ना ..
वत्सेन युक्ता हि ददाति दात्रे मुक्तिं कुलस्यास्य करोति वृद्धिम्.. 102 ..
17.6.m: Even a single cow, yielding abundant milk, gifted along with cloth, bells, and ornaments, / and accompanied by her calf, grants liberation to the giver and brings prosperity to his family.

17.6.s:
yāvaṃti romāṇi bhavaṃti tasyāstāvaṃti varṣāṇi mahīyate saḥ ..
brahmālaye siddha gaṇairvṛto'sau saṃtiṣṭhate sūryasamānatejāḥ .. 103 ..
17.6.d:
यावंति रोमाणि भवंति तस्यास्तावंति वर्षाणि महीयते सः ..
ब्रह्मालये सिद्ध गणैर्वृतोऽसौ संतिष्ठते सूर्यसमानतेजाः .. 103 ..
17.6.m: For as many hairs as are upon her, for so many years he is glorified; / surrounded by hosts of siddhas in the abode of Brahmā, he abides, brilliant as the sun.

17.6.s:
devālayaṃ no vidadhāti vāpīṃ kūpaṃ taḍāgaṃ na karoti kuṇḍam ..
puṇyaṃ vivāhaṃ sujanopakāraṃ nāsau satāṃ vā dvijamaṃdiraṃ ca .. 104 ..
17.6.d:
देवालयं नो विदधाति वापीं कूपं तडागं न करोति कुण्डम् ..
पुण्यं विवाहं सुजनोपकारं नासौ सतां वा द्विजमंदिरं च .. 104 ..
17.6.m: He builds no temple of the gods, no stepwell, well, reservoir, or pool; / he performs no meritorious marriage, provides no help to virtuous folk, and builds no dwelling for good men or brahmins.

17.6.s:
dhanaṃ sadā bhūmigataṃ karoti dharmaṃ na jānāti kulasya cāsau ..
ahaṃ hi tasyānugatā bhavāmi kathaṃ hi kāṃtaṃ parivaṃ cayāmi .. 105 ..
17.6.d:
धनं सदा भूमिगतं करोति धर्मं न जानाति कुलस्य चासौ ..
अहं हि तस्यानुगता भवामि कथं हि कांतं परिवं चयामि .. 105 ..
17.6.m: He constantly buries his wealth in the earth and knows no religious duty of his family. / Indeed, I followed him; for how could I deceive my husband?

17.6.s:
evaṃ hi varttamānaḥ sa kāladharmamupeyivān ..
dhanalobhānmayā deva maraṇaṃ parivarjitam ..106..
17.6.d:
एवं हि वर्त्तमानः स कालधर्ममुपेयिवान् ..
धनलोभान्मया देव मरणं परिवर्जितम् ..106..
17.6.m: Living in this way, he met the fate of death. / Out of greed for wealth, O Lord, death was avoided by me [then].

17.6.s:
paśyantyā gotribhiḥ sarvaṃ gṛhītaṃ dhanasaṃcayam ..
kālena mahatā deva mṛtā'haṃ dvijamaṃdire .. 107 ..
17.6.d:
पश्यन्त्या गोत्रिभिः सर्वं गृहीतं धनसंचयम् ..
कालेन महता देव मृताऽहं द्विजमंदिरे .. 107 ..
17.6.m: As I watched, the entire heap of wealth was seized by the kinsmen. / After a long time, O Lord, I died in the brahmin's house.

17.6.s:
śvetasarpaḥ samabhavaddeśe tasminnarottama ..
tatraivāhaṃ brāhmaṇasya saṃjātā tanayā nṛpa .. 108 ..
17.6.d:
श्वेतसर्पः समभवद्देशे तस्मिन्नरोत्तम ..
तत्रैवाहं ब्राह्मणस्य संजाता तनया नृप .. 108 ..
17.6.m: A white snake came into being in that country, O best of men; / and right there I was born as the daughter of a brahmin, O king.

17.6.s:
varṣeṣṭame tu saṃprāpte pariṇītā dvijanmanā ..
tasminneva gṛhe sarpo madīye vasate nṛpa .. 109 ..
17.6.d:
वर्षेष्टमे तु संप्राप्ते परिणीता द्विजन्मना ..
तस्मिन्नेव गृहे सर्पो मदीये वसते नृप .. 109 ..
17.6.m: When my eighth year arrived, I was married to a twice-born man. / That very snake lived in my house, O king.

17.6.s:
bhāryā mameti saṃdaṣṭo rātrau bharttā mahā hinā ..
mṛto'pi brāhmaṇaiḥ sarpo laguḍairvinipātitaḥ .. 7.2.6.110 ..
17.6.d:
भार्या ममेति संदष्टो रात्रौ भर्त्ता महा हिना ..
मृतोऽपि ब्राह्मणैः सर्पो लगुडैर्विनिपातितः .. 7.2.6.110 ..
17.6.m: Thinking, 'She is my wife,' my husband was bitten at night by that great serpent. / Though dead, the snake was struck down with clubs by the brahmins.

17.6.s:
vaidhavyaṃ mama dattvā tu dvijasarpau mṛtāvubhau ..
pitrā mātrā mahāśokaṃ kṛtvā me muṇḍitaṃ śiraḥ .. 111 ..
17.6.d:
वैधव्यं मम दत्त्वा तु द्विजसर्पौ मृतावुभौ ..
पित्रा मात्रा महाशोकं कृत्वा मे मुण्डितं शिरः .. 111 ..
17.6.m: Having granted me widowhood, both the brahmin and the snake died. / My father and mother, grieving greatly, had my head shaved.

17.6.s:
vasānā śvetavastraṃ ca viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇā ..
māsopavāsaniratā yāni tīrthānyanekaśaḥ .. 112 ..
17.6.d:
वसाना श्वेतवस्त्रं च विष्णुभक्तिपरायणा ..
मासोपवासनिरता यानि तीर्थान्यनेकशः .. 112 ..
17.6.m: Wearing white garments and devoted to bhakti towards Viṣṇu, / dedicated to month-long fasts, I visited sacred fords many times.

17.6.s:
sarpastu makaro jāto godāvaryāṃ śivālaye ..
devaṃ bhīmeśvaraṃ draṣṭuṃ gatā'haṃ svajanaiḥ saha .. 113 ..
17.6.d:
सर्पस्तु मकरो जातो गोदावर्यां शिवालये ..
देवं भीमेश्वरं द्रष्टुं गताऽहं स्वजनैः सह .. 113 ..
17.6.m: The snake, however, was born as a crocodile in the Godāvarī at a shrine of Śiva. / I went with my relatives to see the lord Bhīmeśvara.

17.6.s:
yāvatsnātuṃ praviṣṭā'haṃ vṛtā sarvajanairnṛpa ..
makareṇa tadā dṛṣṭā bhāryeyaṃ mama vallabhā ..
gṛhītā makareṇāhaṃ netumaṃtarjale nṛpa .. 114 ..
17.6.d:
यावत्स्नातुं प्रविष्टाऽहं वृता सर्वजनैर्नृप ..
मकरेण तदा दृष्टा भार्येयं मम वल्लभा ..
गृहीता मकरेणाहं नेतुमंतर्जले नृप .. 114 ..
17.6.m: As I stepped in to perform my ritual ablution, surrounded by all the people, O king, / I was seen by the crocodile, who thought, 'This is my beloved wife.' / I was seized by the crocodile to be dragged into the water, O king.

17.6.s:
hāhākāraḥ samabhavajjanaḥ kṣubdhaḥ samaṃtataḥ ..
kuṃtāghātena kenāsau makarastu nipātitaḥ .. 115 ..
17.6.d:
हाहाकारः समभवज्जनः क्षुब्धः समंततः ..
कुंताघातेन केनासौ मकरस्तु निपातितः .. 115 ..
17.6.m: A cry of distress arose, and the people all around were agitated. / By a thrust of a spear by someone, that crocodile was struck down.

17.6.s:
jhaṣavaktraḥ sthitā cāhaṃ mṛtā kṛṣṭā janairbahiḥ ..
agniṃ dattvā jale kṣiptvā bhasma lokā gṛhāngatāḥ .. 116 ..
17.6.d:
झषवक्त्रः स्थिता चाहं मृता कृष्टा जनैर्बहिः ..
अग्निं दत्त्वा जले क्षिप्त्वा भस्म लोका गृहान्गताः .. 116 ..
17.6.m: Held in the mouth of the aquatic beast, dead, I was dragged out by the people. / Having set fire [to the corpse] and cast the ashes into the water, the people went home.

17.6.s:
strīvadhāllubdhvako jāto jhaṣastīrthaprabhāvataḥ ..
mānuṣīṃ yonimāpannastasminneva mahāvane ..117..
17.6.d:
स्त्रीवधाल्लुब्ध्वको जातो झषस्तीर्थप्रभावतः ..
मानुषीं योनिमापन्नस्तस्मिन्नेव महावने ..117..
17.6.m: Because of the slaying of a woman, the aquatic beast became a hunter; by the power of the sacred ford, / he attained a human birth in that very great forest.

17.6.s:
agnerjalācca sarpācca gajātsiṃhādavṛṣādapi ..
jhaṣādvisphoṭakānmṛtyuryeṣāṃ te narake gatāḥ .. 118 ..
17.6.d:
अग्नेर्जलाच्च सर्पाच्च गजात्सिंहादवृषादपि ..
झषाद्विस्फोटकान्मृत्युर्येषां ते नरके गताः .. 118 ..
17.6.m: Those whose death is from fire, from water, from a snake, from an elephant, from a lion, or even from a bull, / from an aquatic beast, or from smallpox—they go to hell.

17.6.s:
ātmahā bhrūṇahā strīhā brahmaghnaḥ kūṭasākṣyadaḥ ..
kanyāvikrayakartā ca mithyā bratadharastu yaḥ .. .. 119 ..
17.6.d:
आत्महा भ्रूणहा स्त्रीहा ब्रह्मघ्नः कूटसाक्ष्यदः ..
कन्याविक्रयकर्ता च मिथ्या ब्रतधरस्तु यः .. .. 119 ..
17.6.m: A suicide, an aborticide, the killer of a woman, the killer of a brahmin, one who bears false witness, / one who sells a maiden, and one who maintains a false vow;

17.6.s:
vikrīṇāti kratuṃ yastu madyapaḥ syāddvijastu yaḥ ..
rājadrohī svarṇacauro brahmavṛttivilopakaḥ .. 7.2.6.120 ..
17.6.d:
विक्रीणाति क्रतुं यस्तु मद्यपः स्याद्द्विजस्तु यः ..
राजद्रोही स्वर्णचौरो ब्रह्मवृत्तिविलोपकः .. 7.2.6.120 ..
17.6.m: one who sells a sacrifice, a twice-born man who drinks intoxicants, / a traitor to the king, a thief of gold, one who destroys the livelihood of a brahmin;

17.6.s:
goghnastu nikṣepaharo grāmasīmāharastu yaḥ ..
sarve te narakaṃ yāṃti yā ca strī pativaṃcakā .. 121 ..
17.6.d:
गोघ्नस्तु निक्षेपहरो ग्रामसीमाहरस्तु यः ..
सर्वे ते नरकं यांति या च स्त्री पतिवंचका .. 121 ..
17.6.m: the killer of a cow, an embezzler of a deposit, and one who steals the boundary of a village— / all of them go to hell, as does a woman who deceives her husband.

17.6.s:
jhaṣamṛtyuprabhāvena jātā krauṃcī vane nṛpa ..
godāvarīvane vyādho bhramate mṛgamārgakaḥ .. 122 ..
17.6.d:
झषमृत्युप्रभावेन जाता क्रौंची वने नृप ..
गोदावरीवने व्याधो भ्रमते मृगमार्गकः .. 122 ..
17.6.m: By the power of dying from an aquatic beast, I was born as a krauñcī bird in the forest, O king. / In the forest of the Godāvarī, the hunter wandered, tracking game.

17.6.s:
vane krauṃcaḥ sakāmo māṃ mudā kāmayitumudyataḥ ..
dṛṣṭāhaṃ bhramatā tena vyādhenākṛṣya kārmukam .. 123 ..
17.6.d:
वने क्रौंचः सकामो मां मुदा कामयितुमुद्यतः ..
दृष्टाहं भ्रमता तेन व्याधेनाकृष्य कार्मुकम् .. 123 ..
17.6.m: In the forest, an impassioned krauñca bird eagerly prepared to mate with me with joy. / As he wandered, that hunter saw me, and drawing his bow,

17.6.s:
hataḥ krauṃco mṛto rāja nnaṣṭā sthānādahaṃ tataḥ ..
godāvarīvane tasminnevaṃrūpaṃ dadarśa tam .. 124 ..
17.6.d:
हतः क्रौंचो मृतो राज न्नष्टा स्थानादहं ततः ..
गोदावरीवने तस्मिन्नेवंरूपं ददर्श तम् .. 124 ..
17.6.m: the krauñca bird was struck and died, O king; then I fled from that place. / In that forest of the Godāvarī, a seer saw him in that condition.

17.6.s:
ṛṣirvyādhaṃ śaśāpātha dṛṣṭvā karma vigarhitam ..
kāmadharmamakurvāṇaṃ priyā saṃbhāṣatatparam ..
krauṃcaṃ tvamavadhīryasmāttasmātsiṃho bhaviṣyasi .. 125 ..
17.6.d:
ऋषिर्व्याधं शशापाथ दृष्ट्वा कर्म विगर्हितम् ..
कामधर्ममकुर्वाणं प्रिया संभाषतत्परम् ..
क्रौंचं त्वमवधीर्यस्मात्तस्मात्सिंहो भविष्यसि .. 125 ..
17.6.m: Seeing that despicable deed, the seer cursed the hunter: / 'Since you killed the krauñca bird when he was not engaged in the act of love, / but was wholly intent on speaking with his beloved, therefore you shall become a lion.'

17.6.s:
ṛṣistena vinītena sthitvā santoṣito nṛpa ..
ṛṣirvadati tasyāgre na me mithyā vaco bhavet .. 126 ..
17.6.d:
ऋषिस्तेन विनीतेन स्थित्वा सन्तोषितो नृप ..
ऋषिर्वदति तस्याग्रे न मे मिथ्या वचो भवेत् .. 126 ..
17.6.m: The seer, being approached humbly by him as he stood there, was appeased, O king. / The seer spoke before him: 'My word cannot be false.

17.6.s:
siṃhasthasya prasādaṃ te kariṣye muktihetave ..
surāṣṭradeśe bhavitā siṃho raivatake girau .. 127 ..
17.6.d:
सिंहस्थस्य प्रसादं ते करिष्ये मुक्तिहेतवे ..
सुराष्ट्रदेशे भविता सिंहो रैवतके गिरौ .. 127 ..
17.6.m: When you have become a lion, I shall bestow grace upon you for the sake of your liberation. / In the country of Surāṣṭra, you will be a lion on the Raivataka mountain.

17.6.s:
vastrāpathe mahā kṣetre muktiste vihitā dhruvā ..
ityuktvā sa ṛṣirdeva gato bhīmeśvaraṃ prati ..
durvacaḥśravaṇādvyādhaḥ kramātpaṃcatvamāyayau .. 128 ..
17.6.d:
वस्त्रापथे महा क्षेत्रे मुक्तिस्ते विहिता ध्रुवा ..
इत्युक्त्वा स ऋषिर्देव गतो भीमेश्वरं प्रति ..
दुर्वचःश्रवणाद्व्याधः क्रमात्पंचत्वमाययौ .. 128 ..
17.6.m: In the great sacred field of Vastrāpatha, your liberation is surely ordained.' / Having spoken thus, O Lord, that seer went toward Bhīmeśvara. / Upon hearing those harsh words, the hunter gradually met his death.

17.6.s:
krauṃcī krauṃcaviyogena gatā sā ca vanāṃtare ..
mṛtā daivavaśājjātā mṛgī raivatake girau .. 129 ..
17.6.d:
क्रौंची क्रौंचवियोगेन गता सा च वनांतरे ..
मृता दैववशाज्जाता मृगी रैवतके गिरौ .. 129 ..
17.6.m: Separated from the krauñca bird, that female krauñcī went to another forest; / having died by the power of fate, she was born as a doe on Mount Raivataka.

17.6.s:
mṛgayūthagatā nityaṃ modate madavihvalā ..
vyādhaḥ siṃhaḥ samabhavadgirestasya mahāvane .. 7.2.6.130 ..
17.6.d:
मृगयूथगता नित्यं मोदते मदविह्वला ..
व्याधः सिंहः समभवद्गिरेस्तस्य महावने .. 7.2.6.130 ..
17.6.m: Always going among the herd of deer, she rejoiced, overcome with infatuation. / The hunter became a lion in the great forest of that mountain.

17.6.s:
kāmārtā bhramatā dṛṣṭā mṛgī siṃhena yatnataḥ ..
tatra saṃbhramate nityaṃ siṃhaścāpi mṛgī vane .. 131 ..
17.6.d:
कामार्ता भ्रमता दृष्टा मृगी सिंहेन यत्नतः ..
तत्र संभ्रमते नित्यं सिंहश्चापि मृगी वने .. 131 ..
17.6.m: As he roamed, the lion diligently spotted the doe, who was distressed by desire. / The lion and the doe constantly roved about there in the forest.

17.6.s:
siṃho'pi daivayogena mameyamiti manyate ..
paraṃ hiṃsrasvabhāvena tāmādātuṃ pracakrame .. 132 ..
17.6.d:
सिंहोऽपि दैवयोगेन ममेयमिति मन्यते ..
परं हिंस्रस्वभावेन तामादातुं प्रचक्रमे .. 132 ..
17.6.m: By the power of fate, the lion too thought, 'She is mine.' / Yet, driven by his predatory nature, he set about to seize her.

17.6.s:
calatvaṃ mṛgajātīnāṃ vihitaṃ vedhasā svayam ..
punargatā mṛgī yūthaṃ krīḍate cārulocanā .. 133 ..
17.6.d:
चलत्वं मृगजातीनां विहितं वेधसा स्वयम् ..
पुनर्गता मृगी यूथं क्रीडते चारुलोचना .. 133 ..
17.6.m: Fickleness has been ordained for deer by the Creator himself. / Again the lovely-eyed doe rejoined the herd and gamboled.

17.6.s:
bhavasya paścime bhāge tatra raivatake girau ..
anuyātaḥ śanaiḥ so'tha mṛgendro mṛgayūthapaḥ ..
utpapāta tataḥ siṃho saṃghasya mūrddhani .. 134 ..
17.6.d:
भवस्य पश्चिमे भागे तत्र रैवतके गिरौ ..
अनुयातः शनैः सोऽथ मृगेन्द्रो मृगयूथपः ..
उत्पपात ततः सिंहो संघस्य मूर्द्धनि .. 134 ..
17.6.m: In the western part of Bhava's [shrine], there on Mount Raivataka, / he, the king of beasts, the leader of the deer, then slowly followed. / Then the lion leaped upon the head of the herd.

17.6.s:
siṃhasya na mṛgaiḥ kāryaṃ hariṇīṃ prati paśyataḥ ..
yatra sā hariṇī yāti yayau siṃhastathaiva tām .. 135 ..
17.6.d:
सिंहस्य न मृगैः कार्यं हरिणीं प्रति पश्यतः ..
यत्र सा हरिणी याति ययौ सिंहस्तथैव ताम् .. 135 ..
17.6.m: The lion had no concern with the other deer, as he gazed toward the doe. / Wherever that doe went, the lion pursued her in just the same way.

17.6.s:
yadā vegaṃ mṛgī cakre siṃhaḥ kuddhastadā vane ..
siṃho'pi vegavāñjāto mṛgīvegādhiko'bhavat . 136 ..
17.6.d:
यदा वेगं मृगी चक्रे सिंहः कुद्धस्तदा वने ..
सिंहोऽपि वेगवाञ्जातो मृगीवेगाधिकोऽभवत् . 136 ..
17.6.m: When the doe made a dash, the lion grew furious in the forest; / the lion too gained speed, exceeding the speed of the doe.

17.6.s:
yadā siṃhena saṃkrāṃtā dadau jhampāṃ mṛgī tu sā ..
bhavasyāgre nadītoye patitā jalamūrddhani .. 137 ..
17.6.d:
यदा सिंहेन संक्रांता ददौ झम्पां मृगी तु सा ..
भवस्याग्रे नदीतोये पतिता जलमूर्द्धनि .. 137 ..
17.6.m: When attacked by the lion, that doe took a leap; / in front of Bhava's [shrine], she fell into the water of the river, upon the surface of the water.

17.6.s:
laṃbate tu śarīraṃ me veṇau protaṃ śiro mama ..
siṃhaḥ sahaiva patito mṛtaḥ payasi madhyataḥ .. 138 ..
17.6.d:
लंबते तु शरीरं मे वेणौ प्रोतं शिरो मम ..
सिंहः सहैव पतितो मृतः पयसि मध्यतः .. 138 ..
17.6.m: My body hung down, while my head was impaled on a bamboo; / the lion fell along with me and died in the middle of the water.

17.6.s:
svarṇareṣājale deva viśīrṇaṃ mama tadvapuḥ ..
na tu vaktraṃ nipatitaṃ tvaksāraśirasi sthitam .. 139 ..
17.6.d:
स्वर्णरेषाजले देव विशीर्णं मम तद्वपुः ..
न तु वक्त्रं निपतितं त्वक्सारशिरसि स्थितम् .. 139 ..
17.6.m: In the water of the Svarṇareṣā, O Lord, that body of mine decayed; / but the head did not fall down, remaining fixed upon the bamboo.

17.6.s:
etaccaritraṃ yatsarvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sārasvatena vai ..
tattīrthasya prabhāvena siṃhastvaṃ samajāyathāḥ .. 7.2.6.140 ..
17.6.d:
एतच्चरित्रं यत्सर्वं दृष्टं सारस्वतेन वै ..
तत्तीर्थस्य प्रभावेन सिंहस्त्वं समजायथाः .. 7.2.6.140 ..
17.6.m: This entire history was indeed seen by the sage belonging to Sarasvatī. / By the power of that sacred ford, you were born as a lion.

17.6.s:
idaṃ hi saptamaṃ janma sarvapāpakṣayodayam ..
kānyakubje mahādeśe rājā bhojetiviśrutaḥ .. 141 ..
17.6.d:
इदं हि सप्तमं जन्म सर्वपापक्षयोदयम् ..
कान्यकुब्जे महादेशे राजा भोजेतिविश्रुतः .. 141 ..
17.6.m: This indeed is the seventh birth, marking the rise of the destruction of all sins. / In the great country of Kānyakubja, you are the king well known as Bhoja.

17.6.s:
ahaṃ hi hariṇīgarbhe jātā mānuṣarūpiṇī ..
jātaṃ vaktraṃ mṛgīṇāṃ me yasmānna patitaṃ jale .. 142 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṃḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye bhavamāhātmye mṛgānanābhojavṛttāntavarṇane sārasvatamaharṣisaṃskṛtapuroḍāśaprāśanasamupa labdhaspaṣṭavākprasara mṛgānanākathitobhayaprāksaptajanmavṛttāntavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ .. 6 ..
17.6.d:
अहं हि हरिणीगर्भे जाता मानुषरूपिणी ..
जातं वक्त्रं मृगीणां मे यस्मान्न पतितं जले .. 142 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखंडे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये भवमाहात्म्ये मृगाननाभोजवृत्तान्तवर्णने सारस्वतमहर्षिसंस्कृतपुरोडाशप्राशनसमुप लब्धस्पष्टवाक्प्रसर मृगाननाकथितोभयप्राक्सप्तजन्मवृत्तान्तवर्णनंनाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः .. 6 ..
17.6.m:
I was born in the womb of a doe, having human form. / My face became that of a deer because it did not fall into the water.
Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Previous Seven Births of Both as Told by the Deer-Faced Woman, in Which the Flow of Clear Speech Was Obtained by Eating the Sacrificial Cake Consecrated by the Great Seer Sārasvata, in the Description of the Story of the Deer-Faced Woman and Bhoja, in the Māhātmya of Bhava, in the Māhātmya of the Vastrāpatha Sacred Field, in the Second Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the Seventh [Section] of the Eighty-One-Thousand-Verse Compendium, the Glorious Skanda Purāṇa.

17.7.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
kathaṃ tvaṃ hariṇīrūpe jātā mānuṣarūpiṇī ..
kena saṃvardhitā bālye kathaṃ te rūpamīdṛśam .. 1 ..
17.7.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
कथं त्वं हरिणीरूपे जाता मानुषरूपिणी ..
केन संवर्धिता बाल्ये कथं ते रूपमीदृशम् .. 1 ..
17.7.m: The king said: / How were you born in human form from the body of a doe? / By whom were you raised in childhood, and how did you come to have such a form?

17.7.s:
.. mṛgyuvāca .. ..
śṛṇu deva pravakṣyāmi yadvṛttaṃ kanyake vane ..
ṛṣiruddālakonāma gaṃgākūle mahātapāḥ .. 2 ..
17.7.d:
.. मृग्युवाच .. ..
शृणु देव प्रवक्ष्यामि यद्वृत्तं कन्यके वने ..
ऋषिरुद्दालकोनाम गंगाकूले महातपाः .. 2 ..
17.7.m: The doe-faced woman said: / Listen, O king, I will tell what took place in the Kanyaka forest. / There was a seer named Uddālaka on the bank of the Gaṅgā, of great austerity.

17.7.s:
prabhāte mūtramutsṛṣṭuṃ gato deva vanāṃtare ..
mūtrāṃte patito bhūmau vīryabiṃdurdvijanmanaḥ .. 3 ..
17.7.d:
प्रभाते मूत्रमुत्सृष्टुं गतो देव वनांतरे ..
मूत्रांते पतितो भूमौ वीर्यबिंदुर्द्विजन्मनः .. 3 ..
17.7.m: At dawn he went into the forest, O king, to pass urine. / At the end of urinating, a drop of the twice-born's semen fell upon the ground.

17.7.s:
yāvatsa calito vipraḥ śaucaṃ kṛtvā prayatnataḥ ..
tāvanmṛgī samāyātā dṛṣṭvā puṣpavanāṃtarāt .. 4 ..
17.7.d:
यावत्स चलितो विप्रः शौचं कृत्वा प्रयत्नतः ..
तावन्मृगी समायाता दृष्ट्वा पुष्पवनांतरात् .. 4 ..
17.7.m: As soon as that brahmin walked away, having carefully performed his purification, / a doe arrived, having seen it from within a grove of flowers.

17.7.s:
cāpalyādbhakṣitaṃ vīryaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ brahmarṣiṇā svayam ..
yasmādaśnāti me vīryaṃ tasmādgarbho bhaviṣyati .. 5 ..
17.7.d:
चापल्याद्भक्षितं वीर्यं दृष्टं ब्रह्मर्षिणा स्वयम् ..
यस्मादश्नाति मे वीर्यं तस्माद्गर्भो भविष्यति .. 5 ..
17.7.m: Out of fickleness she consumed the semen, and was seen by the brahmin seer himself. / [He thought:] 'Because she consumes my semen, therefore conception will occur.

17.7.s:
mamarūpā tavavaktrā nārī garbhe bhaviṣyati ..
varddhayiṣyati devyastāṃ rasairdivyaiḥ sutāṃ tava .. 6 ..
17.7.d:
ममरूपा तववक्त्रा नारी गर्भे भविष्यति ..
वर्द्धयिष्यति देव्यस्तां रसैर्दिव्यैः सुतां तव .. 6 ..
17.7.m: In her womb will be a woman with my form and your face. / The goddesses will nurture that daughter of yours with heavenly juices.

17.7.s:
kenāpi daivayogena jñānaṃ tasyā bhaviṣyati ..
evamuddālakādeva saṃjātāhaṃ mṛgānanā ..
praviśyāgnau mṛtā pūrvaṃ tvayā sārddhaṃ narādhipa .. 7 ..
17.7.d:
केनापि दैवयोगेन ज्ञानं तस्या भविष्यति ..
एवमुद्दालकादेव संजाताहं मृगानना ..
प्रविश्याग्नौ मृता पूर्वं त्वया सार्द्धं नराधिप .. 7 ..
17.7.m: By some divine fate, knowledge will come to her.' / Thus, O king, I was born deer-faced from Uddālaka. / Having entered the fire, I died of old with you, O lord of men.

17.7.s:
tasmājjātaṃ satītvaṃ me saptajanmani vai prabho ..
yattvayā kurvatā rājyaṃ pāpaṃ vai samupārjitam .. 8 ..
17.7.d:
तस्माज्जातं सतीत्वं मे सप्तजन्मनि वै प्रभो ..
यत्त्वया कुर्वता राज्यं पापं वै समुपार्जितम् .. 8 ..
17.7.m: From that arose my state of being a virtuous wife across seven births, O lord. / As for the sin that was accumulated by you while ruling the kingdom,

17.7.s:
kṣattradharmaṃ parityajya palāyanaparo mṛtaḥ ..
tadeno hi mayā dagdhaṃ citāgnau nṛpasattama .. 9 ..
17.7.d:
क्षत्त्रधर्मं परित्यज्य पलायनपरो मृतः ..
तदेनो हि मया दग्धं चिताग्नौ नृपसत्तम .. 9 ..
17.7.m: having abandoned the duty of a warrior and dying intent on flight, / that very sin was burned by me in the fire of the funeral pyre, O best of kings.

17.7.s:
patiṃ gṛhītvā yā nārī mṛtamagnau viśedyadi ..
sā tārayati bhartāramātmānaṃ ca kuladvayam .. 7.2.7.10 ..
17.7.d:
पतिं गृहीत्वा या नारी मृतमग्नौ विशेद्यदि ..
सा तारयति भर्तारमात्मानं च कुलद्वयम् .. 7.2.7.10 ..
17.7.m: If a woman, embracing her deceased husband, enters the fire, / she delivers her husband, herself, and both families.

17.7.s:
gograhe deśabhaṃge ca saṃgrāme sammukhe mṛtaḥ ..
sa sūryamaṇḍalaṃ bhittvā brahmaloke mahīyate ..11..
17.7.d:
गोग्रहे देशभंगे च संग्रामे सम्मुखे मृतः ..
स सूर्यमण्डलं भित्त्वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ..11..
17.7.m: One who dies in a cattle-raid, during the overthrow of a kingdom, or facing the enemy in battle / pierces the solar orb and is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

17.7.s:
anāśakaṃ yo vidadhāti marttyo dinedine yajñasahasrapuṇyam ..
sa yāti yānena gaṇānvitena vidhūya pāpāni suraiḥ sa pūjyate .. 12..
17.7.d:
अनाशकं यो विदधाति मर्त्त्यो दिनेदिने यज्ञसहस्रपुण्यम् ..
स याति यानेन गणान्वितेन विधूय पापानि सुरैः स पूज्यते .. 12..
17.7.m: The mortal who undertakes fasting to death gains the merit of a thousand sacrifices day by day; / casting off sins, he goes by a vehicle accompanied by attendants and is worshipped by the gods.

17.7.s:
gaṃgājale prayāge vā kedāre puṣkare ca ye ..
vastrāpathe prabhāse ca mṛtāste svargagāminaḥ .. 13 ..
17.7.d:
गंगाजले प्रयागे वा केदारे पुष्करे च ये ..
वस्त्रापथे प्रभासे च मृतास्ते स्वर्गगामिनः .. 13 ..
17.7.m: Those who die in the waters of the Gaṅgā, at Prayāga, at Kedāra, or at Puṣkara, / at Vastrāpatha, and at Prabhāsa—they go to heaven.

17.7.s:
dvārāvatyāṃ kurukṣetre yogābhyāsena ye mṛtāḥ ..
harirityakṣaraṃ mṛtyau yeṣāṃ te svargagāminaḥ .. 14 ..
17.7.d:
द्वारावत्यां कुरुक्षेत्रे योगाभ्यासेन ये मृताः ..
हरिरित्यक्षरं मृत्यौ येषां ते स्वर्गगामिनः .. 14 ..
17.7.m: Those who die in Dvāravatī or Kurukṣetra through the practice of yoga, / or those who have the syllable 'Hari' at death—they go to heaven.

17.7.s:
pūjayitvā hariṃ ye tu bhūmau darbhatilaiḥ saha ..
tilāṃśca pañcalohaṃ ca dattvā ye tu payasvinīm .. 15 ..
17.7.d:
पूजयित्वा हरिं ये तु भूमौ दर्भतिलैः सह ..
तिलांश्च पञ्चलोहं च दत्त्वा ये तु पयस्विनीम् .. 15 ..
17.7.m: Those who, having worshipped Hari on the ground with kuśa grass and sesame seeds, / and having given sesame seeds, five metals, and a milch cow,

17.7.s:
ye mṛtā rājaśārdūla te narāḥ svarga gāminaḥ ..
utpādya putrānsaṃsthāpya pitṛpaitāmahe pade .. 16 ..
17.7.d:
ये मृता राजशार्दूल ते नराः स्वर्ग गामिनः ..
उत्पाद्य पुत्रान्संस्थाप्य पितृपैतामहे पदे .. 16 ..
17.7.m: die, O tiger among kings—those men go to heaven. / Having fathered sons and established them in the ancestral station,

17.7.s:
nirmalā niṣkalaṃkā ye te mṛtāḥ svargagāminaḥ ..
vratopavāsaniratāḥ satyācāraparāyaṇāḥ ..
ahiṃsāniratāḥ śāṃtāste narāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 17 ..
17.7.d:
निर्मला निष्कलंका ये ते मृताः स्वर्गगामिनः ..
व्रतोपवासनिरताः सत्याचारपरायणाः ..
अहिंसानिरताः शांतास्ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः .. 17 ..
17.7.m: those who die pure and stainless go to heaven. / Those devoted to vows and fasts, dedicated to truthful conduct, / intent on non-violence, and peaceful—those men go to heaven.

17.7.s:
sāpavādo raṇaṃ tyaktvā mṛto yasmānnarādhipa ..
saptayoniṣu te janma tasmājjātaṃ mayā saha .. 18 ..
17.7.d:
सापवादो रणं त्यक्त्वा मृतो यस्मान्नराधिप ..
सप्तयोनिषु ते जन्म तस्माज्जातं मया सह .. 18 ..
17.7.m: Because you died under blame, having abandoned the battlefield, O lord of men, / your birth took place in seven wombs together with me.

17.7.s:
tvāṃ vinā me patirmā bhūnmaraṇe yācitaṃ mayā ..
tadāṃtarikṣe rājendra vāguvācāśarīriṇī ..
ādau pāpaphalaṃ bhuktvā paścā tsvargaṃ gamiṣyasi .. 19..
17.7.d:
त्वां विना मे पतिर्मा भून्मरणे याचितं मया ..
तदांतरिक्षे राजेन्द्र वागुवाचाशरीरिणी ..
आदौ पापफलं भुक्त्वा पश्चा त्स्वर्गं गमिष्यसि .. 19..
17.7.m: At my death I prayed: 'May I have no husband other than you.' / Then, O best of kings, a bodiless voice in the sky said: / 'Having first experienced the fruit of your sins, you will afterwards go to heaven.

17.7.s:
yadi vastrāpathe gatvā śiraḥ kaścidvimuṃcati ..
svarṇarekhājale rājanmānuṣaṃ syānmukhaṃ mama .. 7.2.7.20 ..
17.7.d:
यदि वस्त्रापथे गत्वा शिरः कश्चिद्विमुंचति ..
स्वर्णरेखाजले राजन्मानुषं स्यान्मुखं मम .. 7.2.7.20 ..
17.7.m: If someone goes to Vastrāpatha and releases your head / into the water of the Svarṇarekhā, O king, my face will become human.

17.7.s:
ahaṃ mānuṣavaktrā'smi pāpacchāyā''vṛtaṃ mukham ..
dṛśyate mṛgavaktrābhaṃ tasmācchīghraṃ vimuṃcaya .. 21 ..
17.7.d:
अहं मानुषवक्त्राऽस्मि पापच्छाया'ऽवृतं मुखम् ..
दृश्यते मृगवक्त्राभं तस्माच्छीघ्रं विमुंचय .. 21 ..
17.7.m: I am a woman with a human face, but my face is veiled by the shadow of sin / and appears like a deer's face; therefore, have it released quickly.'

17.7.s:
iti śrutvā vaco rājā sārasvatamudaikṣata ..
jano vihasya sānandaṃ sarvaṃ satyaṃ mṛgīvacaḥ .. 22 ..
17.7.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचो राजा सारस्वतमुदैक्षत ..
जनो विहस्य सानन्दं सर्वं सत्यं मृगीवचः .. 22 ..
17.7.m: Hearing these words, the king looked at the sage belonging to Sarasvatī. / Smiling with joy, that brahmin said, 'All the doe's words are true.

17.7.s:
ityuktvā''ha dvijendraḥ sa evaṃ kuru nṛpottama ..
evaṃ rājñā samādiṣṭaḥ pratīhāro yayau vanam .. 23 ..
17.7.d:
इत्युक्त्वा'ऽह द्विजेन्द्रः स एवं कुरु नृपोत्तम ..
एवं राज्ञा समादिष्टः प्रतीहारो ययौ वनम् .. 23 ..
17.7.m: Do thus, O best of kings!' / Thus commanded by the king, the gatekeeper went to the forest.

17.7.s:
vastrāpathe mahātīrthe bhavaṃ draṣṭuṃ tvarānvitaḥ ..
tvaksārajālirmahatī svarṇarekhājalopari .. 24 ..
17.7.d:
वस्त्रापथे महातीर्थे भवं द्रष्टुं त्वरान्वितः ..
त्वक्सारजालिर्महती स्वर्णरेखाजलोपरि .. 24 ..
17.7.m: Hastening to see Bhava at the great sacred ford of Vastrāpatha, / [he went to] the great thicket of bamboo over the water of the Svarṇarekhā,

17.7.s:
varttate tacchiro yatra vaṃśaprotaṃ mahāvane ..
sārasvatasya śiṣyeṇa kuśalena niveditam.. 25 ..
17.7.d:
वर्त्तते तच्छिरो यत्र वंशप्रोतं महावने ..
सारस्वतस्य शिष्येण कुशलेन निवेदितम्.. 25 ..
17.7.m: where that head was impaled on a bamboo in the great forest, / as reported by the skilled disciple of the sage belonging to Sarasvatī.

17.7.s:
tīrthaṃ vastrāpathaṃ gatvā bhavasyāgre mahānadī ..
jāle tatra śiro dṛṣṭaṃ tacca toye vimocitam .. 26 ..
17.7.d:
तीर्थं वस्त्रापथं गत्वा भवस्याग्रे महानदी ..
जाले तत्र शिरो दृष्टं तच्च तोये विमोचितम् .. 26 ..
17.7.m: Having gone to the Vastrāpatha sacred ford, there was the great river in front of Bhava; / there in the thicket the head was seen, and it was released into the water.

17.7.s:
snātvā saṃpūjya tīrtheśaṃ pratīhāraḥ samabhyagāt ..
śiṣyeṇa sahito vegādrathenādityavarcasā .. 27 ..
17.7.d:
स्नात्वा संपूज्य तीर्थेशं प्रतीहारः समभ्यगात् ..
शिष्येण सहितो वेगाद्रथेनादित्यवर्चसा .. 27 ..
17.7.m: Having bathed and worshipped the lord of the sacred ford, the gatekeeper returned / swiftly with the disciple in a chariot possessing the radiance of the sun.

17.7.s:
yadāgataḥ pratīhārastadā sārasvatena sā ..
vṛtā cāndrāyaṇenaiva māsamekaṃ nirantaram .. 28 ..
17.7.d:
यदागतः प्रतीहारस्तदा सारस्वतेन सा ..
वृता चान्द्रायणेनैव मासमेकं निरन्तरम् .. 28 ..
17.7.m: When the gatekeeper arrived, she was instructed by the sage belonging to Sarasvatī / to observe the cāndrāyaṇa vow continuously for one month.

17.7.s:
saṃpūrṇe tu vrate tasyā divyaṃ vaktraṃ sulocanam ..
suśobhanaṃ dīrghakeśaṃ dīrghakarṇaṃ śubhadvijam .. 29 ..
17.7.d:
संपूर्णे तु व्रते तस्या दिव्यं वक्त्रं सुलोचनम् ..
सुशोभनं दीर्घकेशं दीर्घकर्णं शुभद्विजम् .. 29 ..
17.7.m: When her vow was completed, she obtained a celestial face with beautiful eyes, / very lovely, with long hair, long ears, and auspicious teeth,

17.7.s:
kambugrīvaṃ padmagaṃdhaṃ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam..
vratāṃte mūrcchitā bālā gatajñānā vabhūva sā .. 7.2.7.30 ..
17.7.d:
कम्बुग्रीवं पद्मगंधं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम्..
व्रतांते मूर्च्छिता बाला गतज्ञाना वभूव सा .. 7.2.7.30 ..
17.7.m: with a conch-like neck, smelling of lotuses, and endowed with all auspicious marks. / At the end of the vow, the maiden fainted and lost consciousness.

17.7.s:
na devī na ca gaṃdharvī nāsurī na ca kiṃnarī ..
yādṛśī sā tadā jātā tīrthabhāvena sundarī .. 31 ..
17.7.d:
न देवी न च गंधर्वी नासुरी न च किंनरी ..
यादृशी सा तदा जाता तीर्थभावेन सुन्दरी .. 31 ..
17.7.m: Neither goddess, nor gandharva maiden, nor asura maiden, nor kinnara maiden / was such as she became then, beautiful by the nature of the sacred ford.

17.7.s:
pariṇītā tu sā tena bhojarājena sundarī ..
mṛgīmukhīti vikhyātā devī sā bhuvaneśvarī .. 32 ..
17.7.d:
परिणीता तु सा तेन भोजराजेन सुन्दरी ..
मृगीमुखीति विख्याता देवी सा भुवनेश्वरी .. 32 ..
17.7.m: She was married by that king Bhoja, that lovely woman; / renowned as Mṛgīmukhī, she was like the goddess Bhuvaneśvarī.

17.7.s:
na jānāti punaḥ kiṃcidyadvṛttaṃ rājamandire ..
kṛtā sā paṭṭamahiṣī bhojarājena dhīmatā .. 33 ..
17.7.d:
न जानाति पुनः किंचिद्यद्वृत्तं राजमन्दिरे ..
कृता सा पट्टमहिषी भोजराजेन धीमता .. 33 ..
17.7.m: She remembered nothing of what had happened before in the royal palace. / She was made the chief queen by the wise king Bhoja.

17.7.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
deśānāṃ pravaro deśo girīṇāṃ pravaro giriḥ ..
kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ kṣetraṃ vanānāmuttamaṃ vanam .. 34 ..
17.7.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
देशानां प्रवरो देशो गिरीणां प्रवरो गिरिः ..
क्षेत्राणामुत्तमं क्षेत्रं वनानामुत्तमं वनम् .. 34 ..
17.7.m: Īśvara said: / This is the foremost country among countries, the foremost mountain among mountains, / the best sacred field among sacred fields, the best forest among forests.

17.7.s:
gaṃgā sarasvatī tāpī svarṇarekhājale sthitā ..
brahmā viṣṇuśca sūryaśca sarva indrādayaḥ surāḥ .. 35 ..
17.7.d:
गंगा सरस्वती तापी स्वर्णरेखाजले स्थिता ..
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च सूर्यश्च सर्व इन्द्रादयः सुराः .. 35 ..
17.7.m: Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, and Tāpī abide in the water of the Svarṇarekhā; / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and all the gods headed by Indra,

17.7.s:
nāgā yakṣāśca gandharvā asminkṣetre vyavasthitāḥ ..
brahmāṃḍaṃ nirmitaṃ yena trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 36 ..
17.7.d:
नागा यक्षाश्च गन्धर्वा अस्मिन्क्षेत्रे व्यवस्थिताः ..
ब्रह्मांडं निर्मितं येन त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् .. 36 ..
17.7.m: nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas are established in this sacred field, / by which the cosmic egg, the three worlds with the moving and unmoving, was fashioned.

17.7.s:
devā brahmādayo jātāḥ sa bhavo'tra vyavasthitaḥ ..
śivo bhaveti vikhyātaḥ svayaṃ devastrilocanaḥ .. 37 ..
17.7.d:
देवा ब्रह्मादयो जाताः स भवोऽत्र व्यवस्थितः ..
शिवो भवेति विख्यातः स्वयं देवस्त्रिलोचनः .. 37 ..
17.7.m: [and] the gods headed by Brahmā were born—he, Bhava, is situated here. / He is celebrated as Śiva, Bhava, the three-eyed God himself.

17.7.s:
veveti skandaracanādbhavānī cātra saṃsthitā ..
ato yannādhikaṃ proktaṃ tīrthaṃ devi mayā tava .. 38 ..
17.7.d:
वेवेति स्कन्दरचनाद्भवानी चात्र संस्थिता ..
अतो यन्नाधिकं प्रोक्तं तीर्थं देवि मया तव .. 38 ..
17.7.m: And on account of Skanda's babbling words Bhavānī is also established here. / Therefore no sacred ford greater than this has been spoken of by me to you, O goddess.

17.7.s:
tasmiñjale snānaparo naro yadi saṃdhyāṃ vidhāyānu karoti tarpaṇam ..
śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca dadāti dakṣiṇāṃ bhavodbhavaṃ paśyati mucyate bhavāt .. 39 ..
17.7.d:
तस्मिञ्जले स्नानपरो नरो यदि संध्यां विधायानु करोति तर्पणम् ..
श्राद्धं पितॄणां च ददाति दक्षिणां भवोद्भवं पश्यति मुच्यते भवात् .. 39 ..
17.7.m: If a man intent on ritual ablution in that water, having performed the twilight prayers, then performs the water oblation, / offers the śrāddha to the ancestors, gives sacrificial fees, and looks upon Bhava’s origin, he is liberated from worldly existence.

17.7.s:
atha yadi bhavapūjāṃ divyapuṣpaiḥ karoti tadanu śivaśiveti stotrapāṭhaṃ ca gītam ..
suravara gaṇavṛndaiḥ stūyamāno vimānaiḥ suravaraśivarūpo mānavo yāti nākam .. 7.2.7.40 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye svarṇarekhāyāṃ mṛgānanāyāḥ pūrvajanmamṛgamukhaprakṣepaṇena divyamukhatvaprāptyuttaraṃ bhojanṛpatipariṇaya vṛttāntapūrvakaṃ svarṇarekhāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma saptamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 7 ..
17.7.d:
अथ यदि भवपूजां दिव्यपुष्पैः करोति तदनु शिवशिवेति स्तोत्रपाठं च गीतम् ..
सुरवर गणवृन्दैः स्तूयमानो विमानैः सुरवरशिवरूपो मानवो याति नाकम् .. 7.2.7.40 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये स्वर्णरेखायां मृगाननायाः पूर्वजन्ममृगमुखप्रक्षेपणेन दिव्यमुखत्वप्राप्त्युत्तरं भोजनृपतिपरिणय वृत्तान्तपूर्वकं स्वर्णरेखामाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः .. 7 ..
17.7.m:
Now, if he performs the worship of Bhava with celestial flowers, and then sings and recites hymns saying 'Śiva, Śiva,' / praised by hosts of the best of gods in aerial chariots, taking the form of the best of gods, Śiva, the mortal goes to heaven.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Svarṇarekhā, preceded by the account of the marriage of King Bhoja after the deer-faced woman obtained a divine face by casting away her deer-face from a past birth in the Svarṇarekhā,' in the Glory of the Vastrāpatha Field, in the second [sub-section], in the Prabhāsa Section, in the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

17.8.s:
.. bhojarāja uvāca .. ..
prabho sārasvata mayā śrutaṃ māhātmyamuttamam ..
vastrāpathasya kṣetrasya gire raivatakasya ca .. 1 ..
17.8.d:
.. भोजराज उवाच .. ..
प्रभो सारस्वत मया श्रुतं माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ..
वस्त्रापथस्य क्षेत्रस्य गिरे रैवतकस्य च .. 1 ..
17.8.m: King Bhoja said: / O lord Sārasvata, I have heard the supreme glory / of the sacred field Vastrāpatha and of Mount Raivataka,

17.8.s:
viśeṣeṇa svarṇarekhābhavasya ca jalasya ca ..
idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi tīrthotpattiṃ vadasva me.. 2 ..
17.8.d:
विशेषेण स्वर्णरेखाभवस्य च जलस्य च ..
इदानीं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तीर्थोत्पत्तिं वदस्व मे.. 2 ..
17.8.m: and especially of the water arising from the Svarṇarekhā. / Now I wish to hear the origin of the sacred ford; tell me:

17.8.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ madhye ko'yaṃ vyavasthitaḥ ..
keyaṃ nadī svarṇarekhā sarvapātakanāśinī .. 3 ..
17.8.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादीनां मध्ये कोऽयं व्यवस्थितः ..
केयं नदी स्वर्णरेखा सर्वपातकनाशिनी .. 3 ..
17.8.m: Among Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others, who is situated here? / What is this river Svarṇarekhā, the destroyer of all sins?

17.8.s:
kasmādbrahmādayā devā asmiṃstīrthe samāgatāḥ ..
kathaṃ nārāyaṇo devaḥ svayameva samāgataḥ .. 4 ..
17.8.d:
कस्माद्ब्रह्मादया देवा अस्मिंस्तीर्थे समागताः ..
कथं नारायणो देवः स्वयमेव समागतः .. 4 ..
17.8.m: Why did the gods headed by Brahmā come to this sacred ford? / How did Lord Nārāyaṇa himself come?

17.8.s:
hemālayaṃ parityajya bhavānī girimūrddhani ..
saṃsthitā skandamādāya devairindrādibhiḥ saha .. 5 ..
17.8.d:
हेमालयं परित्यज्य भवानी गिरिमूर्द्धनि ..
संस्थिता स्कन्दमादाय देवैरिन्द्रादिभिः सह .. 5 ..
17.8.m: Why did Bhavānī, abandoning Himālaya, remain on the mountain summit, / taking Skanda, together with the gods headed by Indra?

17.8.s:
.. sārasvata uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu sarvaṃ mahārāja kathayiṣye savistaram ..
yena vai kathyamānena sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet .. 6 ..
17.8.d:
.. सारस्वत उवाच .. ..
शृणु सर्वं महाराज कथयिष्ये सविस्तरम् ..
येन वै कथ्यमानेन सर्वपापक्षयो भवेत् .. 6 ..
17.8.m: Sārasvata said: / Hear everything, O great king, I will tell it in detail, / by the recitation of which the destruction of all sins occurs.

17.8.s:
purā brahmadinasyāṃte jagadetaccarācaram ..
saṃhṛtya bhagavānrudro brahmaviṣṇupuraskṛtaḥ .. 7 ..
17.8.d:
पुरा ब्रह्मदिनस्यांते जगदेतच्चराचरम् ..
संहृत्य भगवान्रुद्रो ब्रह्मविष्णुपुरस्कृतः .. 7 ..
17.8.m: Formerly, at the end of Brahmā’s day, having dissolved this world, moving and unmoving, / the blessed Lord Rudra, preceded by Brahmā and Viṣṇu—

17.8.s:
tāṃ ca te sakalāṃ rātrimekamūrttibhavāstrayaḥ ..
tiṣṭhanti rātri paryante punarbhinnā bhavaṃti te .. 8 ..
17.8.d:
तां च ते सकलां रात्रिमेकमूर्त्तिभवास्त्रयः ..
तिष्ठन्ति रात्रि पर्यन्ते पुनर्भिन्ना भवंति ते .. 8 ..
17.8.m: those three, having become a single form, remained for that whole night; / at the end of the night they became distinct once more.

17.8.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivā devā rajaḥsattvatamomayāḥ ..
sṛṣṭiṃ karoti bhagavānbrahmā pālayate hariḥ .. 9 ..
17.8.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवा देवा रजःसत्त्वतमोमयाः ..
सृष्टिं करोति भगवान्ब्रह्मा पालयते हरिः .. 9 ..
17.8.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva are the gods composed of rajas, sattva, and tamas. / The blessed Lord Brahmā performs creation; Hari preserves;

17.8.s:
sarvaṃ saṃharate rudro jagatkālapramāṇataḥ ..
tenādau bhagavānsṛṣṭo dakṣo nāma prajāpatiḥ .. 7.2.8.10 ..
17.8.d:
सर्वं संहरते रुद्रो जगत्कालप्रमाणतः ..
तेनादौ भगवान्सृष्टो दक्षो नाम प्रजापतिः .. 7.2.8.10 ..
17.8.m: Rudra dissolves the entire world according to the measure of time. / First, by him the Prajāpati named Dakṣa was created.

17.8.s:
sarve saṃkṣepataḥ kṛtvā brahmāṇḍaṃ sacarā caram ..
bhinnā devāstrayo jātāḥ satyalokavyavasthitāḥ .. 11 ..
17.8.d:
सर्वे संक्षेपतः कृत्वा ब्रह्माण्डं सचरा चरम् ..
भिन्ना देवास्त्रयो जाताः सत्यलोकव्यवस्थिताः .. 11 ..
17.8.m: Having made all the universe, moving and unmoving, in brief, / the three gods became separate and were situated in Satyaloka.

17.8.s:
trayo bhuvaṃ samāsādya kautukāviṣṭacetasaḥ ..
kailāsaṃ te girivaraṃ samārūḍhāḥ surervṛtāḥ .. 12 ..
17.8.d:
त्रयो भुवं समासाद्य कौतुकाविष्टचेतसः ..
कैलासं ते गिरिवरं समारूढाः सुरेर्वृताः .. 12 ..
17.8.m: The three, having approached the earth with their minds filled with curiosity, / ascended Kailāsa, the excellent mountain, surrounded by the gods.

17.8.s:
ahaṃ jyeṣṭho ahaṃ jyeṣṭho vādo'bhūdbrahmarudrayoḥ ..
tadā kruddho mahādevo brahmāṇaṃ hantumudyataḥ .. 13 ..
17.8.d:
अहं ज्येष्ठो अहं ज्येष्ठो वादोऽभूद्ब्रह्मरुद्रयोः ..
तदा क्रुद्धो महादेवो ब्रह्माणं हन्तुमुद्यतः .. 13 ..
17.8.m: 'I am the eldest!' 'I am the eldest!'—a dispute arose between Brahmā and Rudra. / Then Mahādeva, enraged, set about to slay Brahmā.

17.8.s:
viṣṇunā vārito brahmā na te vādastu yujyate ..
tattvaṃ nāhaṃ yadā nedaṃ brahmāṃḍaṃ sacarācaram .. 14 ..
17.8.d:
विष्णुना वारितो ब्रह्मा न ते वादस्तु युज्यते ..
तत्त्वं नाहं यदा नेदं ब्रह्मांडं सचराचरम् .. 14 ..
17.8.m: Brahmā was restrained by Viṣṇu: 'A dispute is not proper for you. / When neither you, nor I, nor this universe, moving and unmoving, [existed],

17.8.s:
eka eva tadā devo jale śete maheśvaraḥ ..
jāgarti ca yadā devaḥ svecchayā kautukāttataḥ .. 15 ..
17.8.d:
एक एव तदा देवो जले शेते महेश्वरः ..
जागर्ति च यदा देवः स्वेच्छया कौतुकात्ततः .. 15 ..
17.8.m: at that time only one god, Maheśvara, slept upon the water. / And when the god awakes according to his own will, then out of sport,

17.8.s:
anena tvaṃ kṛtaḥ pūrvamahaṃ paścāttvayā kṛtaḥ ..
brahmāṃḍaṃ kūrmarūpeṇa dhṛtamasya prasādataḥ .. 16 ..
17.8.d:
अनेन त्वं कृतः पूर्वमहं पश्चात्त्वया कृतः ..
ब्रह्मांडं कूर्मरूपेण धृतमस्य प्रसादतः .. 16 ..
17.8.m: you were created by him first, and I was created later by you. / By his grace the universe was supported in the form of a tortoise.

17.8.s:
anupraviṣṭā brahmāṃḍaṃ prasādācchaṃ karasya ca ..
sṛṣṭistvayā kṛtā sarvā mayi rakṣā vyavasthitā .. 17 ..
17.8.d:
अनुप्रविष्टा ब्रह्मांडं प्रसादाच्छं करस्य च ..
सृष्टिस्त्वया कृता सर्वा मयि रक्षा व्यवस्थिता .. 17 ..
17.8.m: And through the grace of Śaṃkara, [we] entered into the universe. / All creation was made by you, and protection is established in me.

17.8.s:
udāsīnavadāsīnaḥ saṃsārātsāramīkṣate ..
eka eva śivo devaḥ sarvavyāpī maheśvaraḥ .. 18 ..
17.8.d:
उदासीनवदासीनः संसारात्सारमीक्षते ..
एक एव शिवो देवः सर्वव्यापी महेश्वरः .. 18 ..
17.8.m: Sitting like one indifferent, he perceives the essence from worldly existence. / The god Śiva, the all-pervading Maheśvara, is one alone.

17.8.s:
pitāmahatvaṃ saṃjātaṃ prasādācchaṃkarasya te ..
prasādayāmāsa haraṃ śrutvā brahmā vaco hareḥ .. 19 ..
17.8.d:
पितामहत्वं संजातं प्रसादाच्छंकरस्य ते ..
प्रसादयामास हरं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा वचो हरेः .. 19 ..
17.8.m: Your status as the Grandfather arose by the grace of Śaṃkara.' / Having heard the word of Hari, Brahmā propitiated Hara,

17.8.s:
anādinidhano devo bahuśīrṣo mahābhujaḥ ..
ityādivedavacanaistatastuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ ..
prāha brahmanvaraṃ yatte vṛṇīṣva manasi sthitam .. 7.2.8.20 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe dvitīye vastrāpathakṣetramāhātmye brahmarudravivāde viṣṇuvacanena brahmakṛtarudraprasādanavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ ..8..
17.8.d:
अनादिनिधनो देवो बहुशीर्षो महाभुजः ..
इत्यादिवेदवचनैस्ततस्तुष्टो महेश्वरः ..
प्राह ब्रह्मन्वरं यत्ते वृणीष्व मनसि स्थितम् .. 7.2.8.20 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे द्वितीये वस्त्रापथक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये ब्रह्मरुद्रविवादे विष्णुवचनेन ब्रह्मकृतरुद्रप्रसादनवर्णनंनामाष्टमोऽध्यायः ..8..
17.8.m:
[saying]: 'The God without beginning or end, many-headed, mighty-armed'— / with these and other Vedic words. Then Maheśvara, pleased, / said: 'O Brahmā, choose a boon that resides in your mind.'
Thus ends the eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Propitiation of Rudra performed by Brahmā at the Word of Viṣṇu during the Dispute between Brahmā and Rudra,' in the Glory of the Vastrāpatha Field, in the second [sub-section], in the Prabhāsa Section, in the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

17.9.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
yadi sṛṣṭaṃ mayā sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram ..
tadā mūrtimimāṃ tyaktvā bhavaḥ sṛṣṭo mayā'dhunā .. 1 ..
17.9.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
यदि सृष्टं मया सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ..
तदा मूर्तिमिमां त्यक्त्वा भवः सृष्टो मयाऽधुना .. 1 ..
17.9.m: Brahmā said: / 'If the three worlds, moving and unmoving, were all created by me, / then, having abandoned this form, let Bhava now be created by me,

17.9.s:
pitāmahamahattvaṃ syāttathā śīghraṃ vidhīyatām ..
brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā viṣṇunā sa pramoditaḥ .. 2 ..
17.9.d:
पितामहमहत्त्वं स्यात्तथा शीघ्रं विधीयताम् ..
ब्रह्मणो वचनं श्रुत्वा विष्णुना स प्रमोदितः .. 2 ..
17.9.m: so that the greatness of the Grandfather may be [confirmed]; let it be done quickly.' / Hearing Brahmā’s speech, [Rudra] was delighted by Viṣṇu.

17.9.s:
mahadāścaryajanake saṃprāpto girimūrddhani ..
na vicārastvayākāryaḥ karttavyaṃ brahmabhāṣitam .. 3 ..
17.9.d:
महदाश्चर्यजनके संप्राप्तो गिरिमूर्द्धनि ..
न विचारस्त्वयाकार्यः कर्त्तव्यं ब्रह्मभाषितम् .. 3 ..
17.9.m: He arrived at the mountain summit that produced great wonder. / 'No doubt should be entertained by you; that which was spoken by Brahmā should be done.'

17.9.s:
tathetyuktvā śivo devastatraivāṃtaradhīyata ..
brahmā yayau meruśṛṃgaṃ manasaḥ śirasi sthitam .. 4 ..
17.9.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा शिवो देवस्तत्रैवांतरधीयत ..
ब्रह्मा ययौ मेरुशृंगं मनसः शिरसि स्थितम् .. 4 ..
17.9.m: Saying 'So be it,' the god Śiva vanished right there. / Brahmā went to the peak of Meru situated at the head of the mind.

17.9.s:
tapastepe prajānātho vedoccāraṇatatparaḥ ..
atharvavedoccaraṇaṃ yāvaccakre pitāmahaḥ .. 5 ..
17.9.d:
तपस्तेपे प्रजानाथो वेदोच्चारणतत्परः ..
अथर्ववेदोच्चरणं यावच्चक्रे पितामहः .. 5 ..
17.9.m: The lord of creatures performed austerity, devoted to the chanting of the Veda. / As the Grandfather was performing the chanting of the Atharvaveda,

17.9.s:
mukhādrudraḥ samabhavadraudrarūpo bhavāpahaḥ..
arddhanārīnaravapurduṣprekṣyo'tibhayaṃkaraḥ..6..
17.9.d:
मुखाद्रुद्रः समभवद्रौद्ररूपो भवापहः..
अर्द्धनारीनरवपुर्दुष्प्रेक्ष्योऽतिभयंकरः..6..
17.9.m: Rudra arose from his mouth, of fierce form, the remover of worldly existence, / with a body half-woman and half-man, hard to look upon, extremely terrifying.

17.9.s:
vibhajātmānamityuktvā brahmā cāṃtardadhe bhayāt ..
tathoktosau dvidhā strītvaṃ puruṣatvaṃ tathā'karot .. 7 ..
17.9.d:
विभजात्मानमित्युक्त्वा ब्रह्मा चांतर्दधे भयात् ..
तथोक्तोसौ द्विधा स्त्रीत्वं पुरुषत्वं तथाऽकरोत् .. 7 ..
17.9.m: Saying 'Divide yourself!', Brahmā vanished in fear. / Being addressed thus, he divided himself twofold into femaleness and maleness.

17.9.s:
bibheda puruṣatvaṃ ca daśadhā caikadhā punaḥ ..
ekādaśaite kathitā rudrāstribhuvaneśvarāḥ .. 8 ..
17.9.d:
बिभेद पुरुषत्वं च दशधा चैकधा पुनः ..
एकादशैते कथिता रुद्रास्त्रिभुवनेश्वराः .. 8 ..
17.9.m: And he divided the maleness tenfold, and then once more. / These eleven Rudras, the lords of the three worlds, are declared.

17.9.s:
kṛtvā nāmāni sarveṣāṃ devakārye niyojitāḥ ..
vibhajya punarīśānī svātmānaṃ śaṃkarādvibhoḥ .. 9 ..
17.9.d:
कृत्वा नामानि सर्वेषां देवकार्ये नियोजिताः ..
विभज्य पुनरीशानी स्वात्मानं शंकराद्विभोः .. 9 ..
17.9.m: Having assigned names to all of them, they were appointed to the task of the gods. / Then, dividing herself from the all-pervading Śaṃkara, Īśānī,

17.9.s:
mahādevaniyogena pitāmahamupasthitā ..
tāmāha bhagavānbrahmā dakṣasya duhitā bhava .. 7.2.9.10 ..
17.9.d:
महादेवनियोगेन पितामहमुपस्थिता ..
तामाह भगवान्ब्रह्मा दक्षस्य दुहिता भव .. 7.2.9.10 ..
17.9.m: at the command of Mahādeva, approached the Grandfather. / Blessed Lord Brahmā said to her: 'Become the daughter of Dakṣa.'

17.9.s:
sāpi tasya niyogena prādurāsītprajāpateḥ ..
niyogādbrahmaṇo dakṣo dadau rudrāya tāṃ satīm ..11..
17.9.d:
सापि तस्य नियोगेन प्रादुरासीत्प्रजापतेः ..
नियोगाद्ब्रह्मणो दक्षो ददौ रुद्राय तां सतीम् ..11..
17.9.m: She too, by his direction, became manifest to the Prajāpati. / By the direction of Brahmā, Dakṣa gave that Satī to Rudra.

17.9.s:
dākṣīṃ rudro'pi jagrāha svakīyāmeva śūlabhṛt ..
atha brahmā babhāṣe taṃ sṛṣṭiṃ kuru satīpate ..12.. ..
17.9.d:
दाक्षीं रुद्रोऽपि जग्राह स्वकीयामेव शूलभृत् ..
अथ ब्रह्मा बभाषे तं सृष्टिं कुरु सतीपते ..12.. ..
17.9.m: Rudra, the trident-bearer, also received the daughter of Dakṣa, who was indeed his own. / Then Brahmā said to him: 'Perform creation, O lord of Satī.'

17.9.s:
.. rudra uvāca .. ..
sṛṣṭirmayā na karttavyā karttavyā bhavatā svayam ..
pālanaṃ viṣṇunā kāryaṃ saṃhartā'haṃ vyavasthitaḥ ..13..
17.9.d:
.. रुद्र उवाच .. ..
सृष्टिर्मया न कर्त्तव्या कर्त्तव्या भवता स्वयम् ..
पालनं विष्णुना कार्यं संहर्ताऽहं व्यवस्थितः ..13..
17.9.m: Rudra said: / 'Creation should not be performed by me; it should be performed by you yourself. / Preservation is to be done by Viṣṇu; I am appointed as the destroyer.'

17.9.s: sthāṇuvatsaṃsthito yasmā ttasmātsthāṇurbhavāmyaham ..14..
17.9.d: स्थाणुवत्संस्थितो यस्मा त्तस्मात्स्थाणुर्भवाम्यहम् ..14..
17.9.m: Because I stand firmly like a pillar, therefore I become Sthāṇu.

17.9.s:
rajorūpāḥ sattvarūpāstamorūpāśca ye narāḥ ..
sarve te bhavatā kāryā guṇatrayavibhāgataḥ..15..
17.9.d:
रजोरूपाः सत्त्वरूपास्तमोरूपाश्च ये नराः ..
सर्वे ते भवता कार्या गुणत्रयविभागतः..15..
17.9.m: Those men who are of the nature of passion, goodness, and darkness— / all of them are to be made by you according to the division of the three qualities.

17.9.s:
yadā te tāmasaiḥ kāryaṃ tadā raudro bhava svayam ..
yadā te rājasaiḥ kāryaṃ tadā tvaṃ rājaso bhava..
sāttvikaiste yadā kāryaṃ tadā tvaṃ sāttviko bhava ..16..
17.9.d:
यदा ते तामसैः कार्यं तदा रौद्रो भव स्वयम् ..
यदा ते राजसैः कार्यं तदा त्वं राजसो भव..
सात्त्विकैस्ते यदा कार्यं तदा त्वं सात्त्विको भव ..16..
17.9.m: When your work is through those of darkness, then be yourself fierce; / when your work is through those of passion, then be passionate; / when your work is through those of goodness, then be full of goodness.

17.9.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
ityājñāpya ca brahmāṇaṃ svayaṃ sṛṣṭyādikarmasu ..
gṛhītvā tāṃ satīṃ rudraḥ kailāsamadhitiṣṭhati .. 17 ..
17.9.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
इत्याज्ञाप्य च ब्रह्माणं स्वयं सृष्ट्यादिकर्मसु ..
गृहीत्वा तां सतीं रुद्रः कैलासमधितिष्ठति .. 17 ..
17.9.m: Īśvara said: / Having thus instructed Brahmā himself in the tasks of creation and the rest, / Rudra took Satī and dwelt on Kailāsa.

17.9.s: dakṣaḥ kālena mahatā harasyālayamāyayau .. 18..
17.9.d: दक्षः कालेन महता हरस्यालयमाययौ .. 18..
17.9.m: After a long time, Dakṣa came to Hara's abode.

17.9.s:
atha rudraḥ samutthāya kṛtavāngauravaṃ bahu ..
tato yathocitāṃ pūjāṃ na dakṣo bahu manyate ..19..
17.9.d:
अथ रुद्रः समुत्थाय कृतवान्गौरवं बहु ..
ततो यथोचितां पूजां न दक्षो बहु मन्यते ..19..
17.9.m: Then Rudra arose and showed great respect; / yet Dakṣa did not value the worship, though properly offered.

17.9.s:
tadā vai tamasāviṣṭaḥ so'dhikaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śubhaḥ..
pūjāmanarghyāmanvicchañjagāma kupito gṛham .. 7.2.9.20 ..
17.9.d:
तदा वै तमसाविष्टः सोऽधिकं ब्राह्मणः शुभः..
पूजामनर्घ्यामन्विच्छञ्जगाम कुपितो गृहम् .. 7.2.9.20 ..
17.9.m: Then indeed, overcome with darkness, that noble brahmin, / seeking peerless worship, returned home in anger.

17.9.s:
kadācittāṃ gṛhaṃ prāptāṃ satīṃ dakṣaḥ sudurmanāḥ ..
bhartrā saha viniṃdyaināṃ bhartsayāmāsa vai ruṣā ..21..
17.9.d:
कदाचित्तां गृहं प्राप्तां सतीं दक्षः सुदुर्मनाः ..
भर्त्रा सह विनिंद्यैनां भर्त्सयामास वै रुषा ..21..
17.9.m: Once, when Satī had arrived at his house, Dakṣa, deeply distressed in mind, / reviled her along with her husband and rebuked her in fury:

17.9.s:
paṃca -vaktro daśabhujo mukhe netratrayānvitaḥ..
kaparddī khaṃḍacaṃdrosau tathāsau nīlalohitaḥ..22..
17.9.d:
पंच -वक्त्रो दशभुजो मुखे नेत्रत्रयान्वितः..
कपर्द्दी खंडचंद्रोसौ तथासौ नीललोहितः..22..
17.9.m: "He has five faces, ten arms, and three eyes in his face; / he has matted hair, carries the crescent moon, and is blue and red;

17.9.s:
kapālī śūlahasto'sau gajacarmāvaguṃṭhitaḥ ..
nāsya mātā na ca pitā na bhrātā na ca bāndhavaḥ ..23..
17.9.d:
कपाली शूलहस्तोऽसौ गजचर्मावगुंठितः ..
नास्य माता न च पिता न भ्राता न च बान्धवः ..23..
17.9.m: he carries a skull, holds a trident in his hand, and is wrapped in an elephant hide; / he has no mother, no father, no brother, and no kin;

17.9.s:
sarpāsthimaṃḍitagrīvastyaktvā hemavibhūṣaṇam ..
bhikṣayā bhojanaṃ yasya kathamannaṃ pradāsyati .. 24 ..
17.9.d:
सर्पास्थिमंडितग्रीवस्त्यक्त्वा हेमविभूषणम् ..
भिक्षया भोजनं यस्य कथमन्नं प्रदास्यति .. 24 ..
17.9.m: his neck is adorned with serpents and bones, having cast aside gold ornaments; / his food comes from begging—how will he provide food [for you]?

17.9.s:
kadācitpūrvato yāti gacchanyāti sa paścime ..
dakṣiṇasyāṃ vṛṣo yāti svayaṃ yāti sa cottare .. 25 ..
17.9.d:
कदाचित्पूर्वतो याति गच्छन्याति स पश्चिमे ..
दक्षिणस्यां वृषो याति स्वयं याति स चोत्तरे .. 25 ..
17.9.m: Sometimes he goes to the east, and while going, he goes to the west; / his bull goes to the south, while he himself goes to the north;

17.9.s:
tiryagūrdhvamadho yāti naiva yāti na tiṣṭhati ..
iti citraṃ caritraṃ te bhartturnānyasya dṛśyate .. 26 ..
17.9.d:
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधो याति नैव याति न तिष्ठति ..
इति चित्रं चरित्रं ते भर्त्तुर्नान्यस्य दृश्यते .. 26 ..
17.9.m: he moves sideways, upwards, and downwards; he neither goes nor stays still. / Such strange conduct of your husband is not seen in any other!

17.9.s:
nirguṇaḥ sa guṇātīto niḥsneho mūkavatsthitaḥ ..
sarvajñaḥ sarvagaḥ sarvaḥ paṭhyate bhuvanatraye .. 27 ..
17.9.d:
निर्गुणः स गुणातीतो निःस्नेहो मूकवत्स्थितः ..
सर्वज्ञः सर्वगः सर्वः पठ्यते भुवनत्रये .. 27 ..
17.9.m: He is without qualities, beyond qualities, devoid of affection, standing like a mute; / yet he is recited throughout the three worlds as omniscient, all-pervading, and all-being.

17.9.s:
kadācinnaiva jānāti na śṛṇoti na paśyati ..
daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ dadāti yaḥ ..28..
17.9.d:
कदाचिन्नैव जानाति न शृणोति न पश्यति ..
दैत्यानां दानवानां च राक्षसानां ददाति यः ..28..
17.9.m: Sometimes he does not know at all, does not hear, and does not see; / yet he gives [boons] to daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas;

17.9.s:
na cāsya ca pitā kaścinna ca bhrātāsti kaścana ..
eka eva vṛṣārūḍho nagno bhramati bhūtale ..29..
17.9.d:
न चास्य च पिता कश्चिन्न च भ्रातास्ति कश्चन ..
एक एव वृषारूढो नग्नो भ्रमति भूतले ..29..
17.9.m: he has no father at all, nor any brother; / all alone, mounted on a bull, naked he roams the earth;

17.9.s:
na gṛhaṃ na dhanaṃ gotramanādinidhanovyayaḥ ..
sthirabuddhirna caivāsau krīḍate bhuvanatraye ..7.2.9.30..
17.9.d:
न गृहं न धनं गोत्रमनादिनिधनोव्ययः ..
स्थिरबुद्धिर्न चैवासौ क्रीडते भुवनत्रये ..7.2.9.30..
17.9.m: he has no house, no wealth, no lineage; he is without beginning or end, imperishable; / he has no steady intellect, yet he sports across the three worlds.

17.9.s:
kadācitsatyaloke sau pātālamadhitiṣṭhati ..
girisānuṣu śete'sāvaśivopi śivaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 31 ..
17.9.d:
कदाचित्सत्यलोके सौ पातालमधितिष्ठति ..
गिरिसानुषु शेतेऽसावशिवोपि शिवः स्मृतः .. 31 ..
17.9.m: Sometimes he is in Satyaloka, and sometimes he dwells in Pātāla; / he sleeps upon mountain ridges; though inauspicious, he is called Śiva.

17.9.s:
śrīkhaṃḍādīni saṃtyajya sadā bhasmāvaguṃṭhitaḥ..
sarvadeti vacaḥ satyaṃ kimanyatsa pradāsyati.. 32 ..
17.9.d:
श्रीखंडादीनि संत्यज्य सदा भस्मावगुंठितः..
सर्वदेति वचः सत्यं किमन्यत्स प्रदास्यति.. 32 ..
17.9.m: Discarding sandalwood and other perfumes, he is constantly smeared with ashes; / 'He gives everything' is the saying—yet what else will he give?

17.9.s:
dhiktvāṃ jāmātaraṃ dhiktaṃ yayoḥ snehaḥ parasparam ..
tasya tvaṃ vallabhā bhāryā sa ca prāṇādhikastava .. 33 ..
17.9.d:
धिक्त्वां जामातरं धिक्तं ययोः स्नेहः परस्परम् ..
तस्य त्वं वल्लभा भार्या स च प्राणाधिकस्तव .. 33 ..
17.9.m: Fie on you! Fie on that son-in-law! between whom there is mutual affection: / you are his beloved wife, and he is dearer to you than life.

17.9.s:
na ca pitrāsti te kāryaṃ na mātrā na sakhīṣu ca ..
kevalaṃ bhartṛbhaktā tvaṃ tasmādgaccha gṛhānmama ..34..
17.9.d:
न च पित्रास्ति ते कार्यं न मात्रा न सखीषु च ..
केवलं भर्तृभक्ता त्वं तस्माद्गच्छ गृहान्मम ..34..
17.9.m: You have no concern with your father, nor with your mother, nor among your female friends; / you are devoted only to your husband; therefore depart from my house!

17.9.s:
anye jāmātaraḥ sarve bhartustava pinākinaḥ ..
tvamadyaivāśu cāsmākaṃ gṛhādgaccha varaṃ prati .. 35 ..
17.9.d:
अन्ये जामातरः सर्वे भर्तुस्तव पिनाकिनः ..
त्वमद्यैवाशु चास्माकं गृहाद्गच्छ वरं प्रति .. 35 ..
17.9.m: All the other sons-in-law [are superior] to your bow-wielding husband; / go this very day, at once, from our house to your husband!"

17.9.s:
tasya tadvākyamākarṇya sā devī śaṃkarapriyā ..
viniṃdya pitaraṃ dakṣaṃ dhyātvā devaṃ maheśvaram .. 36 ..
17.9.d:
तस्य तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य सा देवी शंकरप्रिया ..
विनिंद्य पितरं दक्षं ध्यात्वा देवं महेश्वरम् .. 36 ..
17.9.m: Hearing those words of his, that goddess, beloved of Śaṃkara, / reviled her father Dakṣa, meditated on the god Maheśvara,

17.9.s:
śvetavastrā jale snātvā dadāhātmānamātmanā ..
yācitastu śivo bharttā punarjanmāṃtare tayā ..37..
17.9.d:
श्वेतवस्त्रा जले स्नात्वा ददाहात्मानमात्मना ..
याचितस्तु शिवो भर्त्ता पुनर्जन्मांतरे तया ..37..
17.9.m: clothed in white garments, bathed in water, and burned herself by her own power. / But Śiva was solicited by her as her husband in another birth:

17.9.s:
pitā me himavānastu menāgarbhe bhavāmyaham ..
atrāṃtare(?) himavatā tapasā toṣito haraḥ ..
pratyakṣaṃ darśanaṃ dattvā himavaṃtaṃ vaco'bravīt .. 38 ..
17.9.d:
पिता मे हिमवानस्तु मेनागर्भे भवाम्यहम् ..
अत्रांतरे(?) हिमवता तपसा तोषितो हरः ..
प्रत्यक्षं दर्शनं दत्त्वा हिमवंतं वचोऽब्रवीत् .. 38 ..
17.9.m: "May Himavān be my father; may I be born from the womb of Menā!" / Meanwhile, Hara was pleased by the austerity of Himavat; / granting him his direct darśana, he spoke these words to Himavat:

17.9.s:
eṣā dattā sutā tubhyaṃ pariṇeṣyāmi tāmaham ..
devānāṃ kāryyasiddhyarthaṃ girirājo bhaviṣyasi .. 39 ..
17.9.d:
एषा दत्ता सुता तुभ्यं परिणेष्यामि तामहम् ..
देवानां कार्य्यसिद्ध्यर्थं गिरिराजो भविष्यसि .. 39 ..
17.9.m: "This daughter is given to you; I shall marry her. / For the accomplishment of the purpose of the gods, you shall be the king of mountains."

17.9.s:
ātmamūrttau praviṣṭāṃ tāṃ jñātvā devo maheśvaraḥ ..
śaśāpa dakṣaṃ kupitaḥ samāgatyātha tadgṛham .. 7.2.9.40 ..
17.9.d:
आत्ममूर्त्तौ प्रविष्टां तां ज्ञात्वा देवो महेश्वरः ..
शशाप दक्षं कुपितः समागत्याथ तद्गृहम् .. 7.2.9.40 ..
17.9.m: Knowing that she had entered his own form, the god Maheśvara, / enraged, came to Dakṣa's house and cursed Dakṣa:

17.9.s:
tyaktvā dehamimaṃ brāhmyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ kule bhava ..
svāyaṃbhuvatvaṃ saṃtyajya dakṣa prācetaso bhava .. 41 ..
17.9.d:
त्यक्त्वा देहमिमं ब्राह्म्यं क्षत्रियाणां कुले भव ..
स्वायंभुवत्वं संत्यज्य दक्ष प्राचेतसो भव .. 41 ..
17.9.m: "Leaving this brahminical body, be born in the lineage of kṣatriyas! / Abandoning the state of being born from Svayambhū, O Dakṣa, become the son of Pracetas!

17.9.s:
svasyāṃ sutāyāmūḍhāyāṃ putramutpādayiṣyasi ..
evaṃ śaptvā mahādevo yayau kailāsaparvatam .. 42 ..
17.9.d:
स्वस्यां सुतायामूढायां पुत्रमुत्पादयिष्यसि ..
एवं शप्त्वा महादेवो ययौ कैलासपर्वतम् .. 42 ..
17.9.m: You shall generate a son upon your own married daughter!" / Having thus cursed him, Mahādeva went to Mount Kailāsa.

17.9.s:
svāyabhuvo'pi kālena dakṣaḥ prācetaso'bhavat ..
bhavānīṃ sa sutāṃ labdhvā giristuṣṭo himā layaḥ .. 43 ..
17.9.d:
स्वायभुवोऽपि कालेन दक्षः प्राचेतसोऽभवत् ..
भवानीं स सुतां लब्ध्वा गिरिस्तुष्टो हिमा लयः .. 43 ..
17.9.m: Even the son of Svayambhū in time became the son of Pracetas. / Having obtained Bhavānī as his daughter, the mountain Himālaya was delighted.

17.9.s:
menāpi tāṃ sutāṃ labdhvā dhanyaṃ mene gṛhāśramam ..
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā jāyamānāṃ ca svecchayaiva varānanām .. 44 ..
17.9.d:
मेनापि तां सुतां लब्ध्वा धन्यं मेने गृहाश्रमम् ..
तां दृष्ट्वा जायमानां च स्वेच्छयैव वराननाम् .. 44 ..
17.9.m: Menā also, having obtained that daughter, considered her household blessed. / Seeing that fair-faced girl being born by her own mere will,

17.9.s:
menā himavataḥ patnī prāhedaṃ parvateśvaram..
paśya bālāmimāṃ rājanrājīvasadṛśānanām.. 45 ..
17.9.d:
मेना हिमवतः पत्नी प्राहेदं पर्वतेश्वरम्..
पश्य बालामिमां राजन्राजीवसदृशाननाम्.. 45 ..
17.9.m: Menā, wife of Himavat, spoke thus to the lord of mountains: / "Look, O king, at this girl whose face is like a blue lotus,

17.9.s:
hitāya sarvabhūtānāṃ jātāṃ ca tapasā śubhām ..
so'pi dṛṣṭvā mahādevīṃ taruṇādityasannibhām .. 46 ..
17.9.d:
हिताय सर्वभूतानां जातां च तपसा शुभाम् ..
सोऽपि दृष्ट्वा महादेवीं तरुणादित्यसन्निभाम् .. 46 ..
17.9.m: born through austerity for the welfare of all beings, auspicious!" / He too, seeing the great goddess resembling the morning sun,

17.9.s:
kapardinīṃ caturvaktrāṃ trinetrāmatilālasām..
aṣṭahastāṃ viśālākṣīṃ caṃdrāvayavabhūṣaṇām .. 47 ..
17.9.d:
कपर्दिनीं चतुर्वक्त्रां त्रिनेत्रामतिलालसाम्..
अष्टहस्तां विशालाक्षीं चंद्रावयवभूषणाम् .. 47 ..
17.9.m: having matted hair, four faces, three eyes, full of intense desire, / eight-armed, large-eyed, adorned with the crescent moon,

17.9.s:
praṇamya śirasā bhūmau tejasā tu suvihvalaḥ ..
bhītaḥ kṛtāṃjaliḥ stabdhaḥ provāca parameśvarīm .. 48 ..
17.9.d:
प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ तेजसा तु सुविह्वलः ..
भीतः कृतांजलिः स्तब्धः प्रोवाच परमेश्वरीम् .. 48 ..
17.9.m: bowed with his head to the ground, deeply agitated by her radiance; / frightened, with folded hands, rendered motionless, he spoke to the supreme goddess.

17.9.s:
.. himavānuvāca .. ..
kā tvaṃ devi viśālākṣi śaṃsa me saṃśayo mahān .. 49 ..
17.9.d:
.. हिमवानुवाच .. ..
का त्वं देवि विशालाक्षि शंस मे संशयो महान् .. 49 ..
17.9.m: Himavān said: / Who are you, O large-eyed goddess? Tell me, I have a great doubt.

17.9.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
māṃ viddhi paramāṃ śaktiṃ maheśvarasamāśrayām ..
ananyāmavyayāmekāṃ yāṃ paśyaṃti mumukṣavaḥ .. 7.2.9.50 ..
17.9.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
मां विद्धि परमां शक्तिं महेश्वरसमाश्रयाम् ..
अनन्यामव्ययामेकां यां पश्यंति मुमुक्षवः .. 7.2.9.50 ..
17.9.m: The goddess said: / Know me to be the supreme power resting upon Maheśvara, / non-different, imperishable, one, whom seekers of liberation behold.

17.9.s:
divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me rūpamaiśvaram ..
etāvaduktvā vijñānaṃ dattvā himavate svayam .. 51 ..
17.9.d:
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे रूपमैश्वरम् ..
एतावदुक्त्वा विज्ञानं दत्त्वा हिमवते स्वयम् .. 51 ..
17.9.m: I give you a divine eye; behold my lordly form! / Having said this much, giving spiritual knowledge herself to Himavat,

17.9.s:
sūryakoṭipratīkāśaṃ tejobiṃbaṃ nirākulam ..
jvālā mālāsahasrāḍhyaṃ kālānalaśatopamam .. 52 ..
17.9.d:
सूर्यकोटिप्रतीकाशं तेजोबिंबं निराकुलम् ..
ज्वाला मालासहस्राढ्यं कालानलशतोपमम् .. 52 ..
17.9.m: [she revealed her form] like an orb of light resembling ten million suns, undisturbed, / filled with thousands of garlands of flames, equal to a hundred cosmic dissolution fires,

17.9.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālamuddharṣaṃ jaṭāmaṃḍalamaṃḍitam ..
praśāṃtaṃ saumyavadanamanaṃtāścaryasaṃyutam .. 53 ..
17.9.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालमुद्धर्षं जटामंडलमंडितम् ..
प्रशांतं सौम्यवदनमनंताश्चर्यसंयुतम् .. 53 ..
17.9.m: dreadful with fangs, fierce, adorned with a mass of matted hair, / [yet] tranquil, with a gentle face, endowed with infinite wonders,

17.9.s:
caṃdrāvayavalakṣmāṇaṃ caṃdrakoṭisamaprabham ..
kirīṭinaṃ gadāhastaṃ nupurairupaśobhitam .. 54..
17.9.d:
चंद्रावयवलक्ष्माणं चंद्रकोटिसमप्रभम् ..
किरीटिनं गदाहस्तं नुपुरैरुपशोभितम् .. 54..
17.9.m: bearing the crescent moon as a mark, with splendor equal to ten million moons, / crowned with a diadem, holding a mace, adorned with anklets,

17.9.s:
divyamālyāṃbaradharaṃ divyagaṃdhānulepanam ..
śaṃkhacakradharaṃ kāmyaṃ trinetraṃ kṛttivāsasam .. 55 ..
17.9.d:
दिव्यमाल्यांबरधरं दिव्यगंधानुलेपनम् ..
शंखचक्रधरं काम्यं त्रिनेत्रं कृत्तिवाससम् .. 55 ..
17.9.m: wearing celestial garlands and garments, anointed with celestial fragrant pastes, / holding a conch and a discus, lovely, three-eyed, clad in an animal hide,

17.9.s:
aṃḍasthaṃ cāṃḍabāhyasthaṃ bāhyamabhyaṃtaraṃ param ..
sarvaśaktimayaṃ śubhraṃ sarvālaṃkārasaṃyutam ..56..
17.9.d:
अंडस्थं चांडबाह्यस्थं बाह्यमभ्यंतरं परम् ..
सर्वशक्तिमयं शुभ्रं सर्वालंकारसंयुतम् ..56..
17.9.m: dwelling within the cosmic egg and beyond it, external, internal, supreme, / composed of all powers, bright, endowed with all ornaments,

17.9.s:
brahmendropendrayogīndrairvandyamāna padāṃbujam ..
sarvataḥ pāṇipādāṃtaṃ sarvato'kṣiśiromukham.. 57 ..
17.9.d:
ब्रह्मेन्द्रोपेन्द्रयोगीन्द्रैर्वन्द्यमान पदांबुजम् ..
सर्वतः पाणिपादांतं सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्.. 57 ..
17.9.m: whose lotus feet are praised by Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, and the lords of yogins, / with hands and feet on all sides, with eyes, heads, and faces on all sides.

17.9.s:
sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ dadarśa parameśvaram ..
dṛṣṭvā nandīśvaraṃ devaṃ devyā maheśvaraṃ param .. .. 58 ..
17.9.d:
सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठंतं ददर्श परमेश्वरम् ..
दृष्ट्वा नन्दीश्वरं देवं देव्या महेश्वरं परम् .. .. 58 ..
17.9.m: Pervading all and standing firm, he saw the supreme lord. / Having seen Nandīśvara, the god, and the supreme great lord along with the goddess, 58

17.9.s:
bhayena ca samāviṣṭaḥ sa rājā hṛṣṭamānasaḥ ..
ātmanyādhāya cātmānamoṃkāraṃ samanusmaran .. 59 ..
17.9.d:
भयेन च समाविष्टः स राजा हृष्टमानसः ..
आत्मन्याधाय चात्मानमोंकारं समनुस्मरन् .. 59 ..
17.9.m: and seized with fear, that king, joyful in mind, / fixing the self within the self and contemplating the oṃkāra, 59

17.9.s: nāmnāmaṣṭasahasreṇa stutvā'sau hima vāngiriḥ .. 7.2.9.60 ..
17.9.d: नाम्नामष्टसहस्रेण स्तुत्वाऽसौ हिम वान्गिरिः .. 7.2.9.60 ..
17.9.m: having praised him with a thousand and eight names, that Himavat mountain, 60

17.9.s:
bhūyaḥ praṇamya bhūtātmā provācedaṃ kṛtāṃjaliḥ ..
yadetadaiśvaraṃ rūpaṃ jātaṃ te parameśvari .. 61 ..
17.9.d:
भूयः प्रणम्य भूतात्मा प्रोवाचेदं कृतांजलिः ..
यदेतदैश्वरं रूपं जातं ते परमेश्वरि .. 61 ..
17.9.m: bowing again, the self of beings, with joined palms said this: / 'This lordly form of yours that has arisen, O supreme lady, 61

17.9.s:
bhīto'smi sāṃprataṃ dṛṣṭvā tattvamanyatpradarśaya ..
evamuktā ca sā devī tena śailena pārvatī .. 62 ..
17.9.d:
भीतोऽस्मि सांप्रतं दृष्ट्वा तत्त्वमन्यत्प्रदर्शय ..
एवमुक्ता च सा देवी तेन शैलेन पार्वती .. 62 ..
17.9.m: I am terrified now having seen it; show another real form.' / Thus addressed by that mountain, the goddess Pārvatī 62

17.9.s:
saṃhṛtya darśayāmāsa svarūpamaparaṃ param ..
nīlotpaladalaprakhyaṃ nīlotpalasugaṃdhikam .. ..63..
17.9.d:
संहृत्य दर्शयामास स्वरूपमपरं परम् ..
नीलोत्पलदलप्रख्यं नीलोत्पलसुगंधिकम् .. ..63..
17.9.m: withdrew [that form] and showed another supreme natural form, / resembling the petal of a blue lotus, fragrant like a blue lotus, 63

17.9.s:
dvinetraṃ dvibhujaṃ saumyaṃ nīlālakavibhūṣitam ..
raktapādāṃbujatalaṃ suraktakarapallavam ..64..
17.9.d:
द्विनेत्रं द्विभुजं सौम्यं नीलालकविभूषितम् ..
रक्तपादांबुजतलं सुरक्तकरपल्लवम् ..64..
17.9.m: two-eyed, two-armed, gentle, adorned with dark locks, / the soles of her lotus-feet red, her tender hands deep red, 64

17.9.s:
śrīmadviśālasadvṛttaṃ lalāṭatilakojjvalam ..
bhūṣitaṃ cārusarvāṃgaṃ bhūṣaṇairatikomalam ..65..
17.9.d:
श्रीमद्विशालसद्वृत्तं ललाटतिलकोज्ज्वलम् ..
भूषितं चारुसर्वांगं भूषणैरतिकोमलम् ..65..
17.9.m: splendid, broad, well-rounded, radiant with a tilaka on her forehead, / her lovely limbs all adorned with ornaments, exceedingly delicate, 65

17.9.s:
dadhānaṃ corasā mālāṃ viśālāṃ hemanirmitām ..
īṣatsmitaṃ subiṃboṣṭhaṃ nūpurārāvaśobhitam .. 66 ..
17.9.d:
दधानं चोरसा मालां विशालां हेमनिर्मिताम् ..
ईषत्स्मितं सुबिंबोष्ठं नूपुरारावशोभितम् .. 66 ..
17.9.m: bearing on her chest a broad garland fashioned of gold, / smiling gently, with fine bimba-like lips, adorned with the tinkling of anklets, 66

17.9.s:
prasannavadanaṃ divyaṃ cārubhrūmahimāspadam ..
tadīdṛśaṃ samālokya svarūpaṃ śailasattamaḥ ..
bhayaṃ saṃtyajya hṛṣṭātmā babhāṣe parameśvarīm .. 67 ..
17.9.d:
प्रसन्नवदनं दिव्यं चारुभ्रूमहिमास्पदम् ..
तदीदृशं समालोक्य स्वरूपं शैलसत्तमः ..
भयं संत्यज्य हृष्टात्मा बभाषे परमेश्वरीम् .. 67 ..
17.9.m: her face serene, divine, the seat of the glory of lovely brows. / Beholding such a natural form, that best of mountains, / casting off fear, delighted in self, spoke to the supreme lady: 67

17.9.s:
.. himavānuvāca .. ..
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalāḥ kriyāḥ ..
yanme sākṣāttvamavyaktā prasannā dṛṣṭigocarā ..
idānīṃ kiṃ mayā kāryaṃ tanme brūhi maheśvari ..68.. ..
17.9.d:
.. हिमवानुवाच .. ..
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलाः क्रियाः ..
यन्मे साक्षात्त्वमव्यक्ता प्रसन्ना दृष्टिगोचरा ..
इदानीं किं मया कार्यं तन्मे ब्रूहि महेश्वरि ..68.. ..
17.9.m: Himavat said: / 'Today my birth has borne fruit; today my rites are fruitful, / since you, unmanifest, in person, propitious, have come into my sight. / Now what must be done by me? Tell me that, O great lady.' 68

17.9.s:
.. maheśvaryuvāca .. ..
śivapūjā tvayā kāryā dhyānena tapasā sadā ..
ahaṃ tasmai pradātavyā kenacitkāraṇena vai .. 69 ..
17.9.d:
.. महेश्वर्युवाच .. ..
शिवपूजा त्वया कार्या ध्यानेन तपसा सदा ..
अहं तस्मै प्रदातव्या केनचित्कारणेन वै .. 69 ..
17.9.m: The great lady said: / 'Worship of Śiva must be performed by you always with meditation and austerity. / I must indeed be given to him for a certain purpose. 69

17.9.s:
yādṛśastu tvayā dṛṣṭo dhyeyo vai tādṛśastvayā ..
eka eva śivo devaḥ sarvādhāro dharādharaḥ ..7.2.9.70..
17.9.d:
यादृशस्तु त्वया दृष्टो ध्येयो वै तादृशस्त्वया ..
एक एव शिवो देवः सर्वाधारो धराधरः ..7.2.9.70..
17.9.m: Just as he has been seen by you, so indeed should he be meditated upon by you. / God Śiva is the one alone, the foundation of all, the bearer of the earth.' 70

17.9.s:
.. sārasvata uvāca .. ..
tapaśca kṛtavānrudraḥ samāgamya himācalam ..
tasyomā paramāṃ bhaktiṃ cakāra śivasaṃnidhau ..71..
17.9.d:
.. सारस्वत उवाच .. ..
तपश्च कृतवान्रुद्रः समागम्य हिमाचलम् ..
तस्योमा परमां भक्तिं चकार शिवसंनिधौ ..71..
17.9.m: Sārasvata said: / And Rudra, having arrived at the Himācala, performed austerity. / In the presence of Śiva, Umā offered supreme devotion to him. 71

17.9.s:
devakāryeṇa kenāpi devo vai jñāpitaḥ prabhuḥ ..
upayeme haro devīmumāṃ tribhuvaneśvarīm .. 72 ..
17.9.d:
देवकार्येण केनापि देवो वै ज्ञापितः प्रभुः ..
उपयेमे हरो देवीमुमां त्रिभुवनेश्वरीम् .. 72 ..
17.9.m: For some purpose of the gods, the lord god was informed; / Hara wedded the goddess Umā, the ruler of the three worlds. 72

17.9.s:
sa śaptaḥ śaṃbhunā pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ prācetaso nṛpaḥ ..
viniṃdya pūrvavaireṇa gaṃgādvāre'yajaddharim ..73..
17.9.d:
स शप्तः शंभुना पूर्वं दक्षः प्राचेतसो नृपः ..
विनिंद्य पूर्ववैरेण गंगाद्वारेऽयजद्धरिम् ..73..
17.9.m: He, the king Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, was formerly cursed by Śambhu. / Reviling [him] out of former enmity, he performed a sacrifice to Hari at Gaṅgādvāra. 73

17.9.s:
devāśca yajñabhāgārthamāhūtā viṣṇunā svayam ..
sahaiva munibhiḥ sarvairāgatā munipuṃgavāḥ .. 74 ..
17.9.d:
देवाश्च यज्ञभागार्थमाहूता विष्णुना स्वयम् ..
सहैव मुनिभिः सर्वैरागता मुनिपुंगवाः .. 74 ..
17.9.m: The gods were invited by Viṣṇu himself for their share in the sacrifice; / along with all the sages, the foremost among sages arrived. 74

17.9.s:
dṛṣṭvā devakulaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śaṃkareṇa vinā''gatam ..
dadhīco nāma viprarṣiḥ prācetasamathābravīt .. 75 ..
17.9.d:
दृष्ट्वा देवकुलं कृत्स्नं शंकरेण विना'ऽगतम् ..
दधीचो नाम विप्रर्षिः प्राचेतसमथाब्रवीत् .. 75 ..
17.9.m: Seeing the whole host of gods arrived without Śaṃkara, / the brahmin-seer named Dadhīca then addressed the son of Pracetas. 75

17.9.s:
.. dadhīciruvāca .. ..
brahmādyāstu piśācāṃtā yasyājñānuvidhāyinaḥ ..
sa hi vaḥ sāṃprataṃ rudro vidhinā kiṃ na pūjyate .. 76 ..
17.9.d:
.. दधीचिरुवाच .. ..
ब्रह्माद्यास्तु पिशाचांता यस्याज्ञानुविधायिनः ..
स हि वः सांप्रतं रुद्रो विधिना किं न पूज्यते .. 76 ..
17.9.m: Dadhīci said: / 'He whose commands are obeyed by those beginning with Brahmā down to piśācas— / why is that Rudra not worshipped properly by you all now?' 76

17.9.s:
.. dakṣa uvāca .. ..
sarveṣveva hi yajñeṣu na bhāgaḥ parikalpitaḥ ..
na maṃtrā bhāryayā sārddhaṃ śaṃkarasyeti neṣyate .. 77 ..
17.9.d:
.. दक्ष उवाच .. ..
सर्वेष्वेव हि यज्ञेषु न भागः परिकल्पितः ..
न मंत्रा भार्यया सार्द्धं शंकरस्येति नेष्यते .. 77 ..
17.9.m: Dakṣa said: / 'In all sacrifices indeed no portion has been assigned [to him], / nor are mantras [chanted] with his wife; therefore Śaṃkara is not desired.' 77

17.9.s:
vihasya dakṣaṃ kupito vacaḥ prāha mahāmuniḥ ..
śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ sarvajñānamayaḥ svayam ..78..
17.9.d:
